tasks.name: executeActionMovement

uses.description: Runs only the movement and displacement half of an action on the contextual actor, without casting the action or applying any of its other effects. Depending on which movement behaviour the named action defines, the actor is pulled toward, onto, beside, or past the first targeted tile, walks a path to it, or swaps places with whatever is standing on a targeted tile. The move uses the action's own movement speed setting and normally lets the actor pass through obstacles on the way. Nothing happens if the contextual actor does not exist.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The ID of the action whose movement behaviour is applied. The action must exist, and it only does something if it defines one of the caster-movement or swap behaviours.

optional.name: tileCoords[0+]
optional.description: The tiles the action is aimed at; the first one is the movement destination and the rest only matter for swap behaviours that need more than one target tile. Defaults to a single off-map tile, which makes most movement behaviours push the actor off toward the top-left corner of the map. Only one tile coordinate can be supplied as a trigger effect, so multi-tile targeting requires writing the task as a taskString.

tasks.officialDescription: Must be used as a taskString. Executes actor-movement and actor-swap effects for the action strings[0] using tileCoords[] as the targeted tiles.

tasks.name: action

uses.description: Makes a named actor perform an action as its own next act, aimed at a chosen tile. The action is queued rather than fired on the spot: it goes off on that actor's next update, once it is no longer busy and no other action is still resolving, and it then runs as a full cast with the caster's animation, charge time and any follow-up actions the action chains into. Use this when the effect needs a real caster whose stats, equipment and facing matter.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The ID of the action to perform. Supplying an empty value silently queues nothing.

required.name: strings[1]
required.description: The ID of the actor that performs the action. It must name an actor currently present in the zone; if it is empty or names no one, the task falls back to firing the action at a tile instead.

optional.name: tileCoords[0]
optional.description: The tile the action is aimed at. If omitted it defaults to the off-map tile (-1,-1), which aims the action outside the world and usually makes it do nothing visible.

uses.description: Fires an action at a tile with no caster behind it, so the effect happens at the spot itself rather than being performed by anyone. Everything the action does to terrain, items and actors in its area still applies, along with its visuals and element reactions, but no one spends a turn and no caster animation plays. If another action is still resolving, this one waits in line until that delay elapses.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The ID of the action to fire at the tile.

required.name: strings[1]
required.description: Must be present but must not name an actor currently in the zone; leave it empty. Supplying a real actor ID instead makes that actor perform the action rather than firing it at a tile.

optional.name: tileCoords[0]
optional.description: The tile the action originates from and is aimed at. If omitted it defaults to the off-map tile (-1,-1), which instead fires the action on the contextual actor's own tile; that fallback needs a contextual actor to exist, and without one the action fires off-map.

uses.description: Makes the contextual actor cast an action centred on its own tile, right away and as a full cast with visuals. This is the form to use for self-buffs, self-damage, or any effect the actor should apply to its own square. The cast still respects the action's charge or cast time and is skipped if the actor is currently unable to act, and it is postponed if another action is still resolving. The contextual actor must exist.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The ID of the action the contextual actor casts on itself. Providing any second string switches the task to one of its other forms, so this must be the only string supplied.

tasks.officialDescription: Executes 'sValue' action at X,Y (or triggering actor if unspecified). Uses 'sValue2' as caster if specified.

tasks.name: actionOnPartyNumActor

uses.description: Fires an action on the tile occupied by one of the player's party members, picked by its slot number in the party. The action has no caster behind it, so its effects, visuals and element reactions land on that party member's square without anyone spending a turn or playing a caster animation. Nothing happens if the party is too small to have that slot filled, and the action waits its turn if another action is still resolving.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The ID of the action to fire on the chosen party member's tile.

optional.name: floats[0]
optional.description: Zero-based position of the party member in the party list, so 0 is the first member. Defaults to 0 when omitted, and the task does nothing when the number is at or beyond the current party size.

tasks.officialDescription: Executes 'sValue' action on the current landing party actor in slot 'fValue' (starting at 0).

tasks.name: applyElement

uses.description: Hits a single tile with an element, exactly as if an attack of that element had struck it. The tile's terrain reacts, so it may burn, freeze, get wet, break or change into whatever the terrain's reaction to that element is, and every actor standing on the tile reacts to the element as well. Tiles outside the zone bounds are ignored.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The element to apply to the tile. It must be spelled as one of the game's element names, though capitalisation does not matter.

optional.name: tileCoords[0]
optional.description: The tile to hit. If omitted it defaults to the off-map tile (-1,-1), which is out of bounds and so does nothing.

tasks.officialDescription: Applies 'sValue' element at X,Y.

tasks.name: applyElementToArea

uses.description: Hits every tile in a rectangular block with an element, as if an attack of that element had struck each of them. Each tile's terrain reacts and every actor standing on it reacts too, so a block can be set alight, frozen, flooded or shattered in one go. Tiles that fall outside the zone are skipped, and the block is walked column by column from its top-left corner, which is the order a staggered delay follows.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The element applied to every tile in the block. It must be spelled as one of the game's element names, though capitalisation does not matter.

required.name: strings[1]
required.description: The width and height of the block, written as two whole numbers separated by a comma, such as "5,3". Because the value itself contains a comma it cannot be written inside a taskString; this task has to be set up as a trigger effect so the value arrives as a single string.

optional.name: floats[0]
optional.description: Seconds of extra delay added for each successive tile, producing a ripple that spreads out from the top-left corner instead of hitting everything at once. Defaults to no delay, so the whole block reacts immediately. Delayed tiles react later in real time, once their own timer runs out.

optional.name: tileCoords[0]
optional.description: The top-left corner of the block. If omitted it defaults to the off-map tile (-1,-1), which pushes most or all of the block outside the zone so little or nothing is affected.

tasks.officialDescription: Applies 'sValue' element to a rectangle starting at XY with width/height set by sValue2 (X,Y). fValue adds an incremental delay between tiles.

tasks.name: applyElementToZone

uses.description: Hits every tile in the whole current zone with an element at once, so all terrain that reacts to it changes together — a map-wide dousing, freeze, burn or thaw. Actors are left alone unless you ask for them too. Everything happens in a single instant with no ripple or delay.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The element applied to every tile in the zone. It must be spelled as one of the game's element names, though capitalisation does not matter.

optional.name: bools[0]
optional.description: When true, every actor in the zone also reacts to the element, on top of the terrain. Defaults to false, which affects terrain only.

tasks.officialDescription: Applies 'sValue' element to entire zone. If bValue1, also applies to Actors in the zone.

tasks.name: setTileTerrain

uses.description: Replaces the terrain on a single tile with a different terrain type, so the ground there becomes water, stone, grass, a wall or whatever else you name. The tile's own sprite and the sprites of the eight tiles around it are recalculated so the new terrain blends into its surroundings, and lighting is rebuilt if either the old or new terrain blocks light. Nothing happens if the tile is outside the zone, if no terrain type by that name exists, or if the tile already uses that terrain type.

optional.name: strings[0]
optional.description: The ID of the terrain type to change the tile to. If omitted or left empty, the tile keeps the terrain it already has, which means the task does nothing.

optional.name: bools[0]
optional.description: When true, the terrain-change puff effect is played over the tile, but only if the terrain being replaced is one that shows effects when it reacts. Defaults to false, so the change is silent.

optional.name: tileCoords[0]
optional.description: The tile to change. If omitted it defaults to the off-map tile (-1,-1), which is out of bounds and so nothing happens.

tasks.officialDescription: Sets tile at X,Y to 'sValue' terrainTypeID. If bValue1, shows terrain change FX.

tasks.name: setTileTerrainArea

uses.description: Changes every tile in a rectangle to the same terrain type, letting you carve out a lake, wall off a room or pave a road in one step. The tiles are not changed at once: each one is handed to the task queue and applied on a later frame, which lets you stagger them so the change sweeps across the rectangle rather than appearing instantly. The sweep runs column by column from the top-left corner, or from the bottom-right corner if you ask for it reversed. Tiles that fall outside the zone, and tiles that already use the target terrain, are left alone.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The ID of the terrain type every tile in the rectangle is changed to. It is passed along inside a generated task, so the value cannot contain a comma.

optional.name: strings[1]
optional.description: The bottom-right corner of the rectangle, written as two whole numbers separated by a comma, such as "12,8". It overrides the second tile coordinate when supplied, and exists so the second corner can be given as a trigger effect, where only one tile coordinate can be passed. Because it contains a comma it cannot be written inside a taskString.

optional.name: floats[0]
optional.description: Seconds of extra delay added for each successive tile, turning the change into a sweep across the rectangle. Defaults to no extra delay, so every tile changes on the next frame together.

optional.name: bools[0]
optional.description: When true, the terrain-change puff effect is played over each tile as it changes, but only for tiles whose old terrain shows effects when it reacts. Defaults to false.

optional.name: bools[1]
optional.description: When true, the tiles are processed in reverse, so a staggered sweep starts at the bottom-right corner instead of the top-left. Defaults to false. Supplying it requires the first flag to be supplied as well.

optional.name: tileCoords[0]
optional.description: The top-left corner of the rectangle. If omitted it defaults to the off-map tile (-1,-1), which starts the rectangle outside the zone.

optional.name: tileCoords[1]
optional.description: The bottom-right corner of the rectangle, inclusive. If omitted it defaults to (-1,-1), which usually makes the rectangle empty so nothing changes. A second tile coordinate can only be supplied inside a taskString, so trigger effects must use the second string instead.

tasks.officialDescription: Sets tiles in a rectangle to 'sValue' terrainTypeID, starting at the top left of X,Y through to the bottom right set in sValue2 as 'X,Y'. fValue adds a delay between each tile change. If bValue1, shows terrain change FX. If bValue2, reverses order of tiles changed.

tasks.name: script

uses.description: Runs one of the game's loaded Lua scripts by name. The script's text is executed straight away; if it fails, the error is written to the on-screen debug output instead of stopping the game. Naming a script that was never loaded makes the task fail outright.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The name of the Lua script to run, as it was registered when the game loaded its scripts.

tasks.officialDescription: Executes sValue.lua.

tasks.name: consolecommand

uses.description: Runs a debug-console command line exactly as if it had been typed into the in-game console, then wipes the on-screen debug text. The line is a task name followed by its arguments separated by spaces, and each argument is sorted by what it looks like: true/false become flags, numbers become numbers, and everything else stays text. The command runs on the player actor, and a badly formatted argument is reported as an error rather than crashing.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The console command line: a task name, then its arguments separated by spaces rather than commas. Because a taskString is split on commas, the arguments here must be space-separated to survive.

tasks.officialDescription: Executes consolecommand sValue.

tasks.name: togglePause

uses.description: Flips the freeze on actors and actions in the current zone: if they were running they stop, and if they were already frozen they resume. While frozen, actor updates, AI and real-time movement stop, so the world holds still while menus, dialog and the camera keep working. The freeze is lifted automatically whenever a new zone is loaded.

tasks.officialDescription: Toggles pause of all actors and actions.

tasks.name: preventInteraction

uses.description: Locks the player out of interacting with the world for a number of seconds. While the lock is up, movement and other input are ignored, the cursor is hidden or replaced by the loading cursor for longer waits, and item price tags are hidden under roofs. The value is set outright rather than combined with any lock already running, so a smaller number can cut an existing lock short and zero clears it immediately.

optional.name: floats[0]
optional.description: How many seconds the player is prevented from interacting. Defaults to 0, which clears any lock currently in place. Waits longer than about a third of a second show the loading cursor.

tasks.officialDescription: Disables player input for fValue.

tasks.name: delayActions

uses.description: Holds off the next action for a number of seconds, giving whatever is happening on screen time to finish before anything else resolves. While the wait is running, queued casts and actions sit still, combat will not end, autosaving is postponed, and actors do not start their next act. The wait is only ever extended, never shortened, so a value lower than the delay already running has no effect.

optional.name: floats[0]
optional.description: How many seconds to hold off the next action. Defaults to 0, which leaves any existing wait untouched.

tasks.officialDescription: Disables actors and actions for fValue.

tasks.name: cutsceneMode

uses.description: Turns cutscene mode on or off. In cutscene mode the player actor stops taking orders while every other actor keeps moving and acting on its own, roofs stop hiding what is underneath, holding the use key fast-forwards the scene, and sounds are not cleared when a new zone loads — which is what lets a scripted scene play out across zones. Turning it on also switches off the hold-to-speed-up-enemy-turns toggle. The mode is switched off automatically when combat starts or a zone finishes loading.

optional.name: bools[0]
optional.description: True turns cutscene mode on, false turns it off. Defaults to on when no flag is supplied.

tasks.officialDescription: cutsceneMode allows actors to keep moving/etc regardless of turn. If bValue1, cutsceneMode = true. Otherwise false.

tasks.name: timeSpeed

uses.description: Sets how fast game time runs, as a multiplier on every frame's elapsed time, so animations, movement and timers all speed up or slow down together. A value of 1 is normal speed, 2 is double speed, and lower values give slow motion. The game clamps the resulting speed to a tenth of normal at the slowest, so this cannot be used to freeze the game, and it stays in force until something sets it back.

optional.name: floats[0]
optional.description: The game speed multiplier, with 1 being normal. Defaults to 0, which is clamped up to a tenth of normal speed rather than stopping time.

tasks.officialDescription: Sets the game speed to fValue.

tasks.name: setFactionHostile

uses.description: Turns every actor of a faction currently in the zone hostile to the player, or turns them friendly again. Hostile actors will fight the party and can be attacked; friendly ones will not. Only actors already spawned in the zone are affected, so anything that appears later keeps its own setting.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The ID of the faction whose actors change stance. Every actor in the zone belonging to it is affected.

optional.name: floats[0]
optional.description: One or more makes the faction hostile; anything less makes it friendly. Defaults to 0, so leaving it out makes the faction friendly.

optional.name: tileCoords[0]
optional.description: Supplying any tile coordinate whose x is not -1 also wipes the affected actors' dialog nodes, so they can no longer be talked to. The tile itself is not used for anything else. Leaving it out keeps their dialog intact.

tasks.officialDescription: Sets all actors of 'sValue' faction to hostile if fValue =1+. Otherwise sets faction nonhostile. If xValue != -1, clears dialogNode.

tasks.name: setFactionAI

uses.description: Switches every actor of a faction currently in the zone over to a different AI script, changing how they behave from that moment on. Each affected actor restarts at the beginning of the new script, drops whatever it was waiting on, and forgets any signals it had queued. Only actors already in the zone are changed.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The ID of the faction whose actors get the new AI script.

required.name: strings[1]
required.description: The name of the AI script the actors switch to. The special name "base" returns each actor to the script it treats as its baseline.

tasks.officialDescription: Sets AI script of all actors of 'sValue' faction to 'sValue2'.

tasks.name: killFaction

uses.description: Knocks out every actor of a faction currently in the zone at once. Each one goes down as if it had just been defeated: charging and queued actions are cancelled, death reactions and triggers fire, and hostile members hand over their experience to the party. Actors marked unkillable survive, and actors that were already down are simply marked out without replaying the defeat sequence.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The ID of the faction whose actors are knocked out.

tasks.officialDescription: Incaps all actors of 'sValue' faction.

tasks.name: removeFaction

uses.description: Deletes every actor of a faction from the world outright, with no death, no corpse and no experience awarded. They are pulled out of the party if they were in it, unmounted, taken off the turn order, and their open inventory windows are closed; the actors themselves disappear on the next frame. Members of the faction sitting in a loaded special zone, such as a boarded ship's interior, are removed too.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The ID of the faction whose actors are deleted.

tasks.officialDescription: Removes all actors of 'sValue' faction.

tasks.name: changeFaction

uses.description: Moves every actor of one faction in the zone over to another faction, which changes who they count as allies and enemies of. Actors the player controls are left alone, so party members never get reassigned. Their hostility toward the player is not touched, only their faction allegiance.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The ID of the faction to move actors out of.

required.name: strings[1]
required.description: The ID of the faction to move them into.

tasks.officialDescription: Changes all actors of 'sValue' faction to 'sValue2' faction.

tasks.name: moveToNewZone

uses.description: Sends the party straight to another zone with no save and no travel confirmation, dropping them on a chosen tile. The party stops moving, dismounts, and is carried across along with any mounts; barracks members are left behind. The screen fades out and back in, and the player is briefly locked out of interacting while the new zone loads. Unlike the travel tasks this does not ask about fleeing when used during combat.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The ID of the zone to load. It is resolved to a zone file in the game's or a mod's zone data.

optional.name: floats[0]
optional.description: How fast the loading fade runs; larger is faster. Defaults to 0, which falls back to the game's normal fade speed.

optional.name: tileCoords[0]
optional.description: The tile in the new zone the party arrives on, nudged aside if that tile is blocked. Giving an x of -99 instead treats the y as a travel-point number from 0 to 9, so the party arrives at whatever item in the new zone is flagged as that travel point, facing the way that item points. If omitted it defaults to (-1,-1), which is pulled back inside the map and puts the party in the top-left corner.

tasks.officialDescription: Cutscene & scripting use. Transfers party to 'sValue' zone at X,Y. fValue, if specified, sets the fade to black speed.

tasks.name: travel

uses.description: Sends the party to another zone the normal way, autosaving on the way out and fading the screen to black and back. If this happens during combat the player is asked to confirm fleeing first, and repeated fleeing from the same enemies is called out as costing fame and morale; the travel only happens if they agree. Nothing happens at all while the player is in the middle of aiming an action.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The ID of the zone to travel to. It is resolved to a zone file in the game's or a mod's zone data.

optional.name: floats[0]
optional.description: The direction in degrees the party faces on arrival, with -1 leaving their facing alone. Defaults to 0. When the player is asked to confirm fleeing instead, this is passed along as the number the confirmation carries.

optional.name: bools[0]
optional.description: When true, the autosave that normally happens on leaving is skipped. Defaults to false, so travelling autosaves.

optional.name: tileCoords[0]
optional.description: The tile in the destination zone the party arrives on. Giving an x of -99 treats the y as a travel-point number from 0 to 9 instead. If omitted it defaults to (-1,-1), which lands the party in the top-left corner. When fleeing combat, this tile is passed along to the confirmation.

tasks.officialDescription: Travel-friendly trigger moves party to 'sValue' zone at X,Y. fValue = party facingRot. Autosaves unless bValue1=true

tasks.name: travel_point

uses.description: Sends the party to another zone, arriving at one of that zone's numbered travel points rather than at a tile you name, and facing the way that travel point is turned. Travel points are items in the destination zone flagged with a travel-point number, which makes this the reliable way to link doors and stairways without hard-coding coordinates. Fleeing confirmation is asked for if this happens during combat, and nothing happens while the player is aiming an action.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The ID of the zone to travel to. It is resolved to a zone file in the game's or a mod's zone data.

optional.name: floats[0]
optional.description: Which numbered travel point in the destination zone to arrive at, from 0 to 9. Defaults to 0.

optional.name: bools[0]
optional.description: When true, the autosave that normally happens on leaving is skipped. Defaults to false.

optional.name: bools[1]
optional.description: When true, the party slips into the zone quietly: zone-entry triggers, zone effects, weather spawns, zone merges and the opening NPC turn are all skipped. Defaults to false. Supplying it requires the autosave flag to be supplied as well.

tasks.officialDescription: Travel-friendly trigger moves party to 'sValue' zone at point fValue. If bValue1, don't autosave. If bValue2, acts as if entered via console (doesn't roll loot tables, etc).

tasks.name: travel_point_g

uses.description: Sends the party to whichever zone a global variable currently names, arriving at one of that zone's numbered travel points and facing the way it is turned. Use this when the destination is decided at runtime — a zone chosen earlier and stashed in a variable — rather than fixed when the mod is written. Fleeing confirmation is asked for if this happens during combat, and nothing happens while the player is aiming an action.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The name of the global variable holding the ID of the zone to travel to. The variable's contents, not this name, are used as the zone.

optional.name: floats[0]
optional.description: Which numbered travel point in the destination zone to arrive at, from 0 to 9. Defaults to 0.

optional.name: bools[0]
optional.description: When true, the autosave that normally happens on leaving is skipped. Defaults to false.

optional.name: bools[1]
optional.description: When true, the party slips into the zone quietly: zone-entry triggers, zone effects, weather spawns, zone merges and the opening NPC turn are all skipped. Defaults to false. Supplying it requires the autosave flag to be supplied as well.

tasks.officialDescription: As travel_point, but goes to zoneID of globalVar 'sValue'.

tasks.name: travel_leaveLocation

uses.description: Takes the party out of the town, dungeon or other location they are currently inside and puts them back on the map beside its entrance. Anything the player is carrying by hand is dumped into the stash, the cargo hold, or onto the ground, and party members who are not in the landing party are left behind unless the party is aboard a ship. If this happens during combat the player is asked to confirm fleeing first, and nothing happens at all if the party is not inside a location.

optional.name: bools[0]
optional.description: When true, an omitted arrival offset is left as (-1,-1) rather than being turned into no offset, which places the party one tile up and left of the location instead of on it. Defaults to false.

optional.name: bools[1]
optional.description: When true, the autosave that normally happens on leaving is skipped. Defaults to false.

optional.name: tileCoords[0]
optional.description: How far from the location's own spot on the map to place the party, as an offset added to it. If omitted it becomes no offset at all, unless the first flag is set.

tasks.officialDescription: Moves party to where the current Location is. IMPORTANT: XY determines pos offset from that Location. If !bValue1, XY of -1,-1 is treated as 0,0.

tasks.name: travel_gVars

uses.description: Sends the party back to the zone and tile recorded in the game's remembered previous-position variables, which is how a scripted detour returns the player to where they came from. The destination zone comes from the stored previous zone and the arrival tile from the stored x and y, so nothing needs to be named in the task itself. Fleeing confirmation is asked for if this happens during combat, and nothing happens while the player is aiming an action.

optional.name: floats[0]
optional.description: The direction in degrees the party faces on arrival, with -1 leaving their facing alone. Defaults to 0.

optional.name: bools[0]
optional.description: When true, the autosave that normally happens on leaving is skipped. Defaults to false.

tasks.officialDescription: Travel to zone gVar 'playerPrevZone' at XY 'playerX', 'playerY'. fValue = facingRot.

tasks.name: travel_noSave

uses.description: Sends the party to another zone without autosaving first, so the trip cannot be used to lock in progress. If this happens during combat the player is asked to confirm fleeing instead, and the travel only goes ahead if they agree. Outside combat the party is moved across immediately and the player is locked out of interacting for a moment while the zone loads; unlike the other travel tasks this one does not check whether an action is being aimed.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The ID of the zone to travel to. It is resolved to a zone file in the game's or a mod's zone data.

required.name: floats[0]
required.description: The direction in degrees the party faces on arrival, with -1 leaving their facing alone. It must be supplied: unlike the other travel tasks this one reads it without a fallback.

optional.name: tileCoords[0]
optional.description: The tile in the destination zone the party arrives on. Giving an x of -99 treats the y as a travel-point number from 0 to 9 instead. If omitted it defaults to (-1,-1), which lands the party in the top-left corner.

tasks.officialDescription: DO NOT USE. Use 'travel' task instead.

tasks.name: travel_procedural

uses.description: Builds a fresh randomly generated dungeon or wilderness from a level-data recipe and sends the party straight into it. A grid of zones is generated with a winding path from the bottom edge to the top, any mandatory rooms the recipe demands are scattered through it, and the last zone on the path leads out to a zone you name. Any previously saved copy of that same generated world is wiped first, so the layout is new every time. The party normally enters through the first zone's bottom exit, which leads back where they came from.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The ID of the level-data recipe describing the world to generate: its grid size, room sizes, path density and mandatory pieces. Nothing is generated if no recipe by that name exists.

required.name: strings[1]
required.description: The zone the far end of the generated world leads out to, optionally followed by a comma and a second zone ID that replaces the entrance's back-exit. Spaces are stripped out. Because the two-part form contains a comma it cannot be written inside a taskString, so it has to be supplied as a trigger effect.

optional.name: bools[0]
optional.description: When true, the entrance zone gets no exit back to the zone the party left, and the party is dropped in the middle of the entrance zone facing east instead of arriving at its bottom edge. Defaults to false.

optional.name: bools[1]
optional.description: When true, the tile the party will be returned to is worked out from the area of the trigger that fired this task — the middle of its width, one row below its bottom edge — rather than from a tile you give. Defaults to false.

optional.name: tileCoords[0]
optional.description: The tile in the current zone the party should be put back on when they come out of the generated world; the game rewrites the nearest return-path trigger in the entrance zone to point here. If omitted it defaults to (-1,-1), which means no return path is recorded at all.

tasks.officialDescription: Travel-friendly trigger moves party to new procedural world made from levelData 'sValue', which leads to 'sValue2'. If bValue1, there is no way back. If XY set a specific returnXY. bValue2 uses trigger area as returnXY. If sValue2 matches a globalTriggerID the exit executes that trigger instead of a travel trigger. If sValue2 has 2 values (EX: z1, z2) the 2nd one is the zone entered from.

tasks.name: travel_procedural_point

uses.description: Builds a fresh randomly generated dungeon or wilderness from a level-data recipe and sends the party into it at a chosen travel point rather than at the entrance's bottom edge. A grid of zones is generated with a winding path from the bottom edge to the top, mandatory rooms are scattered through it, and the last zone leads out to a zone you name. Any previously saved copy of that generated world is wiped first, so the layout is new every time.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The ID of the level-data recipe describing the world to generate: its grid size, room sizes, path density and mandatory pieces. Nothing is generated if no recipe by that name exists.

required.name: strings[1]
required.description: The zone the far end of the generated world leads out to, optionally followed by a comma and a second zone ID that replaces the entrance's back-exit. Spaces are stripped out. Because the two-part form contains a comma it cannot be written inside a taskString, so it has to be supplied as a trigger effect.

optional.name: floats[0]
optional.description: Which numbered travel point in the entrance zone the party arrives at, from 0 to 9. It is only consulted when the back-exit is switched off; with the back-exit left on the party always arrives at travel point 0. Defaults to 0.

optional.name: bools[0]
optional.description: When true, the entrance zone gets no exit back to the zone the party left, which is also what lets the chosen travel point take effect. Defaults to false.

optional.name: bools[1]
optional.description: When true, the tile the party will be returned to is worked out from the area of the trigger that fired this task — the middle of its width, one row below its bottom edge — rather than from a tile you give. Defaults to false.

optional.name: tileCoords[0]
optional.description: The tile in the current zone the party should be put back on when they come out of the generated world; the game rewrites the nearest return-path trigger in the entrance zone to point here. If omitted it defaults to (-1,-1), which means no return path is recorded at all.

tasks.officialDescription: As 'travel_procedural', but fValue specifies a travelPoint to place the party on.

tasks.name: travel_setReturnPath

uses.description: Sends the party to another zone and, at the same time, records where they should come back out. On arrival the game finds the nearest way-back trigger in the new zone and rewrites it to lead to the zone the party just left, at the recorded tile and facing the opposite way, so a door leads back to the door it came from without either side hard-coding the other. The party autosaves on the way out; if this happens during combat the player is asked to confirm fleeing first, and nothing happens while an action is being aimed.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The ID of the zone to travel to. It is resolved to a zone file in the game's or a mod's zone data.

optional.name: floats[0]
optional.description: The direction in degrees the party faces on arrival; the recorded way back faces the opposite direction. Defaults to 0. When the player is asked to confirm fleeing instead, this is passed along as the number the confirmation carries.

optional.name: bools[0]
optional.description: When true, the tile to come back to is worked out from the area of the trigger that fired this task — the middle of its width, one row below its bottom edge — and the way back always faces south. Defaults to false, in which case the return tile is derived from the arrival tile, only working out sensibly when the party arrives along the top or left edge of the new zone.

optional.name: tileCoords[0]
optional.description: The tile in the destination zone the party arrives on. Giving an x of -99 treats the y as a travel-point number from 0 to 9 instead. If omitted it defaults to (-1,-1), which lands the party in the top-left corner.

tasks.officialDescription: Like 'travel', but sets the closest 'returnPath' trigger in the next zone to go back to this zone. If bValue, sets returnTC to the btm mid of the trigger area.

tasks.name: returnPath

uses.description: Sends the party back the way they came, to a zone and tile that were filled in for it automatically rather than written by hand. A trigger carrying this task has its destination, tile and facing rewritten the moment the party arrives somewhere via a return-path travel, so the same trigger sends them home no matter which door they came through. Whatever destination is stored at the time is autosaved into and travelled to; nothing at all happens if no destination has been filled in yet, and during combat the player is asked to confirm fleeing first.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The ID of the zone to return to. This is normally left as a placeholder and overwritten when the party arrives; if it is empty the task does nothing at all.

optional.name: floats[0]
optional.description: The direction in degrees the party faces on arrival, normally overwritten to face back the way they came. Defaults to 0.

optional.name: tileCoords[0]
optional.description: The tile in the destination zone the party arrives on, normally overwritten with the recorded return tile. If omitted it defaults to (-1,-1), which lands the party in the top-left corner.

tasks.officialDescription: Travel trigger that is set by 'travel_setReturnPath'.

tasks.name: travel_g

uses.description: Sends the party back to the entrance of the most recently generated procedural world, whose zone name the game records automatically when that world is built. Nothing needs naming in the task itself, which makes it the way to re-enter a dungeon the player has already been sent into. The party autosaves on the way out; during combat the player is asked to confirm fleeing first, and nothing happens while an action is being aimed.

optional.name: floats[0]
optional.description: The direction in degrees the party faces on arrival, with -1 leaving their facing alone. Defaults to 0.

optional.name: tileCoords[0]
optional.description: The tile in the destination zone the party arrives on. Giving an x of -99 treats the y as a travel-point number from 0 to 9 instead. If omitted it defaults to (-1,-1), which lands the party in the top-left corner.

tasks.officialDescription: Travel to the zone name stored in globalVar 'lastProcZoneEntry'.

tasks.name: setGlobalVar

uses.description: Stores a piece of text in a global variable, creating it if it does not exist yet and overwriting whatever was there. The game also records the world time at which the variable was last written, which other checks can ask about. Writing a variable makes the game re-check its achievement conditions.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The name of the global variable to write to.

required.name: strings[1]
required.description: The text to store. It must not be empty — an empty value falls through to storing a number instead. Spaces survive being stored and come back intact when the variable is read.

uses.description: Stores a number in a global variable, creating it if it does not exist yet and overwriting whatever was there. The game also records the world time at which the variable was last written, which other checks can ask about. Writing a variable makes the game re-check its achievement conditions.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The name of the global variable to write to.

required.name: floats[0]
required.description: The number to store. It is only used when no non-empty second string is supplied.

tasks.officialDescription: Sets globalVar sValue to fValue (or sValue2 if specified).

tasks.name: setGlobalVar_math

uses.description: Works out a formula and stores the answer in a global variable, replacing whatever was there. The formula is evaluated with the contextual actor standing in as both the caster and the target, so it can read that actor's stats, position and state. By default the answer is cut down to a whole number, which is what most counters and flags want.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The name of the global variable to write the answer into. It is reset to 0 before the answer is added, so the result is an assignment rather than an increment.

required.name: strings[1]
required.description: The formula to work out. It is evaluated against the contextual actor as both caster and target.

optional.name: bools[0]
optional.description: When true the answer keeps its decimal part; when false it is truncated to a whole number. Defaults to false.

tasks.officialDescription: Sets globalVar sValue to Formula in sValue2. Decimals will be truncated. If b1, decimals won't be truncated.

tasks.name: setGlobalVar_toOtherGlobalVar

uses.description: Copies one global variable's contents into another, overwriting whatever the destination held. Reading a variable that has never been set gives the text "0", so copying from an unset variable stores that. This is the way to snapshot a value before something else changes it.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The name of the global variable to write into.

required.name: strings[1]
required.description: The name of the global variable to read from. Its contents, not this name, are what gets stored.

tasks.officialDescription: Sets globalVar sValue to globalVar sValue2.

tasks.name: setGlobalVar_toNearestLocID

uses.description: Finds the closest non-port location — a town, ruin, camp or other place on the map that is not a harbour — within a given range and stores its ID in a global variable. Distances on the world map are measured as sailing distance rather than straight-line tiles. If nothing qualifies the variable is set to an empty value, and the whole task is skipped unless both a variable name and a range are supplied.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The name of the global variable that receives the found location's ID, or an empty value if nothing matched.

required.name: floats[0]
required.description: How far away to look, in tiles. The search covers only locations within this distance of the origin.

optional.name: strings[1]
optional.description: Which zone's locations to search, defaulting to the world map. It may also be a comma-separated list whose first entry is the zone and whose remaining entries are tags a location must carry to qualify. Because the list form contains commas it cannot be written that way inside a taskString; use the extra strings instead.

optional.name: strings[2+]
optional.description: Extra tags appended to the tag list, one per value, so a taskString can supply tags that would otherwise need commas. They are ignored unless a zone was given in the previous string.

optional.name: bools[0]
optional.description: When true, locations the player is not meant to be able to find are included in the search. Defaults to false, which limits the search to discoverable locations whose discovery conditions are currently met.

optional.name: bools[1]
optional.description: When true, the tags are treated as tags to avoid rather than tags to require, so a location carrying any of them is skipped. Defaults to false. Supplying it requires the first flag to be supplied as well.

optional.name: tileCoords[0]
optional.description: The tile to measure distance from. If omitted, distances are measured from whichever actor is currently taking its turn.

tasks.officialDescription: Sets the nearest discoverable non-port location's ID within fValue radius of X,Y in the overworld zone set in sValue2 (defaults to eral if not set) to the gVar set in sValue. If X,Y is unset, will use player's X,Y. You can specify tags the location needs to contain in comma,separated,values after the overworld in sValue2 (eg, sValue2 = eral,grove). If b1, will also check locations that can't be discovered. If b2, locations must NOT have any of the tags set.

tasks.name: setGlobalVarToZoneProperty

uses.description: Reads one of the current zone's own settings and stores it in a global variable as text, letting a mod branch on things like whether the zone is peaceful, its size, or its music. The value is written out the way the game would print it, so a yes/no setting is stored as True or False and a number as its digits. Asking for a setting the zone does not have stores False, and nothing happens at all if no zone is loaded.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The name of the global variable to write the setting into.

required.name: strings[1]
required.description: The name of the zone setting to read, spelled exactly as it is written in zone data. An unrecognised name stores False rather than reporting an error.

tasks.officialDescription: Sets globalVar 'sValue' to the string representation of the current zone's property, set in sValue2.

tasks.name: setGlobalVar_toPartyActorID

uses.description: Stores the ID of one of the player's party members in a global variable, picked by its slot in the party. This is how a script gets hold of a specific companion to act on later. If the party is too small to have that slot filled, the variable is set to an empty value instead.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The name of the global variable that receives the party member's ID, or an empty value if the slot is not filled.

optional.name: floats[0]
optional.description: Zero-based position of the party member in the party list, so 0 is the leader. Defaults to 0.

tasks.officialDescription: Sets globalVar sValue to ID of partyActor[fValue].

tasks.name: setGlobalVar_toActorID

uses.description: Stores the ID of the actor the task is running on into a global variable, so later tasks can refer back to whoever triggered this one. If there is no contextual actor — for instance when the task is run from something that is not attached to anyone — the variable is set to an empty value instead.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The name of the global variable that receives the contextual actor's ID, or an empty value if there is none.

tasks.officialDescription: Sets globalVar sValue to ID of the Actor that executed the trigger.

tasks.name: setGlobalVar_toCrewActorID

uses.description: Stores the ID of one of a ship's crew members in a global variable, picked by its position in that ship's crew list. This is the way to reach a specific sailor aboard a named vessel and then act on them. If the ship does not exist, carries no crew, or has fewer crew than the slot asked for, the variable is set to an empty value.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The name of the global variable that receives the crew member's ID, or an empty value if nothing matched.

optional.name: strings[1]
optional.description: The ID of the ship or actor whose crew is read; it must be present in the zone. If omitted the variable is simply set to an empty value.

optional.name: floats[0]
optional.description: Zero-based position in that ship's crew list, so 0 is the first crew member. Defaults to 0.

tasks.officialDescription: Sets gVar 'sValue' to the ID of the crew Actor in the 'fValue'-th slot (starting at 0) of the ship Actor specified in 'sValue2'.

tasks.name: setGlobalVarWithCommas

uses.description: Joins several values together with commas between them and stores the result in a global variable. It exists because a taskString is itself split on commas, so this is the way to build a comma-separated value — a coordinate pair or a tag list — that another task can later take apart. Giving no values to join stores an empty value.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The name of the global variable to write the joined text into.

optional.name: strings[1+]
optional.description: The pieces to join, in order, with a comma placed between each pair. Any number may be given; supplying none stores an empty value.

tasks.officialDescription: Sets globalVar strings[0] to the remaining combined strings[] values, joined with commas between each.

tasks.name: clearGlobalVar

uses.description: Deletes a global variable outright, along with the record of when it was last written. This is different from storing an empty value: the variable stops existing, and anything reading it afterwards gets the text "0" as though it had never been set. Use it to reset a flag completely rather than blanking it.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The name of the global variable to delete.

tasks.officialDescription: Removes the globalVar 'sValue' from the list of globalVars.

tasks.name: sanitizeGlobalVar

uses.description: Cleans up the text already stored in a global variable and writes the cleaned version back into the same variable. By default it strips out spaces, colons, minus signs, arithmetic symbols, periods and commas and lowercases what is left, which is what makes two differently punctuated player answers compare equal. If the result comes out as "0" — which is what an unset variable reads as — it is stored as an empty value instead.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The name of the global variable to clean up. Its current contents are read, cleaned and written back to the same variable.

optional.name: strings[1]
optional.description: A set of characters to filter by, written as one run of characters with no separators. Supplying it switches off the default cleanup and instead keeps or drops characters by this list, matched without regard to case while the original casing is preserved. Defaults to empty, which uses the default cleanup. It cannot contain a comma when written inside a taskString.

optional.name: bools[0]
optional.description: When true, only characters in the filter list are kept; when false, characters in the list are the ones removed. Defaults to false. It has no effect unless a filter list is supplied.

tasks.officialDescription: Removes all characters that appear in sValue2 from the gVar set in sValue. If b1, only KEEPS characters that appear in sValue2 instead. Comparisons are case-insensitive. If sValue2 is blank or unset, runs the standard sanitize on it (spaces, periods, commas, math operators and colons), which also sets it to all lower case.

tasks.name: modGlobalVar

uses.description: Adds a number to a global variable, treating it as a counter. A variable that does not exist yet starts at zero before the addition, and the result is clamped to roughly plus or minus ten million. Pass a negative number to subtract.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The name of the global variable to add to.

required.name: floats[0]
required.description: The amount to add; negative values subtract.

tasks.officialDescription: Adds 'fValue' to globalVar 'sValue'.

tasks.name: modNodeIDGlobalVar_1

uses.description: Adds one to the global variable named after the dialog node this task was run from, which is the usual way to count how many times a conversation branch has been taken. The variable is created starting at zero if it did not exist, so the first run leaves it at one. Nothing needs naming because the node supplies the variable name itself.

tasks.officialDescription: Must be used in dialog. Adds 1 to the globalVar with the same ID as the currentDialogNodeID.

tasks.name: modNodeIDGlobalVar_999

uses.description: Adds 999 to the global variable named after the dialog node this task was run from, which is the usual way to slam a conversation branch shut for good rather than merely counting a visit. The variable is created starting at zero if it did not exist. Nothing needs naming because the node supplies the variable name itself.

tasks.officialDescription: Must be used in dialog. Adds 999 to the globalVar with the same ID as the currentDialogNodeID.

tasks.name: appendToGlobalVar_math

uses.description: Works out a formula and tacks the answer onto the end of a global variable's existing text rather than replacing it. This builds up a string piece by piece, which is how a list or a generated name gets assembled across several steps. The formula is evaluated with no actor attached, so it can only use values that do not depend on who is involved.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The name of the global variable to append to. Its current contents are read first, so an unset variable starts from the text "0".

required.name: strings[1]
required.description: The formula whose answer is appended, written out as a number.

tasks.officialDescription: Appends the result of Formula 'sValue2' to the end of globalVar 'sValue'.

tasks.name: appendToGlobalVar_string

uses.description: Tacks a piece of text onto the end of a global variable's existing contents rather than replacing them. This builds up a string piece by piece, which is how a list or a generated name gets assembled across several steps. An unset variable starts from the text "0", so clear or set it first if you want to start clean.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The name of the global variable to append to.

required.name: strings[1]
required.description: The text to append.

tasks.officialDescription: Appends 'sValue2' to the end of globalVar 'sValue'.

tasks.name: appendToGlobalVar_zoneID

uses.description: Tacks the ID of the zone the party is currently in onto the end of a global variable's existing contents. This is how a variable name or a record of where something happened gets built without knowing the zone in advance. An unset variable starts from the text "0", so clear or set it first if you want to start clean.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The name of the global variable to append the current zone's ID to.

tasks.officialDescription: Appends the ID of the current zone to the end of globalVar 'sValue'.

tasks.name: appendToGlobalVar_locID

uses.description: Tacks the ID of the town, port or other location the party is currently inside onto the end of a global variable's existing contents. This is how a per-location variable name gets built without knowing which location the player is in. Nothing happens at all if the party is not inside a location, and an unset variable starts from the text "0".

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The name of the global variable to append the current location's ID to.

tasks.officialDescription: Appends the ID of the current location to the end of globalVar 'sValue'.

tasks.name: setNodeIDGlobalVar_1

uses.description: Sets the global variable named after the dialog node this task was run from to one, unless it is already one. This is the plain way to mark a conversation branch as having been seen, without counting repeats. Nothing needs naming because the node supplies the variable name itself.

tasks.officialDescription: Must be used in dialog. Sets the globalVar with the same ID as the currentDialogNodeID to 1.

tasks.name: setGlobalVarTo0

uses.description: Sets a global variable to zero, wiping whatever text or number it held. Unlike deleting the variable this leaves it in place with a definite value of zero, and stamps the moment it was written. Use it to reset a counter or clear a flag.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The name of the global variable to set to zero.

tasks.officialDescription: Sets globalVar 'sValue' to 0.

tasks.name: setGlobalVarToTalkerID

uses.description: Stores the ID of whoever the player is currently talking to in a global variable, so later tasks can act on that character by name. If no conversation is in progress an empty value is stored. This is the usual way for a dialog to remember which of several identical NPCs it is running on.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The name of the global variable that receives the talker's ID.

tasks.officialDescription: Must be used as a dialog specialEffect. Sets the globalVar 'strings[0]' to the currentActorTalkingTo's ID.

tasks.name: setGlobalVarWithTalkerID

uses.description: Stores a piece of text in a global variable whose name is built by sticking the current talker's ID onto the end of a prefix you give. With nobody being talked to, the prefix alone becomes the variable name.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The prefix of the variable name; the ID of whoever is being talked to is appended to it to form the actual variable written.

required.name: strings[1]
required.description: The text to store. It must not be empty — an empty value falls through to storing a number instead.

uses.description: Stores a number in a global variable whose name is built by sticking the current talker's ID onto the end of a prefix you give. That gives each character their own copy of the same counter, which is how a mod tracks something per NPC without declaring a variable for each one. With nobody being talked to, the prefix alone becomes the variable name.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The prefix of the variable name; the ID of whoever is being talked to is appended to it to form the actual variable written.

optional.name: floats[0]
optional.description: The number to store, written out as text. Defaults to 0. It is only used when no non-empty second string is supplied.

tasks.officialDescription: Must be used as a dialog specialEffect. Sets globalVar 'sValue' + the currentActorTalkingTo's ID to the string set in sValue2, or 'fValue' if not set.

tasks.name: setGlobalVarToLocID

uses.description: Stores the ID of the town, port or other location the party is currently inside in a global variable, so later tasks can act on that place by name. Nothing happens at all if the party is not inside a location, leaving whatever the variable already held. This is how a dialog inside a town figures out which town it is in.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The name of the global variable that receives the current location's ID.

tasks.officialDescription: Sets globalVar 'sValue' to the ID of the current location. Doesn't get set if not in a location.

tasks.name: setGlobalVarToPartyActorNum

uses.description: Stores a number in a global variable, replacing whatever was there. Despite the name it does not look anything up about the party — it simply writes the number you give straight into the named variable. The moment of writing is stamped as well, which some conditions can ask about.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The name of the global variable to write to.

required.name: floats[0]
required.description: The number to store.

tasks.officialDescription: Sets globalVar 'sValue' to 'fValue'.

tasks.name: setGlobalVarPlusLocID

uses.description: Stores a number in a global variable whose name is built by sticking the current location's ID onto the end of a prefix you give. That gives every town or port its own copy of the same counter, which is how a mod tracks per-place progress without declaring a variable for each one. The party must actually be inside a location for this to work.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The prefix of the variable name; the current location's ID is appended to it to form the actual variable written.

required.name: floats[0]
required.description: The number to store.

tasks.officialDescription: Sets the globalVar with the ID of 'sValue' + the current location's ID to 'fValue'.

tasks.name: setGlobalVarPlusLocID_math

uses.description: Works out a formula and stores the answer in a global variable whose name is built by sticking the current location's ID onto the end of a prefix you give. That gives every town or port its own copy of the same value, worked out fresh each time. The formula is evaluated with the contextual actor standing in as both caster and target, and the party must actually be inside a location.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The prefix of the variable name; the current location's ID is appended to it to form the actual variable written. The variable is reset to 0 before the answer is added, so the result is an assignment rather than an increment.

required.name: strings[1]
required.description: The formula to work out. It is evaluated against the contextual actor as both caster and target, and the answer keeps its decimal part.

tasks.officialDescription: Sets the globalVar with the ID of 'sValue' + the current location's ID to the result of the formula set in sValue2.

tasks.name: setGlobalVarPlusZoneID

uses.description: Stores a number in a global variable whose name is built by sticking the current zone's ID onto the end of a prefix you give. That gives every zone its own copy of the same counter, which is how a mod tracks per-map progress without declaring a variable for each one. Unlike the location version this always works, since there is always a current zone.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The prefix of the variable name; the current zone's ID is appended to it to form the actual variable written.

required.name: floats[0]
required.description: The number to store.

tasks.officialDescription: Sets the globalVar with the ID of 'sValue' + the current zone's ID to 'fValue'.

tasks.name: modFame

uses.description: Changes one of the player's standings — their reputation in a particular field — by a given amount, and nudges crew morale by a twentieth of that amount in the same direction. The four standings are explore, trade, combat and piracy, each banked in the global variable named fame_ followed by that word. A floating number pops up on screen and a sound plays to tell the player, except for piracy reputation which changes quietly. The standing is never allowed to fall below zero, outstanding royal commissions are re-evaluated, and giving a change of zero does nothing at all.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: Which standing to change: explore, trade, combat or piracy. It names the counter to adjust, which is the global variable fame_ followed by this word, so an unrecognised name quietly starts a standing of its own. The value piracy additionally suppresses the pop-up and the sound.

required.name: floats[0]
required.description: How much to change the standing by; negative values reduce it. Zero makes the task do nothing.

tasks.officialDescription: Adds 'fValue' to globalVar 'fame_' + 'sValue', displays its associated icon and plays a sound.

tasks.name: goToNodeID_plus_GlobalVar

uses.description: Jumps the conversation to a dialog node whose name is the current node's name with a number stuck on the end, and that number is the current value of the global variable named after the current node. Paired with the tasks that count visits to a node, this walks the player through a numbered series of responses that advances every time they come back. If no node with the resulting name exists the conversation falls back to the talker's default handling.

tasks.officialDescription: Must be used in dialog. Tries to go to the dialogNode with the ID of the current dialogNode, plus the string set in the globalVar with the same ID as the dialogNode ID.

tasks.name: enableUI

uses.description: Brings back the quickslot bar and the character stats panel and clears the game's hidden-interface setting, restoring the normal heads-up display. Use it to end a cutscene or scripted sequence that had stripped the screen bare. The panels only actually appear while the player is walking around, not in menus or other modes.

tasks.officialDescription: Shows the quickslots and character stats windows if they had been previously hidden with 'disableUI'.

tasks.name: disableUI

uses.description: Hides the quickslot bar and the character stats panel, sets the game's hidden-interface setting, and closes the small floating info windows, leaving a bare screen. Use it at the start of a cutscene or any scripted sequence that should look uncluttered. The setting is remembered in the save, so it must be turned back on explicitly.

tasks.officialDescription: Hides the quickslots and character stats windows. Show them again with 'enableUI' task.

tasks.name: unlockHelpGem

uses.description: Grants the player the hint gem and makes it usable straight away, clearing any cooldown on it. This is how a tutorial hands over the in-game hint button the first time it becomes relevant. The gem stays unlocked for the rest of the save.

tasks.officialDescription: Unlocks use of the Help Gem and recharges it.

tasks.name: enableHelpGem

uses.description: Switches the hint gem back on after it has been switched off, without granting it to a player who has not unlocked it yet. Any cooldown already counting down is left running. Use it to re-enable hints once a sequence that suppressed them has ended.

tasks.officialDescription: DO NOT USE. Enables use of the Help Gem (if recharged).

tasks.name: disableHelpGem

uses.description: Switches the hint gem off and marks it as permanently unavailable rather than merely cooling down, so the player cannot ask for a hint. Use it during sequences where a hint would spoil something or make no sense. Switching it back on requires an explicit re-enable.

tasks.officialDescription: DO NOT USE. Disables use of the Help Gem.

tasks.name: save

uses.description: Writes a full named save file the player can load from the menu, using the name you give. If a save by that name already exists a plus sign is added to the end until the name is free, so an existing save is never overwritten. Trailing spaces are trimmed off the name.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The name to save under, as it will appear in the load menu. It must not be empty — an empty name makes the task autosave instead.

uses.description: Writes an autosave, rotating the three autosave slots so the previous two are kept. This ignores the hardcore-mode restriction that normally blocks saving, but it still respects a mod's own block on autosaving. Use it for checkpoints the player is not meant to name.

tasks.officialDescription: Saves to Globals.AUTOSAVE_NAME, and notifies player. Saves to slot sValue if specified (or unused variant if save sValue already exists).

tasks.name: quietsave

uses.description: Writes an autosave without any prompt or fanfare, rotating the three autosave slots so the previous two are kept. This ignores the hardcore-mode restriction that normally blocks saving, but it still respects a mod's own block on autosaving. Use it for silent checkpoints partway through a sequence.

tasks.officialDescription: Saves to Globals.AUTOSAVE_NAME, with no notification.

tasks.name: heal

uses.description: Restores health to a single actor, raising an actor who was down as well since the healing is applied as a lasting effect. Without an actor named it heals whoever the task is running on. Nothing happens if the named actor is not present in the zone.

required.name: floats[0]
required.description: How much health to restore. A value of 0 is treated as a full heal. Supplying no number at all instead heals the whole party.

optional.name: strings[0]
optional.description: The ID of the actor to heal; it must be present in the zone. If omitted or empty, the actor the task is running on is healed instead.

uses.description: Fully restores health and magic to every member of the player's party and brings down members back to their feet. It does not clear the maximum-health penalty a knockout leaves behind, and it does not cure fatigue, so party members stay tired. Any spell they were charging or casting is cancelled.

tasks.officialDescription: Heals triggering actor, or actor 'sValue', by fValue.

tasks.name: healparty

uses.description: Fully restores health and magic to every member of the player's party and brings down members back to their feet, clearing any lingering status effects. It does not clear the maximum-health penalty a knockout leaves behind, and it does not cure fatigue, so party members stay tired. Any spell they were charging or casting is cancelled.

tasks.officialDescription: Heals playerParty, without restoring HPMax lost from being KO'd.

tasks.name: fullrestore

uses.description: Completely restores every member of the player's party: health, magic, status effects, the maximum-health penalty left by knockouts, and fatigue are all cleared, and down members are brought back to their feet. This is the full night's-rest restoration rather than a battlefield patch-up. Any spell they were charging or casting is cancelled.

tasks.officialDescription: Fully heals playerParty, including HPMax lost from being KO'd.

tasks.name: revive

uses.description: Brings a downed actor back to its feet with a chosen amount of health, clearing burning, poison and the dying state along with it. Without an actor named it revives whoever the task is running on, and nothing happens if that actor is missing, already up, truly dead, or of a kind that cannot be revived. It can also cure the actor's lingering ailments in the same step.

optional.name: strings[0]
optional.description: The ID of the actor to revive; it must be present in the zone. If omitted or empty, the actor the task is running on is revived instead.

optional.name: floats[0]
optional.description: How much health the actor comes back with. Defaults to 0, which is treated as a full heal.

optional.name: bools[0]
optional.description: When true, all of the actor's harmful status effects and decay are also removed. Defaults to false, which only clears burning, poison and dying.

tasks.officialDescription: Revives triggering actor, or actor 'sValue', by fValue.

tasks.name: fx

uses.description: Plays a visual effect at a fixed spot on the screen rather than anywhere in the world, so it stays put as the camera moves. The coordinates are read as screen pixels from the top-left of the window, not as map tiles. Use this for flashes, sparkles and overlays that belong to the interface rather than to a place in the world.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The ID of the visual effect to play. Nothing appears if no effect by that name is defined.

required.name: bools[0]
required.description: Must be true: it is what switches the coordinates from map tiles to screen pixels. Leaving it out or setting it false plays the effect at the tile instead.

required.name: tileCoords[0]
required.description: The screen position to play the effect at, in pixels from the top-left of the window. Its x must not be -1, or the effect plays at the camera instead.

optional.name: strings[2]
optional.description: The colour to tint the effect, by name. Defaults to white. Because it sits after the actor slot, a taskString must leave that slot empty as a placeholder to reach it.

uses.description: Plays a visual effect that travels from one tile to another, which is how a projectile, a spray or a beam between two points is drawn. The effect starts at the first tile and moves toward the second. Both tiles are needed, and the second can only be supplied inside a taskString since a trigger effect carries just one coordinate.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The ID of the visual effect to play. Nothing appears if no effect by that name is defined.

required.name: tileCoords[0]
required.description: The tile the effect starts at. Its x must not be -1, or the effect plays at the camera instead.

required.name: tileCoords[1]
required.description: The tile the effect travels toward. Its x must not be -1, or the effect simply plays at the starting tile. A second coordinate can only be given inside a taskString.

optional.name: strings[2]
optional.description: The colour to tint the effect, by name. Defaults to white. Because it sits after the actor slot, a taskString must leave that slot empty as a placeholder to reach it.

uses.description: Plays a visual effect centred on a named actor, wherever that actor happens to be standing. This is the way to put a glow, a puff or a status flourish on a specific character without knowing their position. Nothing happens if no actor with that ID is present in the zone.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The ID of the visual effect to play. Nothing appears if no effect by that name is defined.

required.name: strings[1]
required.description: The ID of the actor to centre the effect on; it must be present in the zone. Leaving it empty plays the effect at a tile or the camera instead.

optional.name: strings[2]
optional.description: The colour to tint the effect, by name. Defaults to white.

uses.description: Plays a visual effect on a single tile of the map, staying anchored to that spot in the world as the camera moves. This is the everyday form for explosions, sparkles and impacts at a known place. If the effect is one that follows an actor, it latches onto whoever is standing on that tile.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The ID of the visual effect to play. Nothing appears if no effect by that name is defined.

required.name: tileCoords[0]
required.description: The tile to play the effect on. Its x must not be -1, or the effect plays at the camera instead.

optional.name: strings[2]
optional.description: The colour to tint the effect, by name. Defaults to white. Because it sits after the actor slot, a taskString must leave that slot empty as a placeholder to reach it.

uses.description: Plays a visual effect at whatever the camera is currently looking at, which is the fallback when neither an actor nor a tile is given. It lands in the middle of the view at the moment the task runs and then stays put in the world. Use it for effects that should simply be visible without belonging anywhere in particular.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The ID of the visual effect to play. Nothing appears if no effect by that name is defined.

optional.name: strings[2]
optional.description: The colour to tint the effect, by name. Defaults to white. Because it sits after the actor slot, a taskString must leave that slot empty as a placeholder to reach it.

tasks.officialDescription: Plays fx 'sValue' at X,Y. 'sValue2' uses that actor's position instead. If nothing specified, plays fx at camera position. If b1, X,Y is screen position. If used in a task, string 3 sets fx color and a second TC specifies fx target.

tasks.name: sfx

uses.description: Plays a sound effect once at full volume with no position, so it is heard equally wherever the player is. Naming a visual effect that has no particles of its own instead plays whatever sound that effect carries, at its own volume and pitch. Nothing happens if the name matches neither a sound nor such an effect, or if sound is switched off.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The name of the sound to play. It may also be the name of a soundtrack-only visual effect, in which case that effect's sound, volume and pitch are used.

tasks.officialDescription: Play unlooped sound FX 'sValue' at volume 1, pitch 0.

tasks.name: fxOnTalker

uses.description: Plays a visual effect centred on whoever the player is currently talking to, which is how a conversation punctuates a line with a puff of smoke or a flash. The effect is always drawn in white. Nothing happens if no conversation is in progress or the other party is not present in the zone.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The ID of the visual effect to play. Nothing appears if no effect by that name is defined.

tasks.officialDescription: Plays fx 'sValue' at the X,Y of the currentActorTalkingTo.

tasks.name: fxOnParty

uses.description: Plays the same visual effect on every member of the player's party at once, one copy centred on each of them. This is the way to show a party-wide blessing, cure or transformation. The effects are always drawn in white.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The ID of the visual effect to play on each party member. Nothing appears if no effect by that name is defined.

tasks.officialDescription: Plays fx 'sValue' at the X,Y of each partyActor.

tasks.name: damageNumber

uses.description: Floats a line of text upward above an actor or a tile, the same way damage and healing numbers appear in combat. It lasts about two seconds and is nudged aside so it does not overlap other floating numbers already on screen. Nothing appears at all if the player has floating numbers switched off. Supplying four or more numbers sets the lifetime with the first and the colour with the next three.

required.name: floats[0]
required.description: Extra seconds added to the number's two-second lifetime. Defaults to none.

required.name: floats[1]
required.description: The red channel of the number's colour, from 0 to 255.

required.name: floats[2]
required.description: The green channel of the number's colour, from 0 to 255.

required.name: floats[3]
required.description: The blue channel of the number's colour, from 0 to 255.

optional.name: strings[0]
optional.description: The text to float above the target. Defaults to empty, which shows a blank number. When the second flag is set this is read as a global variable name instead of as the text itself.

optional.name: strings[1]
optional.description: The ID of the actor to float the number above. Leaving it empty puts it above the player. It may instead be written as the actor ID, a comma and a colour name together, which is the only way to set a colour through a trigger effect.

optional.name: bools[0]
optional.description: When true the number sits still instead of drifting upward. Defaults to false.

optional.name: bools[1]
optional.description: When true the first string is read as the name of a global variable and that variable's contents are displayed; an unset variable shows nothing. Defaults to false.

optional.name: tileCoords[0]
optional.description: The tile to float the number above, overriding the target actor's position. If omitted it defaults to (-1,-1) and the actor's own tile is used; with no actor either, nothing is shown.

tasks.name: animate

uses.description: Plays a named animation on an actor, replacing whatever it was doing. Optionally the actor is also held busy for a while, which stops it acting or being acted on until the animation has had time to play, and clears any stun it was under. Nothing happens if the animation does not exist or there is no actor to play it on.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The ID of the animation to play. An unknown name leaves the actor as it was.

required.name: strings[1]
required.description: The ID of the actor to animate; it must be present in the zone. Leave it empty to animate the actor the task is running on, but the slot itself must still be supplied.

optional.name: floats[0]
optional.description: How many seconds to hold the actor busy while the animation plays, which also clears any stun on it. Defaults to none, letting the actor carry on immediately.

tasks.officialDescription: Animates triggering actor (or actor 'sValue2') with animation 'sValue'. Sets busyTimer to fValue if specified.

tasks.name: textOverlay

uses.description: Puts a line of text across the middle of the screen, over everything else, with an optional dark panel behind it — the caption card used for chapter titles and scene-setting lines. It stays up until something replaces or clears it, and giving neither text nor a panel takes it back down. The text is laid out with the game's dynamic text, so it can carry icons and substitutions.

optional.name: strings[0]
optional.description: The text to show. Defaults to empty, which hides the overlay unless a panel opacity is given.

optional.name: floats[0]
