optional.description: How opaque the panel behind the text is, from 0 for none to 255 for solid black. Defaults to 0.

optional.name: bools[0]
optional.description: When true the text is not centred horizontally and starts at the left edge instead. Defaults to false.

optional.name: bools[1]
optional.description: When true the text is not centred vertically and sits at the top instead. Defaults to false. Supplying it requires the first flag to be supplied as well.

optional.name: tileCoords[0]
optional.description: Its x shifts the text sideways in screen pixels, scaled by the interface zoom; -1 counts as no shift. Its y is ignored entirely by this form, so use the tweened or dynamic form to move the text vertically.

tasks.officialDescription: Sets sValue as overlaid text. If sValue = '', clears overlaid text. fValue (0-255) is the alpha of the black behind the overlay. xValue & yValue offset the text. If bValue1, centers text Xpos. Bvalue2, Ypos.

tasks.name: textOverlay_tween

uses.description: Puts a line of text across the screen and slides it up into place from the bottom edge, the way a title card animates in. The slide only happens when there is text, no panel behind it, and a downward offset was given; otherwise it simply appears. Clearing it with no text and no panel slides the overlay back off the bottom of the screen.

optional.name: strings[0]
optional.description: The text to show. Defaults to empty, which slides the overlay back off screen unless a panel opacity is given.

optional.name: floats[0]
optional.description: How opaque the panel behind the text is, from 0 for none to 255 for solid black. Defaults to 0; anything above 0 suppresses the slide-in.

optional.name: tileCoords[0]
optional.description: Its x shifts the text sideways in screen pixels, scaled by the interface zoom, and its y shifts it downward; -1 in either counts as no shift. A downward shift is what triggers the slide-in animation.

tasks.officialDescription: Tweens in sValue as overlaid text. If sValue = '', tweens out. fValue (0-255) is the alpha of the black behind the overlay. xValue & yValue offset the text.

tasks.name: textOverlay_dynamic

uses.description: Puts a line of text across the screen and reveals it letter by letter with a soft click for each character, the way spoken narration is typed out. Apart from the reveal it behaves like the plain overlay: it stays up until something replaces or clears it, and giving neither text nor a panel takes it back down. The text is laid out with the game's dynamic text, so it can carry icons and substitutions.

optional.name: strings[0]
optional.description: The text to reveal. Defaults to empty, which hides the overlay unless a panel opacity is given.

optional.name: floats[0]
optional.description: How opaque the panel behind the text is, from 0 for none to 255 for solid black. Defaults to 0.

optional.name: bools[0]
optional.description: When true the text is not centred horizontally and starts at the left edge instead. Defaults to false.

optional.name: bools[1]
optional.description: When true the text is not centred vertically and sits at the top instead. Defaults to false. Supplying it requires the first flag to be supplied as well.

optional.name: tileCoords[0]
optional.description: Its x shifts the text sideways in screen pixels, scaled by the interface zoom, and its y shifts it downward; -1 in either counts as no shift.

tasks.officialDescription: Same as 'textOverlay', except reveals text dynamically.

tasks.name: pointCameraAt

uses.description: Swings the camera onto a named actor and keeps following them as they move. Any existing lock on the camera is released first, so this always takes effect. The camera can optionally be pinned in place for the length of the current interaction lock, which is how a cutscene stops the player wresting it back.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The ID of the actor to follow; it must be present in the zone. If no such actor exists the camera falls back to the actor the task is running on.

optional.name: bools[0]
optional.description: When true the camera is pinned for as long as the player is locked out of interacting, so nothing else can move it in the meantime. Defaults to false.

optional.name: bools[1]
optional.description: When true the camera behaves as though it were under a roof, hiding roofs above it and blacking out the tiles around an enclosed space. Defaults to false. Supplying it requires the first flag to be supplied as well.

uses.description: Swings the camera onto a fixed tile and leaves it there instead of following anyone. Fog of war around that tile is revealed for the actor the task is running on, so the camera does not look at unexplored blackness. Any existing lock on the camera is released first, and the pan speed can be changed for this move.

required.name: tileCoords[0]
required.description: The tile to look at. Its x must not be -1, or the camera falls back to following an actor instead.

optional.name: floats[0]
optional.description: How fast the camera travels to the new spot; larger is faster. Defaults to 0, which leaves the current speed alone.

optional.name: bools[0]
optional.description: When true the camera is pinned for as long as the player is locked out of interacting, so nothing else can move it in the meantime. Defaults to false.

optional.name: bools[1]
optional.description: When true the camera behaves as though it were under a roof, hiding roofs above it and blacking out the tiles around an enclosed space. Defaults to false. Supplying it requires the first flag to be supplied as well.

uses.description: Swings the camera onto the actor the task is running on and keeps following them, which is the default when neither a tile nor an actor ID is given. With no contextual actor either, it follows whichever actor is currently taking its turn instead. Any existing lock on the camera is released first.

optional.name: bools[0]
optional.description: When true the camera is pinned for as long as the player is locked out of interacting, so nothing else can move it in the meantime. Defaults to false.

optional.name: bools[1]
optional.description: When true the camera behaves as though it were under a roof, hiding roofs above it and blacking out the tiles around an enclosed space. Defaults to false. Supplying it requires the first flag to be supplied as well.

tasks.officialDescription: Points camera at X,Y, or actor.ID if X,Y is unspecified. fValue alters speed if specified. bValue1 sets cameraCantBeChangedTimer to delay_preventInteraction. If bValue2, camera goes under roofs.

tasks.name: lockCameraAt

uses.description: Swings the camera onto a fixed tile and then bolts it there, so nothing else can move it until another camera task explicitly releases it. Fog of war around the tile is revealed for the actor the task is running on, so the camera does not look at unexplored blackness. Use it for a scripted shot that must hold still.

required.name: tileCoords[0]
required.description: The tile to look at and lock onto. Its x must not be -1, or the camera locks onto an actor instead.

optional.name: floats[0]
optional.description: How fast the camera travels to the new spot; larger is faster. Defaults to 0, which leaves the current speed alone.

optional.name: bools[0]
optional.description: When true the camera behaves as though it were under a roof, hiding roofs above it and blacking out the tiles around an enclosed space. Defaults to false.

uses.description: Swings the camera onto the actor the task is running on and then bolts it in place, so nothing else can move it until another camera task explicitly releases it. With no contextual actor it locks onto whichever actor is currently taking its turn instead. Note that the camera stops following that actor once the lock is applied, holding the spot rather than the character.

optional.name: bools[0]
optional.description: When true the camera behaves as though it were under a roof, hiding roofs above it and blacking out the tiles around an enclosed space. Defaults to false.

tasks.officialDescription: Points camera at X,Y, or actor.ID if X,Y is unspecified. fValue alters speed if specified. Locks camera indefinitely. If bValue1, camera goes under roofs.

tasks.name: scaleCameraTo

uses.description: Zooms the camera to a new magnification gradually, sliding from the current zoom to the target at a chosen rate. Use it for a slow push-in or pull-back during a scene. The zoom keeps drifting on its own frame by frame until it arrives.

required.name: tileCoords[0]
required.description: Its x sets how fast the zoom slides, at a tenth of the number given per second. It must be above 0, or the zoom snaps instantly instead.

optional.name: floats[0]
optional.description: The zoom level to end up at, where 1 is normal size and larger values magnify. Defaults to 0, which shrinks the view to nothing.

uses.description: Sets the camera's magnification immediately, with no sliding. Use it to establish a zoom before a scene starts rather than to animate one. A value of 1 is the normal view and larger values magnify.

optional.name: floats[0]
optional.description: The zoom level to snap to, where 1 is normal size and larger values magnify. Defaults to 0, which shrinks the view to nothing.

tasks.officialDescription: Sets camera target scale to fValue, scaling at speed X/10. If speed=0 or less, sets scale instantly.

tasks.name: setRoofDrawNoMatterWhat

uses.description: Forces roofs to be drawn even when the camera is under one, or lets them hide again. Normally a roof over the camera is removed so the player can see inside; turning this on keeps it painted, which is what you want when a scene should be viewed from outside a building. The tile-blackening that goes with being indoors is also switched off while it is on.

optional.name: bools[0]
optional.description: True keeps roofs drawn no matter what; false restores the normal behaviour of hiding a roof the camera is under. Defaults to false.

tasks.officialDescription: Sets camera.drawRoofsNoMatterWhat to bValue1.

tasks.name: cancelIfEnemiesPresent

uses.description: Stops the rest of the trigger it belongs to from running if any hostile actor is alive in the zone, optionally only counting enemies of a particular kind or within a given distance. When it cancels, the trigger is not marked as done, so it can fire again later — which is how a scripted scene waits until a fight is over. Enemies that are queued to spawn this frame count as present too.

optional.name: strings[0]
optional.description: Only count enemies of this kind. Defaults to empty, which counts every hostile actor.

optional.name: floats[0]
optional.description: Only count enemies closer than this many tiles from the reference point. Defaults to 0, which counts hostile actors anywhere in the zone.

optional.name: tileCoords[0]
optional.description: The tile distances are measured from. If omitted it falls back to the tile of the actor the task is running on, and with no such actor to the off-map tile (-1,-1).

tasks.officialDescription: Cancels further effects if any non-incapped hostiles are within 'fValue' of triggering actor or X,Y. If fValue=0, distance is infinite. If sValue1 specified, only checks actors with that actorTypeID.

tasks.name: cancelIfEnemiesNotPresent

uses.description: Stops the rest of the trigger it belongs to from running unless at least one hostile actor is alive in the zone, optionally only counting enemies within a given distance. When it cancels, the trigger is not marked as done, so it can fire again later — which is how a scene waits for a fight to start. Enemies that are queued to spawn this frame count as present too.

optional.name: floats[0]
optional.description: Only count enemies closer than this many tiles from the reference point. Defaults to 0, which counts hostile actors anywhere in the zone.

optional.name: tileCoords[0]
optional.description: The tile distances are measured from. If omitted it falls back to the tile of the actor the task is running on, and with no such actor to the off-map tile (-1,-1).

tasks.officialDescription: Cancels further effects if no non-incapped hostiles are within 'fValue' of triggering actor or X,Y. If fValue=0, distance is infinite.

tasks.name: cancelIfItemPresent

uses.description: Stops the rest of the trigger it belongs to from running if a named item is lying on a particular tile. When no tile is given it instead sweeps the whole area of the trigger that fired it, cancelling if the item is found anywhere inside, and then also checks the top-left corner of the map. When it cancels, the trigger is not marked as done, so it can fire again once the item is gone.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The ID of the item type to look for.

optional.name: tileCoords[0]
optional.description: The tile to check. If omitted it defaults to (-1,-1), which switches on the sweep of the trigger's own area and then checks the map's top-left tile.

tasks.officialDescription: Cancels further effects if item 'sValue' is found at X,Y. If X = -1, checks trigger area for the item.

tasks.name: cancelIfItemNotPresent

uses.description: Stops the rest of the trigger it belongs to from running unless a named item is lying on a particular tile. When no tile is given it first sweeps the whole area of the trigger that fired it and lets the trigger continue if the item is found anywhere inside; failing that it checks the map's top-left tile. When it cancels, the trigger is not marked as done, so it can fire again once the item appears.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The ID of the item type to look for.

optional.name: tileCoords[0]
optional.description: The tile to check. If omitted it defaults to (-1,-1), which switches on the sweep of the trigger's own area and then falls back to the map's top-left tile.

tasks.officialDescription: Cancels further effects if item 'sValue' is not found at X,Y. If X = -1, checks trigger area for the item.

tasks.name: cancelIf

uses.description: Works out a formula and, if it comes out positive, stops the rest of the trigger it belongs to from running. This is the general-purpose guard for putting a condition partway down a list of effects. When it cancels, the trigger is not marked as done, so it can fire again later once the condition changes.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The formula to test. The trigger is cancelled when it comes out above zero. It is evaluated with the actor the task is running on as both caster and target.

optional.name: floats[0]
optional.description: A number handed to the formula as its x value, for conditions that need a threshold or an amount. Defaults to 0.

optional.name: bools[0]
optional.description: When true the trigger is only cancelled if the formula lands strictly between zero and one, so a result of one or more lets it continue. Defaults to false.

optional.name: tileCoords[0]
optional.description: A tile handed to the formula as its target tile, for conditions that ask about a place. If omitted it defaults to the off-map tile (-1,-1).

tasks.officialDescription: Cancels further effects if sValue calculates true (> 0). If bValue, cancels when sValue calcs as false (less or = 0)

tasks.name: facingRot

uses.description: Turns an actor to face a given direction, in degrees. Use it to have a character look toward something before a line of dialog or an action. Nothing happens if there is no actor to turn.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The ID of the actor to turn; it must be present in the zone. Leave it empty to turn the actor the task is running on, but the slot itself must still be supplied.

required.name: floats[0]
required.description: The direction to face, in degrees. Without it nothing happens at all.

tasks.officialDescription: Sets triggering actor (or actor 'sValue' if specified) to fValue rot.

tasks.name: facingRotParty

uses.description: Turns every member of the player's party to face the same direction, in degrees. Use it to line the party up before a scripted scene or a group shot. Every member turns at once, with no animation.

required.name: floats[0]
required.description: The direction all party members face, in degrees.

tasks.officialDescription: Sets party actors to fValue rot.

tasks.name: playSong

uses.description: Starts a piece of music playing on a loop, replacing whatever was playing. By default it fades in after a couple of seconds; the same song already playing simply has its volume and pitch adjusted rather than restarting. Giving no song at all fades the music out to silence, which is how a scene goes quiet.

optional.name: strings[0]
optional.description: The name of the music track to play, looked up among the game's and mods' music files. The special values "travel" and "combat" instead play the current zone's own configured wandering or fighting music at that zone's own volume and pitch, ignoring everything else you set here. Leaving it out or empty fades the music to silence.

optional.name: floats[0]
optional.description: Pitch adjustment, capped at 1. Defaults to 0, the track's natural pitch.

optional.name: bools[0]
optional.description: When true the track keeps playing across zone changes instead of being replaced by the new zone's own music. Defaults to false. It has no effect when playing a zone's configured music.

optional.name: bools[1]
optional.description: When true the track starts instantly at full volume with no lead-in or fade. Defaults to false. Supplying it requires the first flag to be supplied as well.

optional.name: tileCoords[0]
optional.description: Its x is the volume as a percentage, defaulting to full when left at -1; its y is how many extra seconds to wait before the track starts, on top of the usual two-second lead-in, defaulting to none. Neither applies when playing a zone's configured music.

tasks.officialDescription: Plays 'sValue' song at 'fValue' pitch. If sValue = 'travelSong' or 'combatSong', uses Zone defaults instead. If X is set, volume = X/100. If Y set, delay = Y. bValue1 prevents the song from being changed to travelSong. To stop music immediately, set volume to 0. If bValue2, song starts at full volume instead of fading in.

tasks.name: playNearestLocationSong

uses.description: Plays the music belonging to whichever town, port or other location in the current zone is nearest the player. This is how sailing near a settlement picks up that settlement's theme without naming it. Nothing happens if there is no player actor, no location in the zone, or that location has no music of its own.

tasks.officialDescription: Plays the externalSong of the location in the current zone that is closest to the player.

tasks.name: setZoneSongs

uses.description: Changes which music the current zone uses for wandering around and for fighting, along with its volume and pitch, and starts the appropriate one playing right away. The change sticks with the zone, so it is still in force the next time music is picked up after combat or on returning. Each of the two songs is only touched if you actually give one, unless you explicitly ask to clear it.

optional.name: strings[0]
optional.description: The zone's new wandering music. Leaving it empty leaves the existing wandering music alone unless the first flag is set, in which case the zone is left silent while wandering.

optional.name: strings[1]
optional.description: The zone's new fighting music. Leaving it empty leaves the existing fighting music alone unless the second flag is set, in which case the zone is left silent in combat.

optional.name: floats[0]
optional.description: Pitch adjustment applied to whichever songs are being set. Defaults to 0, their natural pitch.

optional.name: bools[0]
optional.description: When true the wandering music is set even to an empty value, which clears it. Defaults to false.

optional.name: bools[1]
optional.description: When true the fighting music is set even to an empty value, which clears it. Defaults to false. Supplying it requires the first flag to be supplied as well.

optional.name: tileCoords[0]
optional.description: Its x is the volume as a percentage for whichever songs are being set, defaulting to full when left at -1; its y is how many seconds the fighting music waits before starting, applied only when the fighting music is being set and only when it is 0 or more.

tasks.officialDescription: Sets zone travel song to 'sValue' &combat song to sValue2 at 'fValue' pitch. If X is set, volume = X/100. Y = combatSongDelay. If bValue1, force assign travelSong even if blank. Same for bValue2 & combat.

tasks.name: removeItem

uses.description: Destroys copies of a named item lying on a chosen tile of the map. Every matching item on that tile goes, however many there are. It can also aim at a numbered travel point instead of a raw tile, which is useful when the item sits at a doorway whose coordinates you do not know.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The ID of the item type to destroy.

required.name: tileCoords[0]
required.description: The tile to clear the item from. Its x must not be -1, or the task takes items out of an inventory instead. When the travel-point flag is set, its x is a travel-point number and its y a travel-point set number instead of map coordinates.

optional.name: strings[1]
optional.description: The name of a global variable holding the item ID to destroy, used in place of the first string when it is not empty. This lets the item be chosen at runtime.

optional.name: bools[0]
optional.description: When true the coordinates are read as a travel-point number and set rather than as a map tile. Defaults to false. Note that when two flags are supplied — which a trigger effect always does — it is the second flag that is read and the first is ignored, because an unused slot is inserted in front.

uses.description: Takes a number of copies of a named item out of the inventory of the actor the task is running on, hunting further afield if they do not have it. If that actor is in the player's party, every other party member is searched next; failing that the item is taken from the party's stash, and failing that from whatever the player is holding by hand. The item is destroyed rather than dropped.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The ID of the item type to take.

optional.name: strings[1]
optional.description: The name of a global variable holding the item ID to take, used in place of the first string when it is not empty. This lets the item be chosen at runtime.

optional.name: floats[0]
optional.description: How many copies to take. Defaults to 1, and 0 is also treated as 1.

tasks.officialDescription: Deletes 'sValue' item at X,Y. If unspecified, removes 'fValue' num of the item from triggering actor's inventory. if sValue2 is used, remove itemID of globalVar[sValue2]. If bValue2, XY specifies a travelpoint.

tasks.name: removeActorItem

uses.description: Destroys one named item from a named actor's inventory, unequipping it first so any bonuses it was granting are removed along with it. If the item was a held weapon, anything slotted into it stops applying too and the actor's charging action may be cancelled. Nothing happens if the actor is not present or does not carry the item.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The ID of the actor to take the item from; it must be present in the zone.

required.name: strings[1]
required.description: The ID of the item type to take. Only the first matching item found in the inventory is removed.

tasks.officialDescription: Removes item 'sValue2' from actor 'sValue'.

tasks.name: removeItemOfValue

uses.description: Destroys the valuable items lying on a single tile, keeping anything cheaper than the threshold you set. With no threshold given it simply clears everything off the tile. This is the way to strip loot from a spot without naming each item.

optional.name: floats[0]
optional.description: The minimum item value to destroy; anything worth at least this much goes. Defaults to -1, which clears the tile entirely. A value of 0 removes nothing at all.

optional.name: tileCoords[0]
optional.description: The tile to clear. If omitted it defaults to (-1,-1), which is out of bounds.

tasks.officialDescription: Deletes items at X,Y of value fValue or greater.

tasks.name: removeEmptyItem

uses.description: Sweeps the whole zone and destroys every container item that has nothing inside it — empty chests, crates, barrels and the like. Containers that still hold something are left alone. It can be narrowed to one kind of container, or left to clear every empty one in the zone.

optional.name: strings[0]
optional.description: Only destroy empty containers of this item type. Defaults to empty, which clears every empty container in the zone.

tasks.officialDescription: Removes all containers from the current zone that have the ID of 'sValue' and have no items inside of them.

tasks.name: removeItemsNearPlayerActor

uses.description: Destroys every copy of a named item lying within a given distance of the player, sweeping the whole zone to find them. Use it to tidy up scattered props once a scene is over. With no distance given it clears only the tile the player is standing on.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The ID of the item type to destroy.

optional.name: strings[1]
optional.description: The name of a global variable holding the item ID to destroy, used in place of the first string when it is not empty. This lets the item be chosen at runtime.

optional.name: floats[0]
optional.description: How far from the player, in tiles, to sweep. Defaults to 0, which clears only the player's own tile.

tasks.officialDescription: Deletes items of type sValue1 within fValue tiles of player Actor.

tasks.name: removeAllItems

uses.description: Destroys everything lying on a single tile, whatever it is. Nothing is spared, so this wipes the tile clean rather than picking out one kind of item. Use it to clear a spot before dropping something new there.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: Unused in this branch but must be provided as a placeholder; the whole tile is cleared regardless of what is named here.

required.name: tileCoords[0]
required.description: The tile to wipe clean. It must not be (-1,-1), or the task sweeps the whole zone for a named item instead.

uses.description: Sweeps the entire zone and destroys every copy of a named item wherever it lies. This is the blunt way to make a prop disappear from a map without knowing where the copies are. It only removes the item type you name, leaving everything else in place.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The ID of the item type to destroy everywhere in the zone.

optional.name: strings[1]
optional.description: The name of a global variable holding the item ID to destroy, used in place of the first string when it is not empty. This lets the item be chosen at runtime.

tasks.officialDescription: Deletes 'sValue' item from zone. Uses gVar if 'sValue2' specified. Can also remove all at XY if no sValue given.

tasks.name: removeAllItemsOfValue

uses.description: Sweeps the whole zone and destroys every item worth at least a given amount, leaving cheaper things where they lie. Use it to strip a map of loot without naming each item. Supplying no threshold makes it do nothing at all.

optional.name: floats[0]
optional.description: The minimum item value to destroy; anything worth at least this much goes. Defaults to 0, which removes nothing.

tasks.officialDescription: Deletes items from zone of value fValue or greater.

tasks.name: removeHeldItems

uses.description: Destroys whatever the player is currently carrying by hand — the items picked up with the cursor and not yet put anywhere. Their hands end up empty. Use it before a scene where the player must not be holding anything.

tasks.officialDescription: Deletes all held items.

tasks.name: addItem

uses.description: Gives a new item to a named actor, putting it into their inventory and equipping it if there is a suitable slot free. Actors of a kind that cannot carry anything are skipped. Nothing happens if the item type does not exist or the named actor is not present in the zone.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The ID of the item type to create. It must be a real item type or nothing happens.

required.name: strings[1]
required.description: The ID of the actor to give the item to; it must be present in the zone. Leaving it empty gives the item to the actor the task is running on instead.

optional.name: floats[0]
optional.description: How many copies to create. Defaults to 1, and 0 is also treated as 1.

uses.description: Creates a new item and drops it onto a chosen tile of the map. Stackable items merge with a matching pile already there. If the tile has no room the item is discarded, unless you insist it be squeezed in anyway.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The ID of the item type to create. It must be a real item type or nothing happens.

required.name: tileCoords[0]
required.description: The tile to drop the item on. Its x must not be -1, or the item goes to an actor or a store instead.

optional.name: floats[0]
optional.description: How many copies to create. Defaults to 1, and 0 is also treated as 1.

optional.name: bools[0]
optional.description: When true the item is forced onto the tile even if there is no room for it, and it is placed on top of anything already there. Defaults to false, which drops the item only if it fits.

uses.description: Creates a new item and gives it to the actor the task is running on, or stows it away if there is nobody to give it to. A player-controlled actor receiving trade goods gets them in the cargo hold instead of their pack; otherwise the item is equipped or carried, and anything it displaces falls to the ground with a sound. With no contextual actor the item goes straight into the cargo hold if it is a trade good, or into the party's stash if not.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The ID of the item type to create. It must be a real item type or nothing happens.

optional.name: floats[0]
optional.description: How many copies the recipient should end up with, rather than how many to add: copies the actor already carries are subtracted, so asking for 3 when they hold 2 adds only the difference. Defaults to 1, and 0 is also treated as 1. This topping-up only applies when the item goes to an actor's own inventory.

tasks.officialDescription: Adds 'fValue' num of item 'sValue' ID to X,Y (or sValue2 actor or triggering actor inventory if unspecified). If bValue1, force item to fit.

tasks.name: addItemToContainer

uses.description: Creates a new item and puts it inside a container — a chest, crate or barrel — sitting on a chosen tile. The first container on the tile with room for it receives the item, and the search can be narrowed to containers of a particular kind. Nothing happens if the item type does not exist, no container is named correctly, or no container on the tile has space.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The ID of the item type to create and put inside. It must be a real item type or nothing happens.

optional.name: strings[1]
optional.description: Only fill a container of this item type. It must also be a real item type, or the task does nothing at all. Defaults to empty, which uses the first container on the tile with room.

optional.name: floats[0]
optional.description: How many copies to create. Defaults to 1, and 0 is also treated as 1.

optional.name: tileCoords[0]
optional.description: The tile whose container is filled. If omitted it defaults to (-1,-1), which is pulled back inside the map and so targets the top-left corner.

tasks.officialDescription: Adds 'fValue' quantity of 'sValue' itemType ID to the first container at X,Y that the item can fit into. If 'sValue2' is specified, that is the itemType ID the container must be. If fValue is 0, it acts as 1.

tasks.name: spawnItem

uses.description: Creates a new item and drops it onto a chosen tile, optionally playing a visual effect where it lands. Stackable items merge with a matching pile already there, and if the tile has no room the item is discarded unless you insist it be squeezed in. The destination can also be given as a numbered travel point rather than raw coordinates.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The ID of the item type to create. If it is not a known item type, it is instead read as the name of a global variable whose contents must name one; failing that, nothing happens.

required.name: tileCoords[0]
required.description: The tile to drop the item on. Its x must not be -1, or the item lands somewhere random instead. When the travel-point flag is set, its x is a travel-point number and its y a travel-point set number.

optional.name: strings[1]
optional.description: A visual effect played in white where the item lands. Defaults to none.

optional.name: floats[0]
optional.description: How many copies to create. Defaults to 1, and 0 is also treated as 1.

optional.name: bools[0]
optional.description: When true the item is forced onto the tile even if there is no room for it. Defaults to false, which drops the item only if it fits.

optional.name: bools[1]
optional.description: When true the coordinates are read as a travel-point number and set rather than as a map tile. Defaults to false. Supplying it requires the first flag to be supplied as well.

uses.description: Creates a new item and drops it on a random tile inside the area of the trigger that fired this task, retrying until it finds somewhere the item fits. This scatters loot or props over a region without naming a spot. A visual effect can be played where it lands.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The ID of the item type to create. If it is not a known item type, it is instead read as the name of a global variable whose contents must name one; failing that, nothing happens.

optional.name: strings[1]
optional.description: A visual effect played in white where the item lands. Defaults to none.

optional.name: floats[0]
optional.description: How many copies to create. Defaults to 1, and 0 is also treated as 1.

optional.name: bools[0]
optional.description: When true the item is forced onto the chosen tile even if there is no room for it. Defaults to false.

tasks.officialDescription: Adds 'fValue' num of item 'sValue' ID to X,Y (or random spot in trigger area if unspecified) and plays 'sValue2' fx if specified. If sValue is not an item type, checks globalVar for an ID. If bValue1, force item to fit. If bValue2, XY refers to a travelpoint (#X, set Y).

tasks.name: moveItems

uses.description: Sweeps every tile in the area of the trigger that fired this task, picks up the items that match your filters, and piles them all onto one destination tile. The pile is forced on regardless of how crowded the tile is. With no filters given it moves everything in the area.

required.name: tileCoords[0]
required.description: The tile everything is moved to. Its x must not be -1, or the task does nothing at all.

optional.name: strings[0]
optional.description: Only move items of this type. Defaults to empty, which moves items of every type.

optional.name: strings[1]
optional.description: Only move items carrying this special property, given by name or by its number. Defaults to empty, which ignores special properties.

optional.name: bools[0]
optional.description: When true only items the player could pick up by hand are moved, leaving fixed scenery in place. Defaults to false.

tasks.officialDescription: Moves items from topLeft of trigger area to X,Y.

tasks.name: moveItemsToActor

uses.description: Hands everything lying on a tile to a named actor, equipping what fits and dropping the rest at that actor's feet, then clears the tile. Use it to have a character scoop up a cache. Nothing happens if the actor is not present or is of a kind that cannot carry anything.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The ID of the actor to give the items to; it must be present in the zone and able to carry things.

optional.name: tileCoords[0]
optional.description: The tile to empty. If omitted it defaults to (-1,-1), which is pulled back inside the map and so empties the top-left corner.

tasks.officialDescription: Moves items from X,Y to actor 'sValue'.

tasks.name: setSpecialInfoTC

uses.description: Points the items on a tile at another tile, setting the linked location that items such as switches, teleport pads and moving blocks use to know where they act. Only items of a kind that can carry such a link are affected, and they can be narrowed down by item type or by a special property. The destination is given as a comma-separated pair of coordinates.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: Only affect items of this type. Leave it empty to affect every linkable item on the tile. When the property-filter flag is set this is read as a special property name or number instead.

required.name: strings[1]
required.description: The tile to point the items at, written as two whole numbers separated by a comma, such as "12,8". Because it contains a comma it cannot be written inside a taskString, so this form has to be set up as a trigger effect.

required.name: tileCoords[0]
required.description: The tile whose items are re-pointed. Its x must not be -1, or the task does nothing at all.

optional.name: bools[0]
optional.description: When true the destination is added to each item's existing link as an offset rather than replacing it. Defaults to false.

optional.name: bools[1]
optional.description: When true the first string is read as a special property to filter by rather than as an item type. Defaults to false. Supplying it requires the first flag to be supplied as well.

uses.description: Points the items on a tile at another tile, setting the linked location that items such as switches, teleport pads and moving blocks use to know where they act. Only items of a kind that can carry such a link are affected, and they can be narrowed down by item type or by a special property. The destination is given as a pair of numbers.

required.name: floats[0]
required.description: The x coordinate of the tile to point the items at.

required.name: floats[1]
required.description: The y coordinate of the tile to point the items at. Both numbers are needed, and they are only consulted when no comma-separated destination and no second tile coordinate were supplied.

required.name: tileCoords[0]
required.description: The tile whose items are re-pointed. Its x must not be -1, or the task does nothing at all.

optional.name: strings[0]
optional.description: Only affect items of this type. Leave it empty to affect every linkable item on the tile. When the property-filter flag is set this is read as a special property name or number instead.

optional.name: bools[0]
optional.description: When true the destination is added to each item's existing link as an offset rather than replacing it. Defaults to false.

optional.name: bools[1]
optional.description: When true the first string is read as a special property to filter by rather than as an item type. Defaults to false. Supplying it requires the first flag to be supplied as well.

uses.description: Points the items on a tile at another tile, setting the linked location that items such as switches, teleport pads and moving blocks use to know where they act. Only items of a kind that can carry such a link are affected, and they can be narrowed down by item type or by a special property. The destination is given as a second tile coordinate.

required.name: tileCoords[0]
required.description: The tile whose items are re-pointed. Its x must not be -1, or the task does nothing at all.

required.name: tileCoords[1]
required.description: The tile to point the items at. A second tile coordinate can only be given inside a taskString, and it is only consulted when no comma-separated destination was supplied.

optional.name: strings[0]
optional.description: Only affect items of this type. Leave it empty to affect every linkable item on the tile. When the property-filter flag is set this is read as a special property name or number instead.

optional.name: bools[0]
optional.description: When true the destination is added to each item's existing link as an offset rather than replacing it. Defaults to false.

optional.name: bools[1]
optional.description: When true the first string is read as a special property to filter by rather than as an item type. Defaults to false. Supplying it requires the first flag to be supplied as well.

tasks.officialDescription: Sets the specialInfoTC of any valid items that have the ID of 'sValue' (or all items if none set) at tile X,Y to a new specialInfoTC set in 'sValue2' as 'X,Y'. If b1, the specialInfoTC is offset by the X,Y rather than set to it. If b2, 'sValue' is a specialProperty to check for instead of ID.

tasks.name: replaceEquipment

uses.description: Swaps out whatever a named actor has in one equipment slot and puts a freshly created item there instead. Whatever was in the slot is destroyed rather than dropped. Weapons go into the slot number you give, while armour and accessories fall back to their usual slots if you ask for slot 0.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The ID of the actor whose gear is swapped; it must be present in the zone and able to carry things.

required.name: strings[1]
required.description: The ID of the item type to create and equip.

required.name: floats[0]
required.description: Which equipment slot to replace: 0 and 1 are the two hands. For armour a 0 is read as the armour slot instead, and for an accessory a 0 is read as the accessory slot.

tasks.officialDescription: Equips item 'sValue2' to actor 'sValue'. If fValue is specified, replaces that slot. Otherwise replaces the 1st relevant slot (0 for wpns, etc.)

tasks.name: dropItem

uses.description: Takes a number of copies of an item out of a named actor's inventory and drops them on the ground at that actor's feet. Use it to make a character shed something the player can then pick up. Nothing happens if the actor is not present in the zone.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The ID of the actor to take the item from; it must be present in the zone.

required.name: strings[1]
required.description: The ID of the item type to drop. The actor must actually be carrying it, or the task fails.

optional.name: floats[0]
optional.description: How many copies to drop. Defaults to 1, and 0 is also treated as 1.

tasks.officialDescription: Drops item 'sValue2' from actor 'sValue'.

tasks.name: buryAllItemsOfType

uses.description: Buries every matching item across the whole zone, or digs them all back up. A buried item is hidden from view, cannot be picked up or interacted with, and stops reacting to anything until it is dug out. Items can be picked by type, by a special property, or by both at once.

optional.name: strings[0]
optional.description: Bury items of this type. Defaults to empty, which matches nothing on its own.

optional.name: strings[1]
optional.description: Also bury items carrying this special property, given by name or by its number. Defaults to empty, which adds no extra matches.

optional.name: bools[0]
optional.description: When true the matching items are dug up instead of buried. Defaults to false.

tasks.officialDescription: buries all items of type sValue. if bValue1, unburies them. sValue2 = itemType.specialProperty to (un)bury, if specified.

tasks.name: buryGlobalVarItems

uses.description: Goes through every item in the zone that records its state in a global variable and buries or reveals each one according to that variable. An item whose variable is above zero is dug up and visible; one whose variable is zero or unset is buried out of sight. This is how a map's collectibles remember which ones the player has already dealt with.

tasks.officialDescription: buries or unburies items that convert to globals, depending on if their globalVar is set.

tasks.name: buryLocations

uses.description: Hides the map markers of every location in the current zone the player has not discovered yet, burying the marker items on each location's tile and the four tiles around it. Discovered locations are left visible. This is what keeps undiscovered towns and ruins off the world map until they are found.

tasks.officialDescription: buries undiscovered locations.

tasks.name: reactOnMatchingItems

uses.description: Sweeps the zone looking for items of one kind that are facing an item of another kind directly back at them, and makes both members of each matched pair react. This is the machinery behind puzzles where pieces must be lined up nose to nose. Items are only considered matched when the second faces exactly opposite the first.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The ID of the item type to look for first; every item of this type in the zone is checked against the tile it faces.

required.name: strings[1]
required.description: The ID of the item type that must be facing back. Leave it empty to match the first type against itself, which makes the pair react to being matched with their own kind rather than with a different one.

tasks.officialDescription: Finds all 'sValue' items in the zone that are adjacent & facing eachother, and applies Element.matched. If sValue2 is specified, matches sValue & sValue2 items.

tasks.name: specialKeyStatusUpdate

uses.description: Tells the whole party whether they are standing in a zone with a keyhole pedestal in it and whether that zone is a castle, by making every party member react to the matching cues. Equipment and abilities that watch for those cues can then switch themselves on or off. It reacts once per keyhole pedestal found in the zone.

tasks.officialDescription: DO NOT USE.

tasks.name: removeActor

uses.description: Deletes a named actor from the world with no death and no corpse, taking them out of the party, the turn order and any open windows. A puff of smoke can be played where they were, and their belongings can be tipped into the party's stash first so nothing is lost. Nothing happens if no actor with that ID is present.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The ID of the actor to delete; it must be present in the zone.

optional.name: strings[1]
optional.description: The visual effect played where the actor was, when the effect flag is set. Defaults to the standard vanishing puff.

optional.name: bools[0]
optional.description: When true a visual effect is played where the actor was. Defaults to false, which removes them silently.

optional.name: bools[1]
optional.description: When true everything the actor was carrying is tipped into the party's stash before they vanish. Defaults to false, which destroys their belongings with them. Supplying it requires the first flag to be supplied as well.

uses.description: Deletes whichever actor is standing on a chosen tile, with no death and no corpse, taking them out of the party, the turn order and any open windows. A puff of smoke can be played where they were, and their belongings can be tipped into the party's stash first. Nothing happens if the tile is empty.

required.name: tileCoords[0]
required.description: The tile whose occupant is deleted. Its x must not be -1, or the task looks the actor up by ID instead.

optional.name: strings[1]
optional.description: The visual effect played where the actor was, when the effect flag is set. Defaults to the standard vanishing puff. Reaching this slot means filling the first string slot too, with anything at all.

optional.name: bools[0]
optional.description: When true a visual effect is played where the actor was. Defaults to false, which removes them silently.

optional.name: bools[1]
optional.description: When true everything the actor was carrying is tipped into the party's stash before they vanish. Defaults to false. Supplying it requires the first flag to be supplied as well.

tasks.officialDescription: Removes actor 'sValue', or actor at X,Y if specified. If bValue1, adds actor_flee fx. If bValue2, puts their items in your stash.

tasks.name: removeActorType

uses.description: Deletes every actor of a given kind from the zone at once, with no deaths and no corpses. Use it to clear out a crowd of extras when a scene ends. Each one can leave a vanishing puff behind.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The kind of actor to delete; every actor in the zone of this type goes.

optional.name: bools[0]
optional.description: When true a vanishing puff is played where each actor was. Defaults to false, which removes them silently.

tasks.officialDescription: Remove all actors of type 'sValue'. If bValue1, adds actor_flee fx.

tasks.name: removeActors_despawnable

uses.description: Clears out every actor in the zone that is allowed to despawn — the wandering extras and spawned enemies rather than the story characters. It also clears them from a loaded ship interior and drops anything the player was holding in build mode. Optionally it only clears the ones that are down or drowning, awarding the party their experience if this happens during combat.

optional.name: bools[0]
optional.description: When true a vanishing puff is played where each removed actor was. Defaults to false, which removes them silently.

optional.name: bools[1]
optional.description: When true only actors that are already down or drowning are cleared, and hostile ones hand over their experience if this happens in combat. Defaults to false, which clears every despawnable actor. Supplying it requires the first flag to be supplied as well.

tasks.officialDescription: Remove all actors with canDespawn=true. If bValue1, adds actor_flee fx. If bValue2, only affects incapped actors.

tasks.name: setActorFloat

uses.description: Writes a number straight into one of a named actor's own settings, changing it in place. It is the general-purpose way to poke at a numeric property a mod cannot otherwise reach. Nothing happens if the actor is not present or has no setting by that name.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The ID of the actor to change; it must be present in the zone.

required.name: strings[1]
required.description: The name of the actor setting to write, spelled exactly as it is written in actor data. An unrecognised name is quietly ignored.

optional.name: floats[0]
optional.description: The number to store in that setting. Defaults to 0.

tasks.officialDescription: Sets actor 'sValue's float property 'sValue2' to 'fValue'.

tasks.name: setActorBool

uses.description: Writes a yes-or-no value straight into one of a named actor's own settings, changing it in place. The value can be given either as a flag or as a number, with any number above zero counting as yes. Nothing happens if the actor is not present or has no setting by that name.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The ID of the actor to change; it must be present in the zone.

required.name: strings[1]
required.description: The name of the actor setting to write, spelled exactly as it is written in actor data. An unrecognised name is quietly ignored.

optional.name: floats[0]
optional.description: Any value above 0 sets the setting to yes. Defaults to 0. Either this or the flag being set is enough.

optional.name: bools[0]
optional.description: True sets the setting to yes. Defaults to false, which sets it to no unless the number above is positive.

tasks.officialDescription: Sets actor 'sValue's bool property 'sValue2' to bValue1.

tasks.name: setActorAI

uses.description: Switches a named actor over to a different AI script, restarting it from the beginning and dropping whatever it was waiting on. Optionally the new script is also run through once immediately rather than waiting for the actor's next turn. Nothing happens if the actor is not present in the zone.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The ID of the actor whose AI changes; it must be present in the zone.

optional.name: strings[1]
optional.description: The name of the AI script to switch to. Defaults to empty, which leaves the actor running an unnamed script and so effectively idle. The special name "base" returns the actor to the script it treats as its baseline.

optional.name: bools[0]
optional.description: When true the new script is executed once straight away, with the actor as its subject, instead of waiting for its next update. Defaults to false.

tasks.officialDescription: Sets actor 'sValue's lua ai script to 'sValue2'. If bValue1, run the ai script once.

tasks.name: setActorName

uses.description: Changes the display name of a named actor, which is what shows in the stats panel, in dialog and over their head. Use it to reveal a stranger's real name once the player learns it. Nothing happens if the actor is not present in the zone.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The ID of the actor to rename; it must be present in the zone.

optional.name: strings[1]
optional.description: The new display name. Defaults to empty, which leaves the actor nameless.

tasks.officialDescription: Sets actor 'sValue's name to 'sValue2'.

tasks.name: setActorIdleAnimOverride

uses.description: Replaces the animation a named actor plays while standing around doing nothing, so a character can be made to sit, sleep, lean or work in place. It stays in force until it is cleared. Nothing happens if the actor is not present in the zone.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The ID of the actor whose idle animation changes; it must be present in the zone.

optional.name: strings[1]
optional.description: The ID of the animation to idle with. Defaults to empty, which returns the actor to its normal idle.

tasks.officialDescription: Sets actor 'sValue's idleAnimOverride to  'sValue2'.

tasks.name: setActorDialogNodeID

uses.description: Changes which conversation a named actor starts when the player talks to them. Use it to move a character on to their next scene, or to silence them by clearing it. Nothing happens if the actor is not present in the zone.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The ID of the actor whose conversation changes; it must be present in the zone.

optional.name: strings[1]
optional.description: The ID of the dialog node to start from. The special value "defaultDialogNode" restores whatever that kind of actor normally opens with. Defaults to empty, which leaves the actor with nothing to say.

tasks.officialDescription: Sets actor 'sValue's dialogNodeID to  'sValue2'.

tasks.name: setActorAIActions

uses.description: Hands a named actor a queue of actions its AI should try to use, one after another, in place of whatever it had queued before. The actor attempts the first one on its turn if it is able to, then moves on to the next. Nothing happens if the actor is not present in the zone.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The ID of the actor whose action queue is set; it must be present in the zone.

optional.name: strings[1]
optional.description: The action IDs to queue, separated by commas, in the order they should be attempted. Because it contains commas the multi-action form cannot be written inside a taskString. Defaults to empty, which leaves the actor with a single blank entry queued.

tasks.officialDescription: Sets actor 'sValue's queuedAiActions to 'sValue2' (ex: action1, action2, ...).

tasks.name: setActorMovementType

uses.description: Changes how a named actor gets around — burrowing through earth, teleporting, flying over obstacles and so on — by switching its movement type and rebuilding the rules for where it can step. Any special movement rules from the old type are cleared first. Nothing happens if the actor is not present in the zone.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The ID of the actor whose movement changes; it must be present in the zone.

optional.name: strings[1]
optional.description: The movement type to switch to, such as the burrowing or earth-travel behaviours. The special value "defaultMovementType" restores whatever that kind of actor normally uses. Defaults to empty, which clears any special movement rules.

tasks.officialDescription: Sets actor 'sValue's movementType to 'sValue2'. If sValue2 is set to 'defaultMovementType', actorType.movementType is used.

tasks.name: setActorPalettes

uses.description: Recolours a named actor wholesale by putting the same colour palette on their armour, their skin and their clothes at once. This is the quick way to turn a character into a silhouette, a ghost or a uniformed variant. An unrecognised palette name clears all three back to their defaults, and nothing happens if the actor is not present.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The ID of the actor to recolour; it must be present in the zone.

optional.name: strings[1]
optional.description: The palette applied to armour, skin and clothes alike. Defaults to empty, and any name that is not a real palette is treated the same way, which restores the default colours.

tasks.officialDescription: Sets actor 'sValue's palettes to 'sValue2'.

tasks.name: setActorArmorPalette

uses.description: Recolours just the armour of a named actor. It can also be set to follow whatever the actor is actually wearing, which is how armour colour is resynchronised after an equipment change. An unrecognised palette name clears the override back to the default, and nothing happens if the actor is not present.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The ID of the actor to recolour; it must be present in the zone.

optional.name: strings[1]
optional.description: The palette applied to the actor's armour. The special value "defaultPalette" restores what that kind of actor normally uses, and "currentArmorPalette" takes the colour from the armour they are actually wearing, or their bare-skinned colour if they wear none. Defaults to empty, which clears the override.

tasks.officialDescription: Sets actor 'sValue's armorPalette to 'sValue2'. If sValue2 is set to 'defaultPalette', actorType.armorPalette is used. If sValue2 is 'currentArmorPalette', the equipped armor palette is used.

tasks.name: setActorSkinPalette

uses.description: Recolours just the skin of a named actor, which is how a character is turned pale, sunburnt, undead or into another variety of their species. It can also roll a random skin colour from the ones that kind of actor is allowed. An unrecognised palette name clears the override back to the default, and nothing happens if the actor is not present.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The ID of the actor to recolour; it must be present in the zone.

optional.name: strings[1]
optional.description: The palette applied to the actor's skin. The special value "defaultPalette" restores what that kind of actor normally uses, and "randomPalette" picks at random from the skin colours that kind of actor allows. Defaults to empty, which clears the override.

tasks.officialDescription: Sets actor 'sValue's skinPalette to 'sValue2'. If sValue2 is 'defaultPalette', actorType.skinPalette is used. If sValue2 is 'randomPalette', a random palette from actorType.skinPalettes is used.

tasks.name: setActorClothPalette

uses.description: Recolours just the clothing of a named actor, which is how uniforms, disguises and crew colours are applied. It can copy the player's own clothing colour or roll a random one from the palettes the player is allowed to wear. An unrecognised palette name clears the override back to the default, and nothing happens if the actor is not present.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The ID of the actor to recolour; it must be present in the zone.

optional.name: strings[1]
optional.description: The palette applied to the actor's clothing. The special value "defaultPalette" restores what that kind of actor normally uses, "playerPalette" copies the player's own clothing colour, and "randomPalette" picks at random from the clothing colours the player can wear. Defaults to empty, which clears the override.

tasks.officialDescription: Sets actor 'sValue's clothPalette to 'sValue2'. If sValue2 is 'defaultPalette', actorType.clothPalette is used. If sValue2 is 'randomPalette', a random selectable player palette is chosen. If sValue2 is 'playerPalette', the player's current clothPalette is used.

tasks.name: setActorUnarmoredPalette

uses.description: Sets the colour a named actor shows on their body when they are not wearing armour, and applies it to their armour colour too unless they currently have armour equipped. Use it to change the look of a bare-chested or lightly dressed character without disturbing their gear. An unrecognised palette name clears the override, and nothing happens if the actor is not present.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The ID of the actor to recolour; it must be present in the zone.

optional.name: strings[1]
optional.description: The palette used for the actor's unarmoured body. The special value "defaultPalette" restores what that kind of actor normally uses for armour. Defaults to empty, which clears the override.

tasks.officialDescription: Sets actor 'sValue's unarmoredPalette to 'sValue2'. Updates armorPalette if no armor is equipped.

tasks.name: setActorCombatLabel

uses.description: Puts a short label above a named actor that is only shown during combat, which is how ships and units are tagged with a fleet name or a number. Clearing it removes the tag. Nothing happens if the actor is not present in the zone.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The ID of the actor to label; it must be present in the zone.

optional.name: strings[1]
optional.description: The text of the label. Defaults to empty, which removes the label.

tasks.officialDescription: Sets actor 'sValue's combatLabel to 'sValue2'.

tasks.name: setActorCombatLabel_color

uses.description: Sets the colour of a named actor's combat label from raw colour channel values rather than a colour name. Supplying a fourth number sets the transparency as well. Nothing happens if the actor is not present in the zone.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The ID of the actor whose label colour changes; it must be present in the zone.

required.name: floats[0]
required.description: The red channel, from 0 to 255. Supplying three or more numbers switches the task to reading the colour from them and ignores any colour name given.

required.name: floats[1]
required.description: The green channel, from 0 to 255.

required.name: floats[2]
required.description: The blue channel, from 0 to 255.

optional.name: floats[3]
optional.description: The transparency, from 0 for invisible to 255 for solid. Defaults to fully solid when only three numbers are given.

uses.description: Sets the colour of a named actor's combat label by name, which is how friendly, hostile and allied fleets are told apart at a glance. Four special names pick up the game's own fleet label colours. Nothing happens if the actor is not present in the zone.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The ID of the actor whose label colour changes; it must be present in the zone.

optional.name: strings[1]
optional.description: The label colour by name, or as three or four comma-separated channel values. The special names "enemyFleet", "playerFleet", "assistFleet" and "assistFleet_hostile" use the game's own fleet label colours. Defaults to white.

tasks.officialDescription: Sets actor 'sValue's combatLabel_color to 'sValue2'. If sValue2 is 'enemyFleet', 'playerFleet', 'assistFleet' or 'assistFleet_hostile', that set global Color is used.

tasks.name: setActorCombatTeam

uses.description: Puts a named actor on a combat team, which decides who counts as a friend when the AI picks targets and helps. Actors on the same side of the fight but on different teams will not treat each other as allies. Nothing happens if the actor is not present in the zone.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The ID of the actor whose team changes; it must be present in the zone.

optional.name: strings[1]
optional.description: The name of the team to join. The special value "defaultCombatTeam" restores whatever that kind of actor normally belongs to. Defaults to empty, which leaves the actor on no team.

tasks.officialDescription: Sets actor 'sValue's combatTeam to 'sValue2'. If 'sValue2' is 'defaultCombatTeam', actorType.defaultCombatTeam is used.

tasks.name: setActorCombatMusicOverride

uses.description: Gives a named actor its own battle music, which replaces the zone's usual combat track whenever a fight starts that includes it. Use it to give a boss its own theme. Nothing happens if the actor is not present in the zone.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The ID of the actor to give battle music to; it must be present in the zone.

optional.name: strings[1]
optional.description: The music track that plays when this actor is in a fight. Defaults to empty, which removes the override and lets the zone's own combat music play.

tasks.officialDescription: Sets actor 'sValue's combatMusicOverride to 'sValue2'.

tasks.name: setActorFaction

uses.description: Moves a named actor into a different faction, which changes who counts as their allies and enemies. Player-controlled actors and anyone already in the player's own faction are refused, and so is any attempt to move an actor into the player's faction, so this cannot be used to recruit. Nothing happens if the actor is not present in the zone.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The ID of the actor whose faction changes; it must be present in the zone, must not be player-controlled and must not already belong to the player.

optional.name: strings[1]
optional.description: The faction to move the actor into. The special value "defaultFaction" restores whatever that kind of actor normally belongs to, and the value "player" is refused outright. Defaults to empty, which leaves the actor with no faction.

tasks.officialDescription: Sets actor 'sValue's faction to 'sValue2'. If 'sValue2' is 'defaultFaction', actorType.defaultFaction is used. Can't change to/from 'player' faction.

tasks.name: setActorID

uses.description: Renames a named actor, changing the ID other tasks and triggers use to find them. Their belongings and any open conversation follow the new name. The player actor cannot be renamed and the new name cannot be "player"; if the name is already taken, or you ask for it, a number is tacked on to keep it unique.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The current ID of the actor to rename; it must be present in the zone and must not be the player.

optional.name: strings[1]
optional.description: The new ID. Leaving it empty, or setting it to "player", does nothing at all.

optional.name: bools[0]
optional.description: When true the new ID is always made unique by appending the zone name and a number, even if nothing else is using it. Defaults to false, which only does so when the name is already taken.

tasks.officialDescription: Sets actor 'sValue's ID to 'sValue2'. If bValue1 is true, forces a unique ID based on sValue2. Cant change an ID to/from 'player'.

tasks.name: setActorSprite

uses.description: Changes the sprite a named actor is drawn with, swapping their whole appearance for another image in the game's texture set. Use it to transform a character or switch a prop actor between states. Nothing happens if the actor is not present in the zone.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The ID of the actor to redraw; it must be present in the zone.

optional.name: strings[1]
optional.description: The name of the sprite to draw the actor with. The special value "defaultSprite" restores whatever that kind of actor normally uses. Defaults to empty, which leaves the actor with no sprite.

tasks.officialDescription: Sets actor 'sValue's sprite to 'sValue2'. If 'sValue2' is 'defaultSprite', actorType.defaultSprite is used.

tasks.name: setActorBodyPartSprite

uses.description: Changes the sprite used for one part of a named actor's body — their head, face, arms, legs and so on — leaving the rest of them alone. This is how hairstyles, expressions and outfits are swapped piecemeal. Nothing happens if the actor is not present or has no body part by that name.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The ID of the actor to change; it must be present in the zone.

required.name: strings[1]
required.description: The name of the body part to change, such as the head or face slot.

required.name: strings[2]
required.description: The name of the sprite to put on that part. The special value "defaultSprite" restores what that kind of actor normally uses, and "randomSprite" picks at random from the sprites that kind of actor allows for the part.

uses.description: Changes the sprite used for one part of a named actor's body, with the part and the sprite packed into a single comma-separated value. This is the form to use as a trigger effect, where only two strings are available. Nothing happens if the value has no comma in it, or if the actor is not present or has no body part by that name.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The ID of the actor to change; it must be present in the zone.

required.name: strings[1]
required.description: The body part name and the sprite name, separated by a comma, such as "head,head3". It must contain a comma or nothing happens. The sprite half accepts "defaultSprite" to restore the normal one and "randomSprite" to pick at random from the sprites that kind of actor allows.

tasks.officialDescription: Sets the sprite for actor 'sValue's bodyPart set in 'sValue2'. sValue2 needs to be in the format 'bodyPartID, spriteSheet'. If the 'spriteSheet' part of sValue2 is 'defaultSprite', actorType.defaultBodyPartSprites for the bodyPart is used. If it is 'randomSprite', a random sprite for the bodyPart from actorType.bodyPartSprites is used.

tasks.name: setFaceSprite

uses.description: Changes the face sprite of the actor the task is running on, which is how an expression is swapped mid-conversation. Only the face changes; the rest of the character is untouched. Nothing happens if there is no contextual actor.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The name of the sprite to use for the face.

tasks.officialDescription: Sets the 'face' bodyPart sprite for the currentActorTalkingTo (or current task actor if not in dialog) to 'sValue'.

tasks.name: setCurrentActor_partSpritesThatTakePriorityOverClass

uses.description: Tells whichever actor is currently taking its turn that certain body parts should keep the sprites they already have rather than being overwritten by the sprites its class would impose. Use it to preserve a custom head or face through a class change. Nothing happens if no actor is currently acting.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The body part names to protect, separated by commas. Because it contains commas the multi-part form cannot be written inside a taskString.

tasks.officialDescription: Sets 'partSpritesThatTakePriorityOverClass' of the current player leader to sValue1 (ex: 'torso, armR, shoulderR')

tasks.name: setActor_partSpritesThatTakePriorityOverClass

uses.description: Tells a named actor that certain body parts should keep the sprites they already have rather than being overwritten by the sprites its class would impose. Use it to preserve a custom head or face through a class change. Nothing happens if the actor is not present in the zone.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The ID of the actor to change; it must be present in the zone.

required.name: strings[1]
required.description: The first body part name to protect.

optional.name: strings[2+]
optional.description: Any number of further body part names to protect, one per value. They are joined onto the first with commas, which is how a taskString supplies a list.

tasks.officialDescription: Sets actor 'sValue's partSpritesThatTakePriorityOverClass to 'sValue2' (ex: 'torso, armR, shoulderR')

tasks.name: giveActorsBaseXP

uses.description: Hands every actor in the zone a starting lump of experience in each of the game's classes they have barely touched, so freshly spawned characters are not left at nothing. Actors already past that threshold in a class are skipped for it. Then, if the shared-experience setting held in the global variable XPShare is above zero, every actor is additionally given that percentage of each class's banked experience pool, so a party that has earned a great deal brings newcomers up with it; leave XPShare at its default of zero and this second helping does not happen. Both helpings ignore fatigue, party size and the player's experience multiplier.

tasks.officialDescription: Awards between 54 and 84 XP in all classes to every actor in the zone, if they have less than 54 XP.

tasks.name: moveActor

uses.description: Teleports a named actor onto a chosen tile and turns them to face a given direction. There is no walking and no animation — they simply appear there, whether or not the tile is occupied. Nothing happens if the actor is not present in the zone.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The ID of the actor to move; it must be present in the zone.

optional.name: floats[0]
optional.description: The direction the actor faces after moving, in degrees. Defaults to 0.

optional.name: tileCoords[0]
optional.description: The tile to place the actor on. If omitted it defaults to (-1,-1), which puts them off the map.

tasks.officialDescription: Moves actor 'sValue' to X,Y and sets facingRot to 'fValue'.

tasks.name: moveActor_point

uses.description: Teleports a named actor onto one of the zone's numbered travel points and turns them to face a given direction. Travel points are items placed in the map data, so this positions a character without hard-coding coordinates. Nothing happens if the actor is not present in the zone.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The ID of the actor to move; it must be present in the zone. The slot must be supplied even though nothing happens when it names no one.

required.name: tileCoords[0]
required.description: Its x is the travel-point number and its y the travel-point set, so (2,0) means travel point 2 of the first set. Sets beyond the first are the lettered variants of each point.

optional.name: floats[0]
optional.description: The direction the actor faces after moving, in degrees. Defaults to 0.

tasks.officialDescription: Moves actor 'sValue' to #X, set Y (A=0, B=1...) travel point.

tasks.name: movePartyTo

uses.description: Teleports the whole party onto a chosen tile, shuffling members onto nearby free tiles if the spot is crowded, and snaps the camera there. While walking around, the player is briefly locked out of interacting so the jump does not eat an input. The party can also be turned to face a given direction.

required.name: tileCoords[0]
required.description: The tile the party is moved to. If omitted it defaults to (-1,-1), which is pulled back inside the map and lands them in the top-left corner.

optional.name: floats[0]
optional.description: The direction every party member faces after moving, in degrees. Defaults to 0, which leaves their facing alone.

tasks.officialDescription: Moves entire party and camera by X,Y - triggerActor.position. If fValue != 0, sets actors' facingRot to fValue.

tasks.name: movePartyTo_point

uses.description: Teleports the whole party onto one of the zone's numbered travel points, shuffling members onto nearby free tiles if the spot is crowded. It can also spread the party out across the whole set of travel points rather than piling them on one, and pull the rest of the player's fleet into a ship zone so the whole flotilla arrives together.

required.name: tileCoords[0]
required.description: Its x is the travel-point number and its y the travel-point set, so (2,0) means travel point 2 of the first set.

optional.name: bools[0]
optional.description: When true the party is spread out across the whole travel-point set rather than stacked on the one point, each member taking a different point. Defaults to false.

optional.name: bools[1]
optional.description: When true, and the party is aboard ship, every other vessel in the player's fleet that is not already present is brought into the zone and added to the party. Defaults to false. Supplying it requires the first flag to be supplied as well.

tasks.officialDescription: Moves entire party and camera to travel point #X, set Y (A=0, B=1...) If bValue1, doesn't use X - just puts party on the set. If b2, brings out boats from player fleet.

tasks.name: movePartyBy

uses.description: Shifts every party member by a fixed offset from wherever they currently stand, and slides the camera by the same amount so the view does not jump. Members are kept inside the map bounds. They can also all be turned to face a given direction.

optional.name: floats[0]
optional.description: The direction every party member faces after moving, in degrees. Defaults to 0, which leaves their facing alone.

optional.name: tileCoords[0]
optional.description: How far to shift, as an x and y offset in tiles. If omitted it defaults to (-1,-1), shifting everyone one tile up and to the left.

tasks.officialDescription: Moves entire party and camera by X,Y. If fValue != 0, sets actors' facingRot to fValue.

tasks.name: moveAllActorsBy

uses.description: Shifts every actor in the zone by a fixed offset from wherever they currently stand, and slides the camera by the same amount. Actors are kept inside the map bounds. They can also all be turned to face a given direction.

optional.name: floats[0]
optional.description: The direction every actor faces after moving, in degrees. Defaults to 0, which leaves their facing alone.

optional.name: tileCoords[0]
optional.description: How far to shift, as an x and y offset in tiles. If omitted it defaults to (-1,-1), shifting everyone one tile up and to the left.

tasks.officialDescription: Moves all actors and camera by X,Y. If fValue != 0, sets actors' facingRot to fValue.

tasks.name: addToParty

uses.description: Adds a named actor to the player's party, turning them into an ally the player controls. A ship joins the player's fleet, and crew are shuffled about accordingly. Nothing happens if the actor is not present in the zone or is already a member — and in that case the task reports failure, which stops the trigger that ran it: any effects listed after this one are abandoned.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The ID of the actor to recruit; it must be present in the zone.

tasks.officialDescription: Adds actor ID 'sValue' to the party.

tasks.name: addTalkerToParty

uses.description: Adds the actor the task is running on to the player's party and fleet, turning them into a controllable ally. An actor whose ID marks them as a hireling is given a fresh permanent ID first and is put into the landing party. Recruiting costs a point of crew morale while morale is high.

optional.name: bools[0]
optional.description: When true the new member is also put into the landing party, so they come ashore with the player. Defaults to false, though hirelings are added to it regardless.

tasks.officialDescription: Adds the currentActorTalkingTo (or current task actor if not in dialog) to the player's crew. Also adds to the landing party and makes their ID unique if their ID starts with 'hire_'. If b1, adds to the landing party regardless of actor ID.

tasks.name: addTalkerToParty_temp
