uses.description: Adds the actor the task is running on to the player's party as a temporary guest rather than a permanent recruit. Their appearance cannot be edited, their corpse cannot be looted, the player cannot fully take them over, and they are dressed in the player's own colours. Their action list is rebuilt on joining, and if the difficulty settings had granted them a bonus ability they get their hard-mode support ability and a rank in each of their class's actions.

tasks.officialDescription: Adds the currentActorTalkingTo (or current task actor if not in dialog) to the player's landing party as a temporary party actor. Does not add the actor to the player's crew. Can be removed using the 'removeTempPartyActors' task.

tasks.name: removeFromParty

uses.description: Takes a named actor out of the player's party, leaving them in the world as an independent character rather than storing them in the barracks. They can also be dropped from the player's fleet at the same time. Nothing happens if the actor is not currently in the party — and in that case the task reports failure, which stops the trigger that ran it: any effects listed after this one are abandoned.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The ID of the party member to dismiss.

optional.name: bools[0]
optional.description: When true the actor is also dropped from the player's fleet. Defaults to false.

tasks.officialDescription: Removes actor ID 'sValue' from the party. If bValue1, removes from fleet as well (if applicable).

tasks.name: clearPartyPath

uses.description: Cancels the route the party is currently walking, stopping them where they stand. Use it to interrupt automatic movement before a scene starts. Nothing else about the party changes.

tasks.officialDescription: Makes party actors temporarily able to move freely, without following the currently selected party leader.

tasks.name: addToLandingParty

uses.description: Adds one of the player's crew to the landing party, the small group that goes ashore and fights on foot. The actor must actually be crew aboard the player's fleet, and the landing party normally cannot grow past its size limit. In a peaceful zone the new member is also brought into the world beside the player straight away.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The ID of the crew member to add; they must be aboard one of the player's ships.

optional.name: bools[0]
optional.description: When true the member is only enrolled and not brought into the current zone; when false they are brought in beside the player even outside a peaceful zone. Defaults to false.

optional.name: bools[1]
optional.description: When true the landing party's size limit is ignored, letting it grow past its normal maximum. Defaults to false. Supplying it requires the first flag to be supplied as well.

tasks.officialDescription: Adds the player crew actor with the ID of 'sValue' to the player's landing party if they can fit, and to the current Zone. If b1, don't add them to the current Zone. If b2, adds them to the landing party even if they can't fit.

tasks.name: removeFromLandingParty

uses.description: Takes a named actor out of the landing party, the group that goes ashore on foot. The main player character can never be removed, and neither can the last remaining member. Nothing happens if the actor is not in the landing party.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The ID of the landing party member to remove.

optional.name: bools[0]
optional.description: Passed through as the removal's own option flag. Defaults to false.

tasks.officialDescription: Removes the player crew actor with the ID of 'sValue' from the player's landing party, if they are currently in it, and the current Zone. If b1, don't remove them from the current Zone.

tasks.name: handleTiredStates

uses.description: Ends the day for the party: everyone is patched up and their status effects cleared, but they each pick up another point of fatigue, so repeated rests wear the crew down. Party members waiting in the barracks are fully restored instead, including their knockout penalty, and have a point of fatigue cured. This is the routine behind resting.

tasks.officialDescription: DO NOT USE. Makes party tired, and makes barracks actors rested.

tasks.name: hideParty

uses.description: Makes every party member invisible for a number of seconds, so they cannot be seen on the map while the timer runs. Use it to clear the screen for a scripted scene without moving anyone. The timer counts down in game time and they reappear on their own.

required.name: floats[0]
required.description: How many seconds the party stays invisible.

tasks.officialDescription: Turns party invisible for 'fValue' time.

tasks.name: path

uses.description: Sends an actor walking to a tile along a route worked out for them, following the map's own pathing rules and stopping at obstacles it cannot get past. Whatever route they were on is discarded first. A different route-finder that follows the zone's waypoints can be used instead, and their walking speed can be changed for the trip.

optional.name: strings[0]
optional.description: The ID of the actor to send walking. If it names no one, the actor the task is running on walks instead.

optional.name: floats[0]
optional.description: The actor's walking speed for the trip; larger is faster. Defaults to leaving their speed alone.

optional.name: bools[0]
optional.description: When true the route is worked out along the zone's waypoint network instead of by ordinary pathing, which suits long journeys across a map built with waypoints. Defaults to false.

optional.name: tileCoords[0]
optional.description: The tile to walk to. If omitted it defaults to (-1,-1), which is off the map and yields no usable route.

tasks.officialDescription: Sets path of actor of ID 'sValue' (or triggerActor if unspecifed) to X,Y. If bValue is true, uses waypoints. fValue permanently sets movementSpeed if specified.

tasks.name: pathParty

uses.description: Sends every party member walking to the same tile, each along their own route worked out with the map's pathing rules. Whatever routes they were on are discarded first. They walk at their normal speeds and will bunch up when they arrive.

optional.name: tileCoords[0]
optional.description: The tile every party member walks to. If omitted it defaults to (-1,-1), which is off the map and yields no usable route.

tasks.officialDescription: Sets path of all party actors to X,Y.

tasks.name: destination

uses.description: Points an actor at a destination tile and lets them make their own way there step by step, rather than handing them a precomputed route. Any route they were already following is discarded. Their walking speed can be changed for the trip.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The ID of the actor to send. If it names no one, the actor the task is running on is sent instead, but the slot must still be supplied.

optional.name: floats[0]
optional.description: The actor's walking speed for the trip; larger is faster. Defaults to leaving their speed alone.

optional.name: tileCoords[0]
optional.description: The destination tile. If omitted it defaults to (-1,-1), which sends the actor off the map.

tasks.officialDescription: Sets destination of actor of ID 'sValue' (or triggerActor if unspecifed) to X,Y. fValue permanently sets movementSpeed if specified.

tasks.name: movement

uses.description: Slides an actor straight to a tile in one smooth move, passing through anything in the way. Their current route and pending inputs are dropped first, and if it is the player being moved their controls are cleared too. Leaving either coordinate at -1 keeps that axis where it already was, so the actor can be slid along a single row or column.

optional.name: strings[0]
optional.description: The ID of the actor to slide. Leave it empty to slide the actor the task is running on; naming an actor that is not present does nothing.

optional.name: floats[0]
optional.description: The actor's movement speed for the slide; larger is faster. Defaults to leaving their speed alone.

optional.name: bools[0]
optional.description: When true the actor plays their flinch animation once as they move, as though they had been struck. Defaults to false.

optional.name: tileCoords[0]
optional.description: The tile to slide to. A -1 in either coordinate leaves that axis unchanged, and omitting it entirely leaves the actor where they are.

tasks.officialDescription: Sets movement of actor of ID 'sValue' (or triggerActor if unspecifed) to go to X,Y. (If X or Y are unspecified, only moves along the specified axis.) If bValue1, actor uses pain animation. fValue permanently sets movementSpeed if specified.

tasks.name: addZoneFX

uses.description: Registers a visual effect with the current zone so it plays again and again on a timer for as long as the party is there, and again each time they enter. This is how ambient effects like falling leaves, drifting mist or dripping water are attached to a map. The effect is remembered with the zone rather than played once.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The ID of the visual effect to attach to the zone.

optional.name: floats[0]
optional.description: How many seconds between repeats. Defaults to 0, which replays it as fast as the game updates. A value of -1 or lower, or anything above about 9998, stops the repeats so it only plays on entering the zone.

optional.name: bools[0]
optional.description: When true the effect is not added again if the zone already has a copy of it, which avoids stacking duplicates. Defaults to false.

optional.name: tileCoords[0]
optional.description: The tile the effect plays at. If omitted it defaults to (-1,-1), and an x of -1 makes the effect follow the camera instead of sitting at a fixed spot.

tasks.officialDescription: Adds a recurring FX 'sValue' to the zone at XY that recurs every 'fValue' indefinitely. If bValue1, then only add FX if it isn't already in the zone.

tasks.name: createZoneSpecialFX

uses.description: Generates a full-map overlay texture for the current zone and lays it over the whole map in tiles, which is how the shimmering water surface and similar zone-wide effects are produced. The overlay is built from the zone's own layout, so it lines up with the terrain, and it is registered with the zone so it keeps drawing. It can be drawn beneath everything as a water surface or on top of everything as a haze, and can be made to drift across the map.

optional.name: strings[0]
optional.description: The name of a pattern image to build the overlay from, in place of the default. Defaults to empty, which uses the standard pattern.

optional.name: floats[0]
optional.description: How much to reduce the overlay's opacity by; larger values make it fainter. Defaults to none. It only takes effect the first time this overlay is created for a zone.

optional.name: bools[0]
optional.description: When true the overlay is drawn beneath everything else at the water surface's own transparency, giving a reflective water look; when false it is drawn on top of everything as a haze. Defaults to false.

optional.name: bools[1]
optional.description: When true each generated overlay tile is also written out to the desktop as an image file, which is a debugging aid rather than something to ship. Defaults to false. Supplying it requires the first flag to be supplied as well.

optional.name: tileCoords[0]
optional.description: Gives the overlay a drift, at a tenth of each coordinate per unit of movement, and makes it wrap around the edges of the map and only draw while roofs are drawn. If omitted it defaults to (-1,-1), which still counts as a drift; leave both at -1 only if you want that. It only takes effect the first time this overlay is created for a zone.

tasks.officialDescription: Creates FX based on zone_tintMap, or if bValue1, deepWater. sValue = pattern texture override. XY * 0.1 = veloc. fValue = -alpha offset. If bValue2, saves textures to the desktop.

tasks.name: removeZoneFX

uses.description: Takes a repeating visual effect off the current zone so it stops playing. Note that it only actually removes anything when told to remove every copy; asking to remove just one leaves the effect in place. Nothing happens if the zone does not have that effect.

optional.name: strings[0]
optional.description: The ID of the visual effect to take off the zone. Defaults to empty, which matches nothing.

optional.name: bools[0]
optional.description: Must be true for anything to be removed: it strips every copy of the effect from the zone. Defaults to false, which removes nothing at all.

tasks.officialDescription: Removes recurring FX 'sValue' from the zone. If bValue1, removes all instances of that FX.

tasks.name: addZoneBackgroundTex

uses.description: Adds an image to the current zone's backdrop, drawn behind the map and scrolling with a parallax offset as the camera moves. Layers stack in the order they are added, so several can be combined for depth. Adding an image the zone already has does nothing.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The name of the image to use as a backdrop layer. It must not be empty.

tasks.officialDescription: Adds texture 'sValue' to the list of background textures for the current Zone, if it doesn't already exist.

tasks.name: removeZoneBackgroundTex

uses.description: Takes a backdrop image off the current zone, or clears every backdrop layer at once. Use it to change the sky or scenery behind a map partway through a scene. Removing an image the zone does not have does nothing.

optional.name: strings[0]
optional.description: The name of the backdrop layer to remove. Defaults to empty, which matches nothing. It is ignored when the clear-everything flag is set.

optional.name: bools[0]
optional.description: When true every backdrop layer is cleared and the named image is ignored. Defaults to false, which removes only the named layer.

tasks.officialDescription: Removes texture 'sValue' from the list of background textures for the current zone, if it exists. If b1, removes all background textures.

tasks.name: setZonePalettes

uses.description: Recolours one family of terrain across the whole current zone by pointing it at a different colour palette, which is how a map is reskinned into a snowy, volcanic or nocturnal variant without changing any tiles. An unrecognised slot name sets every terrain family at once, so it is the way to wash the entire map in one palette. The change sticks with the zone.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: Which family of terrain to recolour. Recognised names cover stone, its dark and light variants, dirt and dark dirt, grass and dark grass, water, wood and dark wood, and eight numbered miscellaneous slots; each accepts a short name, a capitalised name, or the full property name. Any name that matches none of them recolours every family at once.

required.name: strings[1]
required.description: The palette to apply to that terrain family.

tasks.officialDescription: Sets 'sValue' zone palette to 'sValue2'. If 'sValue' is blank, sets all palettes.

tasks.name: setZonePeaceful

uses.description: Marks the current zone as peaceful or hostile, ending any fight in progress either way. In a peaceful zone, neutral non-player actors are made invincible so the player cannot kill the townsfolk; turning it off strips that protection and lets actors act again. Every actor's protection is re-evaluated when the setting actually changes.

optional.name: bools[0]
optional.description: True makes the zone peaceful, false makes it hostile and re-enables acting. Defaults to false.

tasks.officialDescription: Set zone.peaceful true if bValue1. False otherwise.

tasks.name: disableFog

uses.description: Turns off the fog of war for the current zone and stops the camera drawing it, so the whole map is visible at once. Use it to reveal an area for a cutscene or a map-wide view. It stays off until something turns it back on.

tasks.officialDescription: Disables fog for this zone.

tasks.name: setZoneRollingPinStyle

uses.description: Switches the current zone between the flat top-down view and the rolled-back perspective used for the world map, where the far half of the screen is squashed toward the horizon and a sky is drawn. Turning it on changes how tiles, effects and the tile cursor are placed on screen. The setting sticks with the zone.

optional.name: bools[0]
optional.description: True switches the zone to the rolled-back horizon view, false back to the flat view. Defaults to false.

tasks.officialDescription: Sets the current zone's rollingPinStyle to bValue1.

tasks.name: screenDarkWaveEffect

uses.description: Sets how tightly the darkness layer ripples across the screen, giving shadows a wavering, underwater or heat-haze quality. Changing the value also restarts the ripple's timing so the change is visible immediately. Setting it to the value it already has does nothing.

required.name: floats[0]
required.description: The ripple frequency for the darkness layer; larger values give tighter waves and 0 turns the effect off.

tasks.officialDescription: Sets zone's darkness wave frequency to fValue.

tasks.name: changeZoneDarkColor

uses.description: Marks the current zone as dark and sets the colour its darkness is tinted with, which controls the mood of night, caves and interiors. The colour normally takes hold as the lighting is next recalculated, but it can be pushed onto the camera straight away for an instant change. The setting sticks with the zone.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The colour of the zone's darkness, by name or as three or four comma-separated channel values.

optional.name: bools[0]
optional.description: When true the camera's darkness colour is changed at once rather than at the next lighting update, so there is no fade. Defaults to false.

tasks.officialDescription: Changes zone darkness color to sValue (given as 'R, G, B'). If bValue1, sets color immediately instead of easing.

tasks.name: setZoneDarknessToWorldDarkness

uses.description: Marks the current zone as dark and sets its darkness colour to whatever the outdoors looks like at the moment, so an interior matches the time of day and weather outside. Towns and ports get their own slight tint on top. The colour normally takes hold at the next lighting update, but it can be pushed onto the camera straight away.

optional.name: bools[0]
optional.description: When true the camera's darkness colour is changed at once rather than at the next lighting update, so there is no fade. Defaults to false.

tasks.officialDescription: Sets the current zone's darknessColor based on the time of day. If b1, also change camera's darknessColor.

tasks.name: screenWaveEffect

uses.description: Sets how tightly the whole screen ripples, giving the view a wavering, underwater or heat-haze quality. Changing the value also restarts the ripple's timing so the change is visible immediately. Setting it to the value it already has does nothing.

required.name: floats[0]
required.description: The ripple frequency for the screen; larger values give tighter waves and 0 turns the effect off.

tasks.officialDescription: Sets zone wave frequency to fValue.

tasks.name: setZoneBG

uses.description: Sets which terrain type is painted across the empty space beyond the edges of the current zone, so the map appears to sit on an ocean, a void or a field rather than ending abruptly. Naming no terrain, or one that does not exist, leaves the surroundings blank. The setting sticks with the zone.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The ID of the terrain type painted around the map's edges.

tasks.officialDescription: Set zone BG; sValue = terrainType.

tasks.name: setZoneBGFX

uses.description: Sets a full-screen visual effect drawn behind the current zone, such as drifting clouds or moving water beneath the map. Naming nothing clears it. The setting sticks with the zone.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The ID of the effect drawn behind the map. Leave it empty to clear the backdrop effect.

tasks.officialDescription: Sets zone bgFXID to 'sValue'.

tasks.name: setZoneFloatProperty

uses.description: Writes a number straight into one of the current zone's own numeric settings, changing it in place. Setting one of the screen-ripple or music volume and pitch settings this way also takes effect immediately rather than waiting for the next zone load. The map's width and height are protected and cannot be changed, and an unrecognised or non-numeric setting name is quietly ignored.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The name of the zone setting to write, spelled exactly as it is written in zone data. It must name a numeric setting, and the map width and height cannot be set this way.

optional.name: floats[0]
optional.description: The number to store in that setting. Defaults to 0.

tasks.officialDescription: Sets the float-type property of the current zone, specified in 'sValue', to the float set in 'fValue'.

tasks.name: setZoneStringProperty

uses.description: Writes a colour into one of the current zone's own colour settings, giving the channel values as numbers rather than a colour name. A fourth number sets the transparency. Setting the darkness colour this way applies to the camera at once, and an unrecognised setting name is quietly ignored.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The name of the zone setting to write, spelled exactly as it is written in zone data. It must name a text or colour setting, and the zone's own ID cannot be changed this way.

required.name: floats[0]
required.description: The red channel, from 0 to 255. Three or more numbers are only read as a colour when no text value is supplied.

required.name: floats[1]
required.description: The green channel, from 0 to 255.

required.name: floats[2]
required.description: The blue channel, from 0 to 255.

optional.name: floats[3]
optional.description: The transparency, from 0 for invisible to 255 for solid. Defaults to fully solid when only three numbers are given.

uses.description: Writes a piece of text into one of the current zone's own text or colour settings, changing it in place. Setting the wandering or fighting music this way starts it playing at once, and setting the darkness colour applies it to the camera at once. The zone's own ID is protected and cannot be changed, and an unrecognised setting name is quietly ignored.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The name of the zone setting to write, spelled exactly as it is written in zone data. It must name a text or colour setting, and the zone's own ID cannot be changed this way.

optional.name: strings[1+]
optional.description: The value to store. Any number of values may be given and they are joined back together with commas, which is how a colour written as separate channel numbers, or any other comma-containing value, is supplied inside a taskString. Defaults to empty.

tasks.officialDescription: Sets the string-type property of the current zone, specified in 'sValue', to the string set in 'sValue2'.

tasks.name: setZoneBoolProperty

uses.description: Writes a yes-or-no value straight into one of the current zone's own settings, changing it in place. Setting the zone's peaceful flag this way also runs the full peaceful-mode changeover, ending any fight and updating actors' protection. An unrecognised or non-flag setting name is quietly ignored.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The name of the zone setting to write, spelled exactly as it is written in zone data. It must name a yes/no setting.

optional.name: bools[0]
optional.description: The value to store. Defaults to false.

tasks.officialDescription: Sets the bool-type property of the current zone, specified in 'sValue', to the bool set by 'b1'.

tasks.name: initWaypoints

uses.description: Rebuilds the current zone's waypoint network from scratch, finding every waypoint marker item on the map and every location in the zone and linking them up through their marker connections. Do this after adding, moving or removing waypoint markers, or the long-distance route-finder will still be using the old network. Buried markers are ignored.

tasks.officialDescription: refreshes waypoint data of the current zone

tasks.name: safe

uses.description: Puts the zone into a cautious movement mode, where actors take the shortest safe step toward their goal instead of picking the tactically best midpoint. Use it where clever pathing would look wrong or risk actors wandering into hazards. It is cleared automatically the next time a turn advances.

tasks.officialDescription: When in this trigger, ZoneManager.I.safe is true. Safe is used by the AI.

tasks.name: sendAISignal

uses.description: Shouts a named signal to every actor within a distance, and each one that has a response registered for that signal in its AI script runs it at once. This is how a guard raises an alarm or a boss cues its minions. Downed actors are skipped.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The name of the signal to send. Only actors whose AI script has a response registered for exactly this name react.

optional.name: floats[0]
optional.description: How far the signal carries, in tiles. Defaults to 0, which reaches only actors on the origin tile itself.

optional.name: tileCoords[0]
optional.description: The tile the signal is shouted from. If either coordinate is left at -1 it falls back to the tile of the actor the task is running on, or to the camera's position if there is none.

tasks.officialDescription: Sends signal 'sValue' to all actors within 'fValue' of X,Y (or triggering actor pos, or camera).

tasks.name: disableTrigger

uses.description: Marks a trigger in the current zone as already used, so it will not fire again while the party stays in that zone. The trigger can be picked by its alias or by its number. A trigger already marked used is left alone.

optional.name: strings[0]
optional.description: The alias of the trigger to switch off. If it names no trigger in the zone, the number is used instead. Defaults to empty.

optional.name: floats[0]
optional.description: The number of the trigger to switch off, used when no alias matches. Defaults to 0, which is the zone's first trigger.

tasks.officialDescription: Disables trigger of IDnum fValue or alias sValue.

tasks.name: enableTrigger

uses.description: Clears the used mark from a trigger in the current zone, so a one-shot trigger can fire again. The trigger can be picked by its alias or by its number. A trigger that is not currently marked used is left alone.

optional.name: strings[0]
optional.description: The alias of the trigger to switch back on. If it names no trigger in the zone, the number is used instead. Defaults to empty.

optional.name: floats[0]
optional.description: The number of the trigger to switch back on, used when no alias matches. Defaults to 0, which is the zone's first trigger.

tasks.officialDescription: Re-enables trigger of IDnum fValue or alias sValue.

tasks.name: trigger

uses.description: Fires a named trigger right now, running all of its effects, which is how one trigger chains into another or a dialog kicks off a scripted sequence. The name is looked for among the current zone's own triggers first and then among the game's global triggers. A formula can be attached as a condition, and the trigger's own conditions can be bypassed.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The alias of the trigger to fire, searched first in the current zone and then among global triggers. Leaving it empty fires a trigger by number instead.

optional.name: strings[1]
optional.description: A condition worked out against the actor the task is running on; the trigger only fires if it comes out above zero. Defaults to empty, which fires unconditionally.

optional.name: bools[0]
optional.description: When true the trigger's own conditions and its used mark are ignored entirely, forcing it to fire. Defaults to false.

optional.name: bools[1]
optional.description: When true only the trigger's requirement formula is checked and its used mark, travel-mode restriction and other gating are skipped. Defaults to false. Supplying it requires the first flag to be supplied as well.

uses.description: Fires one of the current zone's triggers by its number rather than its alias, running all of its effects. Use it where a trigger has no alias to name it by. A formula can be attached as a condition, and the trigger's own conditions can be bypassed.

required.name: floats[0]
required.description: The number of the trigger in the current zone to fire. Nothing happens if the zone has no trigger with that number.

optional.name: strings[1]
optional.description: A condition worked out against the actor the task is running on; the trigger only fires if it comes out above zero. Reaching this slot means filling the first string slot too, and it must be left empty or the trigger is looked up by name instead.

optional.name: bools[0]
optional.description: When true the trigger's own conditions and its used mark are ignored entirely, forcing it to fire. Defaults to false.

optional.name: bools[1]
optional.description: When true only the trigger's requirement formula is checked and its used mark, travel-mode restriction and other gating are skipped. Defaults to false. Supplying it requires the first flag to be supplied as well.

tasks.officialDescription: Executes trigger of sValue aliasID (including globalTriggers), or of IDnum fValue. sValue2 is an additional fReq. If bValue1, then execute regardless of the trigger's fReq/Once-only. If bValue2, can't rerun a Once-Only trigger.

tasks.name: addTrigger

uses.description: Copies one of the game's global triggers into the current zone, giving it a fresh number so it lives alongside the zone's own triggers. From then on it behaves as a zone trigger and can be switched on and off individually. Nothing happens if no global trigger has that name or the zone already has a trigger with it.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The name of the global trigger to copy into the zone.

tasks.officialDescription: Adds global trigger 'sValue' to the current zone. Only usable if delay is not 0 (otherwise it crashes).

tasks.name: removeTrigger

uses.description: Deletes a trigger from the current zone outright, so it can never fire again there. This is stronger than switching it off, which only marks it used. Nothing happens if the zone has no trigger with that alias.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The alias of the trigger to delete from the zone.

tasks.officialDescription: Removes trigger of aliasID 'sValue' from the current zone.

tasks.name: setGlobalVarToTriggerProperty

uses.description: Reads one of a global trigger's own settings and stores it in a global variable as text. Use it to inspect how a trigger is configured — its area, its conditions, its flags — from a script. The value is written out the way the game would print it, and asking for a setting the trigger does not have stores False.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The name of the global variable to write the setting into.

required.name: strings[1]
required.description: The name of the global trigger to read from. Nothing is stored if no global trigger has that name.

required.name: strings[2]
required.description: The name of the trigger setting to read, spelled exactly as it is written in trigger data.

uses.description: Reads one of a global trigger's own settings and stores it in a global variable, with the trigger name and the setting name packed into a single comma-separated value. This is the form to use as a trigger effect, where only two strings are available. Asking for a setting the trigger does not have stores False.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The name of the global variable to write the setting into.

required.name: strings[1]
required.description: The global trigger's name and the setting name, separated by a comma, such as "tEnterZone,onlyExecuteOnce". Spaces are stripped. Because it contains a comma it cannot be written inside a taskString.

uses.description: Reads one of the current zone's triggers' own settings and stores it in a global variable as text. The trigger is picked by its number, or the one currently running can be inspected instead, which lets a trigger read its own configuration. Asking for a setting the trigger does not have stores False.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The name of the global variable to write the setting into.

required.name: strings[1]
required.description: The name of the trigger setting to read, spelled exactly as it is written in trigger data. It must not contain a comma, or the task looks up a global trigger instead.

optional.name: floats[0]
optional.description: The number of the trigger in the current zone to read. Defaults to 0, the zone's first trigger; any negative value reads the trigger that is currently running instead.

tasks.officialDescription: Sets gVar 'sValue' to the property 'sValue2' of a trigger in the current zone whose numID is 'fValue'. If sValue2 is 'aliasID,property', then it will instead set the property from the global trigger whose 'aliasID' matches, even if fValue is set. If fValue is negative, gets the property from the currently executing trigger, if it exists. Result is an empty string if no trigger was found.

tasks.name: setGlobalVar_toTriggerNumIDSearch

uses.description: Hunts through the current zone's triggers for one that matches a set of filters and stores its number in a global variable, or -1 if nothing matches. Triggers can be narrowed down by whether they can still fire, by whether their area covers a given tile, and by either the exact text of their requirement condition or the presence of a particular effect. Later matches can be reached by skipping the first few.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The name of the global variable that receives the found trigger's number, or -1 if nothing matched.

optional.name: strings[1]
optional.description: What to match against: with the effect-search flag set, the ID of an effect the trigger must carry; otherwise the exact text of the trigger's requirement condition, with spaces ignored. Defaults to empty, which matches every trigger.

optional.name: floats[0]
optional.description: How many matches to skip before settling on one, so 1 finds the second match. Defaults to 0, the first match.

optional.name: bools[0]
optional.description: When true the search looks for a trigger carrying an effect with the given ID instead of matching its requirement condition. Defaults to false.

optional.name: bools[1]
optional.description: When true the search is inverted to consider only triggers that currently cannot fire, rather than only those that can. Defaults to false. Supplying it requires the first flag to be supplied as well.

optional.name: tileCoords[0]
optional.description: Only consider triggers whose area covers this tile. If its x is negative the area check is skipped entirely; the tile is pulled inside the map bounds first.

tasks.officialDescription: Sets gVar 'sValue' to the numID of the 'fValue'-th (starting at 0) active trigger at X,Y, or the entire current zone if X,Y is not set, that matches a check set in 'sValue2'. If b1 is false, the check is for if the fReq of the trigger matches sValue2. If b1 is true, the check is for if the effectID in sValue2 is used in any trigger effect. If b2, only checks disabled triggers. Result is -1 if no triggers found.

tasks.name: setGlobalVar_toTriggerNumID

uses.description: Looks up one of the current zone's triggers by its alias and stores its number in a global variable, or -1 if no trigger has that alias. Numbers are what the enable, disable and fire tasks take when a trigger has no alias of its own, so this bridges between the two.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The name of the global variable that receives the trigger's number, or -1 if nothing matched.

required.name: strings[1]
required.description: The alias of the trigger in the current zone to look up. Leaving it empty stores the currently running trigger's number instead.

optional.name: floats[0]
optional.description: Must not be negative for this form; a negative value stores the currently running trigger's number instead. Defaults to 0.

uses.description: Stores the number of the trigger that is currently running in a global variable, which is how a trigger finds out its own number so it can switch itself off or on again later. If no trigger is running, -1 is stored.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The name of the global variable that receives the running trigger's number, or -1 if none is running.

optional.name: floats[0]
optional.description: Any negative value selects this form even when a trigger alias is given. Defaults to 0, which selects it only when no alias is supplied.

tasks.officialDescription: Sets gVar 'sValue' to the numID of the trigger in the current zone that has an aliasID matching 'sValue2'. If fValue is negative or sValue2 is blank, sets gVar to the currently executing trigger numID, if there is one. Result is -1 if no triggers found.

tasks.name: setGlobalVar_toTriggerAliasID

uses.description: Looks up one of the current zone's triggers by its number and stores its alias in a global variable, or an empty value if the trigger has none or does not exist. Giving a negative number stores the alias of the trigger that is currently running instead, which is how a trigger learns its own name.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The name of the global variable that receives the trigger's alias, or an empty value if nothing matched.

optional.name: floats[0]
optional.description: The number of the trigger in the current zone to look up. Defaults to 0, the zone's first trigger; any negative value reads the trigger that is currently running instead.

tasks.officialDescription: Sets gVar 'sValue' to the aliasID of the trigger in the current zone that has 'fValue' as its numID. If fValue is negative, sets gVar to the currently executing trigger aliasID, if there is one. Sets a blank string if the trigger doesn't have an aliasID set or isn't found.

tasks.name: specialSpawn

uses.description: Runs one of the game's special spawn rules over the whole current zone, sprinkling whatever it describes across the map — scattered rubble, wandering wildlife, patches of undergrowth and the like. Depending on the rule it either walks every tile in turn or picks a number of random tiles based on its chance setting. This is the same machinery that dresses a procedurally generated map.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The ID of the special spawn rule to apply across the zone.

tasks.officialDescription: Applies specialSpawn 'sValue' to the zone.

tasks.name: spawn

uses.description: Creates a new copy of a named actor prefab and drops it into the zone as a fresh actor with a unique ID. The copy is given a facing, has its stat modifiers rebuilt, and can be told to play an animation the moment it appears. Prefabs are actor definitions the game keeps ready to clone, and nothing happens if the name matches neither a prefab nor a spawn group.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The name of the actor prefab to clone. If it is not a prefab, the value is tried as a spawn group instead.

optional.name: strings[1]
optional.description: An animation the new actor plays as soon as it appears. Defaults to none.

optional.name: floats[0]
optional.description: The direction the new actor faces, in degrees. Defaults to 0.

optional.name: bools[0]
optional.description: When true the new actor keeps the prefab's own name as its ID instead of being given a unique one, which lets other tasks find it by that exact name but breaks if two are spawned. Defaults to false.

optional.name: tileCoords[0]
optional.description: The tile the actor is placed on. If omitted it defaults to (-1,-1), which instead drops the actor on a random free tile inside the area of the trigger that fired this task.

uses.description: Spawns a whole group of actors from a named spawn definition, choosing which and how many to create so the group's strength roughly matches the party's, then scattering them over free tiles. Each one is turned to face something sensible, has its stat modifiers rebuilt, and appears with the spawn definition's own effect. Nothing happens if the group cannot be built or there is nowhere to put them.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The ID of the spawn definition to draw the group from. If it is an actor prefab name instead, a single prefab copy is created.

optional.name: strings[1]
optional.description: The group name within the spawn definition to spawn, which also acts as the name used to stop the same group spawning twice. Defaults to the spawn definition's own ID.

optional.name: floats[0]
optional.description: Added to the strength the group is built to match, on top of the party's own strength and the game's spawn modifiers. Defaults to 0, which matches the party.

optional.name: bools[0]
optional.description: When true every spawned actor turns to face the middle of the area they were placed in, rather than facing the player or a random way. Defaults to false.

optional.name: bools[1]
optional.description: When true the spawned actors turn to face the player even when they were scattered across the trigger area rather than placed at a tile. Defaults to false. Supplying it requires the first flag to be supplied as well.

optional.name: tileCoords[0]
optional.description: The tile the group is gathered around; they spread out into a strip beside it. If omitted it defaults to (-1,-1), which scatters them across the area of the trigger that fired this task and leaves them facing random directions.

tasks.officialDescription: Creates SpawnData 'sValue'. (Executes 'spawn_actorPrefab' instead if sValue matches an actorPrefab ID.) 'sValue2' is the groupID. Groups won't spawn if actors of groupID already exist. NOTE: group spawns in random spots IN TRIGGER AREA, unless X,Y specified. fValue = group power level mod. bValue1 = group face toward trigger area center.

optional.name: bools[0]

optional.name: tileCoords[0]
optional.description: The tile the actor is placed on. If omitted it defaults to (-1,-1), which instead drops the actor on a random free tile inside the area of the trigger that fired this task.

required.description: The ID of the spawn definition to draw the group from. If it is an actor prefab name instead, a single prefab copy is created.

optional.name: strings[1]
optional.description: The group name within the spawn definition to spawn, which also acts as the name used to stop the same group spawning twice. Defaults to the spawn definition's own ID.

optional.name: floats[0]
optional.description: Added to the strength the group is built to match, on top of the party's own strength and the game's spawn modifiers. Defaults to 0, which matches the party.

tasks.officialDescription: Creates actorPrefab 'sValue'at X,Y. 'sValue2' specifies an animation to use when spawning. fValue = facingRot. bValue1 = use actorPrefab ID exactly (instead of zone-specific actorID).

tasks.name: spawn_actorPrefab_point

The destination is given as a numbered travel point rather than raw coordinates.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The name of the actor prefab to clone. If it is not a prefab, the value is tried as a spawn group instead.

required.name: tileCoords[0]
required.description: Its x is a travel-point number and its y a travel-point set; the actor is placed on that travel point and turned to face the way it points. It must be supplied, since there is no valid travel point numbered -1.

optional.name: strings[1]
optional.description: An animation the new actor plays as soon as it appears. Defaults to none.

optional.name: floats[0]
optional.description: The direction the new actor faces, in degrees. Defaults to 0.

optional.description: When true the new actor keeps the prefab's own name as its ID instead of being given a unique one, which lets other tasks find it by that exact name but breaks if two are spawned. Defaults to false.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The ID of the spawn definition to draw the group from. If it is an actor prefab name instead, a single prefab copy is created.

optional.name: strings[1]
optional.description: The group name within the spawn definition to spawn, which also acts as the name used to stop the same group spawning twice. Defaults to the spawn definition's own ID.
