optional.description: Its x is a travel-point number and its y a travel-point set; the group is gathered at that travel point facing the way it points. If omitted it defaults to (-1,-1), which scatters them across the area of the trigger that fired this task instead.

tasks.officialDescription: As 'spawn_actorPrefab', except X specifies what travelPoint to use, and Y specifies which set of travelPoints to use (0 red, 1 blue, 2 green, 3 brown).

tasks.name: spawn_g

uses.description: Spawns a group of actors from whichever spawn definition a global variable currently names, so the group can be chosen at runtime rather than fixed when the mod is written. Everything else behaves as an ordinary group spawn: the group is built to roughly match the party's strength and scattered over free tiles. Nothing happens if the variable's contents name no spawn definition.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The name of the global variable holding the ID of the spawn definition to use. Its contents, not this name, choose the group.

optional.name: strings[1]
optional.description: The group name within the spawn definition to spawn. Defaults to empty, which uses the spawn definition's own ID.

optional.name: floats[0]
optional.description: Added to the strength the group is built to match, on top of the party's own strength. Defaults to 0.

optional.name: bools[0]
optional.description: When true every spawned actor turns to face the middle of the area they were placed in. Defaults to false.

optional.name: bools[1]
optional.description: When true the spawned actors turn to face the player even when scattered across the trigger area. Defaults to false. Supplying it requires the first flag to be supplied as well.

optional.name: tileCoords[0]
optional.description: The tile the group is gathered around. If omitted it defaults to (-1,-1), which scatters them across the area of the trigger that fired this task.

tasks.officialDescription: Same as 'spawn', but sValue is a globalVar to use as the spawnData.

tasks.name: spawn_g_nearPlayer

uses.description: Spawns a group of actors from whichever spawn definition a global variable currently names, placing them in the three-by-three block of tiles centred on the player rather than anywhere in the trigger's area. This is the ambush spawn: enemies appear right on top of the party. They can instead be placed three tiles behind the player, so they appear at the party's back.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The name of the global variable holding the ID of the spawn definition to use. Its contents, not this name, choose the group.

optional.name: strings[1]
optional.description: The group name within the spawn definition to spawn. Defaults to empty, which uses the spawn definition's own ID.

optional.name: floats[0]
optional.description: Added to the strength the group is built to match, on top of the party's own strength. Defaults to 0.

optional.name: bools[0]
optional.description: When true every spawned actor turns to face the middle of the block they were placed in. Defaults to false.

optional.name: bools[1]
optional.description: When true the block is centred three tiles behind the player instead of on them, so the group appears at the party's back. Defaults to false. Supplying it requires the first flag to be supplied as well.

optional.name: tileCoords[0]
optional.description: Passed along to the underlying spawn as a tile to gather at, which then overrides the block around the player. If omitted it defaults to (-1,-1), which keeps the group around the player.

tasks.officialDescription: Same as 'spawn', but sValue is a globalVar to use as the spawnData, and the group is placed near the player. If b2, group is placed roughly 3 tiles behind the player.

tasks.name: spawn_actorPrefab_point_specialZone

uses.description: Creates a new copy of a named actor prefab and places it inside the loaded special zone — the separate map used for a boarded ship's interior — on one of that zone's numbered travel points, facing the way the point is turned. The new actor arrives fully healed, with any charging action and status effects cleared, and can play an animation as it appears. Nothing happens if no special zone is loaded, the name is not a prefab, or the travel point does not exist.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The name of the actor prefab to clone into the special zone.

required.name: strings[1]
required.description: An animation the new actor plays as soon as it appears. Leave it empty for none, but the slot must still be supplied.

required.name: bools[0]
required.description: When true the new actor keeps the prefab's own name as its ID instead of being given a unique one. The slot must be supplied.

required.name: tileCoords[0]
required.description: Its x is which travel point of the set to use, counted in the order they were found, and its y is the travel point set. It must be supplied, since there is no travel point numbered -1.

tasks.officialDescription: PROBABLY DO NOT USE. Adds a copy of actorPrefab 'sValue' to the current specialZone, on the xValue'th travelPoint of travelPoint set yValue.

tasks.name: spawn_location

uses.description: Populates the town or port the party is currently inside with its own regular inhabitants, drawn from the spawn groups that location lists, and stands them on the location's designated townsfolk spots. Wealthier locations get one or two extra groups. If the player owns a home here, the port's own extra scenery spawns are laid down as well.

tasks.officialDescription: Spawns actorPrefabs from the current location's auto_spawnDataID list, up the a maximum based on the current wealthLevel. Places them on the first unoccupied travelPoint set B item.

tasks.name: spawn_onItem

uses.description: Spawns a group of actors from a named spawn definition and stands each of them on a tile that holds an item with a chosen special property, which is how spawn markers placed in the map data decide where enemies appear. The group is built to roughly match the party's strength and the tiles are picked at random among the marked ones. All of them are made to give experience when defeated, and the spawn definition's own effect plays on each.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The ID of the spawn definition to draw the group from. Nothing happens if no such definition exists.

optional.name: strings[1]
optional.description: The special property a tile's item must carry for actors to be placed there, given by name or by its number. Defaults to no property, which places them anywhere.

optional.name: floats[0]
optional.description: Added to the strength the group is built to match, on top of the party's own strength and the game's spawn modifiers. Defaults to 0.

optional.name: bools[0]
optional.description: When true the group is spawned even if a group of the same name already exists in the world, allowing duplicates. Defaults to false, which skips the spawn in that case.

optional.name: tileCoords[0]
optional.description: A tile every spawned actor turns to face. If omitted it defaults to (-1,-1) and they keep the facing the spawn gave them.

tasks.officialDescription: Creates SpawnData 'sValue' actors on items with 'sValue2' specialProperty. fValue = group power level mod. If bValue1, can spawn even if group is already extant. Actors look at XY if specified.

tasks.name: spawn_seamonster

uses.description: Summons a sea monster fleet in the deep water near the actor the task is running on, gathering the spawned creatures into a single hostile fleet with cargo of their own. It only works if that actor is on or beside deep water and there is open deep water within reach. With no group named, the nearest monster beacon within fifty tiles decides which monster appears and is consumed in the process; failing that the default monster is used.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The ID of the spawn definition to draw the monsters from. Leave it empty to let the nearest monster beacon choose, falling back to the default sea monster.

optional.name: floats[0]
optional.description: Added to the strength the monster group is built to match. Defaults to 0.

tasks.officialDescription: Spawns a sea monster using spawnData 'sValue'. fValue specifies the desiredPowerLevel. If sValue is an empty string, finds the closest monsterBeacon item and uses 'sm' + its quantity as the spawnData ID.

tasks.name: spawn_fleet

uses.description: Spawns a whole fleet of ships from a named spawn definition and puts it on the world map, complete with a faction, a commodore, cargo drawn from that faction's trade and its own sailing behaviour. Use it to place patrols, merchant convoys and raiders. The task fails outright if the spawn definition does not exist.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The ID of the spawn definition describing the fleet's ships. It must exist or the task fails.

required.name: strings[1]
required.description: The ID of the actor to serve as the fleet's commodore. Leave it empty for none, but the slot must still be supplied.

optional.name: floats[0]
optional.description: Added to the strength the fleet is built to match. Defaults to 0.

optional.name: bools[0]
optional.description: When true the fleet is a merchant convoy rather than a fighting force. Defaults to false.

optional.name: bools[1]
optional.description: When true the fleet is an elite one, which affects how it is presented and crewed. Defaults to false. Supplying it requires the first flag to be supplied as well.

optional.name: tileCoords[0]
optional.description: The tile the fleet is placed on. If omitted it defaults to (-1,-1), leaving the fleet to be positioned by its own spawning rules.

tasks.officialDescription: Spawns a battle fleet in the current zone using spawnData 'sValue' at TC X,Y with the commodoreID set in sValue2. fValue sets the fleetPowerLevelMod. If b1, is a merchant fleet instead. If b2, is elite.

tasks.name: spawn_corpse

uses.description: Places the body of one of the party's fallen members into the zone, picked at random from those not already placed. At most two bodies can be laid out this way at a time, and the game remembers which ones so the same body is not placed twice. It is used to strew a battlefield or a graveyard with the party's own dead.

optional.name: tileCoords[0]
optional.description: The tile the body is placed on. If omitted it defaults to (-1,-1), which puts it on a free tile in the middle of the area of the trigger that fired this task.

tasks.officialDescription: Spawns a random corpse from partyActors_corpse either at XY or in the centermost occupiable tile in the trigger area.

tasks.name: talk

uses.description: Opens a conversation, either with a named actor or with nobody in particular. Naming an actor present in the world starts their dialog and points the camera between them and the player; leaving it empty or naming no one instead shows a plain speech box with no speaker, using the first value as the name to display above it. A specific dialog node can be forced instead of whatever the actor would normally say.

optional.name: strings[0]
optional.description: The ID of the actor to talk to. If it is empty or names no one present, a speaker-less speech box is shown instead and this value is used as the name displayed above it.

optional.name: strings[1]
optional.description: The dialog node to start from, overriding whatever the actor would normally say. Defaults to empty, which uses the actor's own dialog; for a speaker-less box it must be supplied or nothing happens.

optional.name: bools[0]
optional.description: When true the camera is not moved to sit between the player and the actor being talked to. Defaults to false. It has no effect on a speaker-less speech box.

optional.name: bools[1]
optional.description: When true a speaker-less speech box is stretched to nearly the full height of the screen, which suits a long passage of narration. Defaults to false. Supplying it requires the first flag to be supplied as well.

optional.name: tileCoords[0]
optional.description: Its y sets the height in pixels of a speaker-less speech box. If omitted, or zero or less, the box uses its normal height. Its x is not used.

tasks.officialDescription: Enter dialog with actor 'sValue'. 'sValue2' specifies dialogNode if assigned. If bValue1, dialog is centered on speaker. If bValue2, makes dialog fullscreen.

tasks.name: tryDialog

uses.description: Looks for a conversation registered against a named slot whose requirement currently passes, and starts the first one that qualifies. This is how several mods or story stages can each offer their own version of the same scene and the game picks whichever applies. A registered entry with no lines of its own simply runs its effects instead of opening a window, and nothing happens when nothing qualifies.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The name of the slot to look up registered conversations for.

optional.name: tileCoords[0]
optional.description: If a conversation did start, the camera is pointed at this tile and pinned there. If omitted it defaults to (-1,-1) and the camera is left alone.

tasks.officialDescription: Checks for any dialogOverrides for nodeID sValue.

tasks.name: tryDialog_commodore

uses.description: Looks for a conversation registered against a named slot whose requirement currently passes and starts the first one that qualifies, then swings the camera onto the enemy fleet's flagship and pops an exclamation mark over it. This is the hail from an approaching hostile fleet. Nothing special happens to the camera if no conversation started or there is no enemy fleet.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The name of the slot to look up registered conversations for.

tasks.officialDescription: DO NOT USE. Used specifically for dialog with an enemyFleet during fleet combat.

tasks.name: exitDialog

uses.description: Closes the conversation window and hands control back to the player, returning the game to ordinary walking-around mode. It only does anything while a conversation is actually open. Use it to end a scene from inside a dialog.

tasks.officialDescription: Exits dialog mode.

tasks.name: attractAttention

uses.description: Makes a noise at a tile that nearby actors notice: everyone within range turns to look toward it, and their AI scripts receive an attention signal they can react to. Actors only notice a noise made on their own side of a roof, so a sound indoors does not carry outside. Actors with no wits, or those locked into a script, ignore it.

required.name: tileCoords[0]
required.description: The tile the noise comes from. Its x must not be -1, or the noise comes from the actor the task is running on instead.

optional.name: floats[0]
optional.description: How far the noise carries, in tiles. Defaults to 12.

uses.description: Makes a noise at the tile of the actor the task is running on, so nearby actors turn to look at them and their AI scripts receive an attention signal. It carries twelve tiles and, as usual, does not cross between indoors and outdoors. It can optionally reach even actors who would normally ignore it.

optional.name: bools[0]
optional.description: When true even actors that are unable to act, locked into a script, witless, or on the other side of a roof are made to look. Defaults to false.

tasks.officialDescription: All actors (within fValue if specified) turn to face X,Y. If bValue1, works on all actors.

tasks.name: attractAttentionToPlayer

uses.description: Makes a noise at the player's own tile, so nearby actors turn to look at the party and their AI scripts receive an attention signal they can react to. Use it to blow the party's cover deliberately. It can optionally reach even actors who would normally ignore it.

optional.name: floats[0]
optional.description: How far the noise carries, in tiles. Defaults to 12.

optional.name: bools[0]
optional.description: When true even actors that are unable to act, locked into a script, witless, or on the other side of a roof are made to look. Defaults to false.

tasks.officialDescription: All actors (within fValue if specified) turn to face the player. If bValue1, works on all actors.

tasks.name: executeDialogEffect

uses.description: Runs a dialog effect exactly as though a conversation had invoked it: the name is tried first as a global trigger, then as one of the current zone's triggers, and finally run as a task in its own right. The actor the task is running on stands in as the one being talked to, so effects that act on the talker reach them. A dialog node can be named for effects that need to know which conversation they came from.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The effect to run: a global trigger name, a zone trigger alias, or a whole task written as one comma-separated value.

required.name: strings[1]
required.description: The dialog node the effect should behave as though it came from, which decides the node-named global variables the effect reads and writes. Leave it empty if the effect does not care, but the slot must still be supplied.

optional.name: floats[0]
optional.description: A number handed to the effect, for effects that take one. Defaults to 0.

tasks.officialDescription: Executes special dialog effect 'sValue', using 'sValue2' dialogNode (optional), and passing in fValue (optional).

tasks.name: loadSpecialZone

uses.description: Loads a second map on top of the current one as a special zone — the layer used for a ship floating on the sea, a moving platform, or a structure that slides about independently of the terrain — and places it at a chosen spot. The layer keeps its own tiles, items and actors and can be scaled, moved and later merged down into the map beneath. Loading a new one replaces whatever special zone was already loaded. The position is given in whole tiles.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The ID of the zone to load as the overlaid layer.

optional.name: strings[1]
optional.description: The scale to draw the layer at, written as text; anything that does not read as a number is ignored. Defaults to full size. Because a plain number written in a taskString would be taken as a number rather than a string, it has to be forced into a text slot.

optional.name: floats[0]
optional.description: A depth adjustment deciding how far in front of or behind the map the layer is drawn. Defaults to none.

optional.name: bools[0]
optional.description: When true the layer is only drawn while roofs are being drawn, which hides it when the camera goes indoors. Defaults to false.

optional.name: tileCoords[0]
optional.description: Where to place the layer, in whole tiles from the map's origin. If omitted it defaults to (-1,-1), placing it one tile up and left of the origin.

tasks.officialDescription: Loads in zone 'sValue' as a non-interactive overlay at X,Y. fValue = depthMod. sValue2 = scale, if specified (default to 1). If bValue1, only draws zone if roofs are drawn.

tasks.name: loadSpecialZone_precision

uses.description: Loads a second map on top of the current one as a special zone — the layer used for a ship floating on the sea, a moving platform, or a structure that slides about independently of the terrain — and places it at a chosen spot. The layer keeps its own tiles, items and actors and can be scaled, moved and later merged down into the map beneath. Loading a new one replaces whatever special zone was already loaded. The position is given in hundredths of a tile, for fine placement.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The ID of the zone to load as the overlaid layer.

optional.name: strings[1]
optional.description: The scale to draw the layer at, written as text; anything that does not read as a number is ignored. Defaults to full size. Because a plain number written in a taskString would be taken as a number rather than a string, it has to be forced into a text slot.

optional.name: floats[0]
optional.description: A depth adjustment deciding how far in front of or behind the map the layer is drawn. Defaults to none.

optional.name: bools[0]
optional.description: When true the layer is only drawn while roofs are being drawn, which hides it when the camera goes indoors. Defaults to false.

optional.name: tileCoords[0]
optional.description: Where to place the layer, in hundredths of a tile from the map's origin, so 250 means two and a half tiles. If omitted it defaults to (-1,-1), which is a hundredth of a tile up and left of the origin.

tasks.officialDescription: Same as 'loadSpecialZone' task, but X,Y is divided by 100 to get a precise tile position.

tasks.name: loadSpecialZone_playerFlagship

uses.description: Loads a second map on top of the current one as a special zone — the layer used for a ship floating on the sea, a moving platform, or a structure that slides about independently of the terrain — and places it at a chosen spot. The layer keeps its own tiles, items and actors and can be scaled, moved and later merged down into the map beneath. Loading a new one replaces whatever special zone was already loaded. The layer is always the interior of the player's own flagship, so no zone needs naming. The position is given in whole tiles.

optional.name: strings[1]
optional.description: The scale to draw the layer at, written as text; anything that does not read as a number is ignored. Defaults to full size. Because a plain number written in a taskString would be taken as a number rather than a string, it has to be forced into a text slot. Reaching this slot means filling the first string slot too, with anything at all.

optional.name: floats[0]
optional.description: A depth adjustment deciding how far in front of or behind the map the layer is drawn. Defaults to none.

optional.name: bools[0]
optional.description: When true the layer is only drawn while roofs are being drawn, which hides it when the camera goes indoors. Defaults to false.

optional.name: tileCoords[0]
optional.description: Where to place the layer, in whole tiles from the map's origin. If omitted it defaults to (-1,-1), placing it one tile up and left of the origin.

tasks.officialDescription: As 'loadSpecialZone', but disregards 'sValue' and loads the player's flagship bz instead.

tasks.name: loadSpecialZone_playerFlagship_precision

uses.description: Loads a second map on top of the current one as a special zone — the layer used for a ship floating on the sea, a moving platform, or a structure that slides about independently of the terrain — and places it at a chosen spot. The layer keeps its own tiles, items and actors and can be scaled, moved and later merged down into the map beneath. Loading a new one replaces whatever special zone was already loaded. The layer is always the interior of the player's own flagship, so no zone needs naming. The position is given in hundredths of a tile, for fine placement.

optional.name: strings[1]
optional.description: The scale to draw the layer at, written as text; anything that does not read as a number is ignored. Defaults to full size. Because a plain number written in a taskString would be taken as a number rather than a string, it has to be forced into a text slot. Reaching this slot means filling the first string slot too, with anything at all.

optional.name: floats[0]
optional.description: A depth adjustment deciding how far in front of or behind the map the layer is drawn. Defaults to none.

optional.name: bools[0]
optional.description: When true the layer is only drawn while roofs are being drawn, which hides it when the camera goes indoors. Defaults to false.

optional.name: tileCoords[0]
optional.description: Where to place the layer, in hundredths of a tile from the map's origin, so 250 means two and a half tiles. If omitted it defaults to (-1,-1), which is a hundredth of a tile up and left of the origin.

tasks.officialDescription: Same as 'loadSpecialZone_playerFlagship' task, but X,Y is divided by 100 to get a precise tile position.

tasks.name: moveSpecialZone

uses.description: Sends the loaded special zone layer drifting to a new position, so a ship glides across the water or a platform slides into place. The layer travels there over time rather than jumping, and can be told to ease in and out of the motion or to bounce back to where it started. The destination is given in whole tiles.

optional.name: floats[0]
optional.description: How fast the layer travels; larger is faster. Defaults to leaving the current speed alone.

optional.name: bools[0]
optional.description: When true the layer eases into and out of the movement instead of travelling at a constant rate. Defaults to false.

optional.name: bools[1]
optional.description: When true the layer travels back to where it started once it arrives, giving a there-and-back drift. Defaults to false. Supplying it requires the first flag to be supplied as well.

optional.name: tileCoords[0]
optional.description: Where the layer travels to, in whole tiles from the map's origin. If omitted it defaults to (-1,-1).

tasks.officialDescription: Moves specialZone to X,Y at fValue speed. Eases if bValue1.

tasks.name: moveSpecialZone_precision

uses.description: Sends the loaded special zone layer drifting to a new position, so a ship glides across the water or a platform slides into place. The layer travels there over time rather than jumping, and can be told to ease in and out of the motion or to bounce back to where it started. The destination is given in hundredths of a tile, for fine placement.

optional.name: floats[0]
optional.description: How fast the layer travels; larger is faster. Defaults to leaving the current speed alone.

optional.name: bools[0]
optional.description: When true the layer eases into and out of the movement instead of travelling at a constant rate. Defaults to false.

optional.name: bools[1]
optional.description: When true the layer travels back to where it started once it arrives, giving a there-and-back drift. Defaults to false. Supplying it requires the first flag to be supplied as well.

optional.name: tileCoords[0]
optional.description: Where the layer travels to, in hundredths of a tile from the map's origin. If omitted it defaults to (-1,-1).

tasks.officialDescription: Same as 'moveSpecialZone' task, but X,Y is divided by 100 to get a precise tile position.

tasks.name: scaleSpecialZone

uses.description: Grows or shrinks the loaded special zone layer toward a new size over time, so a ship appears to sail closer or further away. The layer eases toward the size rather than snapping to it. Both the target size and the rate are needed.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The size to grow or shrink toward, where 1 is full size, written as text. Anything that does not read as a number leaves the size alone. Because a plain number written in a taskString would be taken as a number rather than a string, it has to be forced into a text slot.

required.name: floats[0]
required.description: How fast the layer changes size; larger is faster. Values of zero or less leave the current rate alone, but the value must be supplied.

tasks.officialDescription: Scale specialZone to sValue scale at fValue speed.

tasks.name: mergeSpecialZone

uses.description: Stamps the loaded special zone layer down onto the map beneath it, so its terrain and contents become part of the real map at whatever position it had reached. Use it when a ship docks or a structure settles into place and should stop being a separate moving layer. The layer's position is rounded to whole tiles first.

optional.name: bools[0]
optional.description: When true the items already on the map underneath are kept; when false they are destroyed where the layer covers them. Defaults to false.

optional.name: tileCoords[0]
optional.description: Where to place the layer before stamping it down, in whole tiles. If its x is -1 the layer is stamped wherever it currently sits.

tasks.officialDescription: Overwrites area with specialZone (excluding transparent/BG terrain). Sets specialZone at X,Y if specified. If b1, doesn't overwrite existing items.

tasks.name: barracksLineup

uses.description: Lines up every party member and everyone waiting in the barracks in neat rows, all facing east, so the player can walk along and inspect the whole roster. Anyone not currently in the zone is brought into it. Party members are nudged forward a fraction so they can be told apart from the reserves standing behind them.

required.name: floats[0]
required.description: How many tiles apart to stand them along each row. Values of zero or less are treated as 1, but the value must be supplied.

optional.name: tileCoords[0]
optional.description: The tile the first row starts at. If omitted it defaults to (-1,-1), starting the line-up one tile up and left of the map origin.

tasks.officialDescription: DO NOT USE.

tasks.name: unlockExtras

uses.description: Unlocks the game's extra options and extra playable races for good, adding every actor type flagged as player-unlockable to the list the player can pick from at character creation. The any-difficulty completion achievement is granted at the same time, and the settings file is written out so the unlock survives quitting.

tasks.officialDescription: Sets extra races and extra options to be unlocked and saves the config.ini file.

tasks.name: trySetAchievement

uses.description: Records an achievement as earned, both in the save's own flags and, when the game is running through Steam, as a real platform achievement that is uploaded straight away. Outside Steam only the save flag is set. The flag is a plain global variable, so mods can read it back like any other.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The achievement's name. It is both the global variable set to 1 and the platform achievement identifier, so it must match the achievement as registered with the platform for the real unlock to happen.

tasks.officialDescription: Attempts to set Steam achievement sValue.

tasks.name: retro

uses.description: Flips the game's retro visuals mode on or off, changing the look of the presentation. Running it again switches back. It is a display toggle only and changes nothing about the world.

tasks.officialDescription: toggles Retro Visuals mode

tasks.name: resetLocations

uses.description: Throws away every location in the world and rebuilds the whole set from the game's and mods' location data. Anything a mod had changed about a location at runtime — its name, faction, stock, discovered state — is lost. This is a heavy reset used when location data itself has changed.

tasks.officialDescription: clears all data about the specified Location and reloads them from defaultLocations.txt (ex: resetloc port1)

tasks.name: refreshUndamagedShipZones

uses.description: Throws away the saved interiors of every ship in the player's fleet, so the next time anyone boards one it is rebuilt fresh from the ship's design. Use it after repairs, so battle damage and displaced furniture inside the hull are cleared. Nothing happens if the player has no fleet.

tasks.officialDescription: Deletes all saved boat zones from the current save file for every ship actor in the player's fleet.

tasks.name: boardActor

uses.description: Starts a boarding action: the party leaves the sea battle and is moved into the interior of a target ship, with a boarding timer running and the current music carried over. Both ships involved must actually be vessels. The player is briefly locked out of interacting while the interior loads.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The ID of the ship being boarded; its interior is the zone the party enters.

required.name: strings[1]
required.description: The ID of the ship the boarders come from.

tasks.officialDescription: sValue = target to board. sValue2 = boarder

tasks.name: endBoarding

uses.description: Ends a boarding action and takes the party back out of the boarded ship's interior, with the screen blacking out over the transition. It does nothing unless a boarding is actually in progress. A destination zone can be named to send the party somewhere other than where they came from.

optional.name: strings[0]
optional.description: The zone to return to instead of the one the boarding started from. Defaults to returning the usual way.

tasks.officialDescription: calls ZoneManager.I.returnFromBoardingZone()

tasks.name: enterFleetBattle

uses.description: Starts a fleet battle between two named ships, moving the fight onto the dedicated fleet-battle map. The party's position and the crew's experience are recorded first so they can be restored afterwards, and the enemy fleet is assembled around the target's flagship. Any saved copy of the battle map is thrown away so the fight starts clean.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The ID of the ship whose fleet is fought.

required.name: strings[1]
required.description: The ID of the second ship drawn into the battle. Leave it empty for none, but the slot must still be supplied.

uses.description: Starts a fleet battle around the ship the task is running on, working out the second party automatically from the nearest allied vessel within two tiles that shares its faction. The fight moves onto the dedicated fleet-battle map, and the party's position and crew experience are recorded first so they can be restored afterwards. The battle is recorded as one the player did not start.

tasks.officialDescription: sets gVars playerX & playerY to player pos. Enters new fleetBattle zone, bringing Player, sValue, and sValue2 Actors' fleets with them. Puts fleets on travel_point A,B,C respectively.

tasks.name: enterFleetBattle_player

uses.description: Starts a fleet battle between two named ships, moving the fight onto the dedicated fleet-battle map. The party's position and the crew's experience are recorded first so they can be restored afterwards, and the enemy fleet is assembled around the target's flagship. Any saved copy of the battle map is thrown away so the fight starts clean.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The ID of the ship whose fleet is fought.

required.name: strings[1]
required.description: The ID of the second ship drawn into the battle. Leave it empty for none, but the slot must still be supplied.

uses.description: Starts a fleet battle around the ship the task is running on, working out the second party automatically from the nearest allied vessel within two tiles that shares its faction. The fight moves onto the dedicated fleet-battle map, and the party's position and crew experience are recorded first so they can be restored afterwards. The battle is recorded as one the player started, which affects the fallout.

tasks.officialDescription: sets gVars playerX & playerY to player pos. Enters new fleetBattle zone, bringing Player, sValue, and sValue2 Actors' fleets with them. Puts fleets on travel_point A,B,C respectively. Sets the fleet battle as having been initiated by the player.

tasks.name: setDialogSpeed

uses.description: Changes how fast conversation text is typed out on screen, as a multiplier on the normal speed. Larger values race through the text and smaller values draw it out for a slow, weighty delivery. The setting is remembered in the save.

optional.name: floats[0]
optional.description: The text speed multiplier, where 1 is normal. Defaults to 1.

tasks.officialDescription: Sets the dialogSpeedMult game option to 'fValue'.

tasks.name: setMoney

uses.description: Sets the player's purse to the result of a formula, so the amount can depend on the party, the world state or anything else a formula can read. The answer is rounded down to a whole number of coins. This replaces the current amount rather than adding to it.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The formula worked out to give the new amount of money. Leaving it empty sets the money from a plain number instead.

uses.description: Sets the player's purse to a flat amount, replacing whatever they were carrying. Use it to bankrupt the party or hand them a fixed sum. The value is rounded down to a whole number of coins.

optional.name: floats[0]
optional.description: The new amount of money. Defaults to 0, which empties the purse.

tasks.officialDescription: Sets current money to fValue, or formula sValue.

tasks.name: enterCombat

uses.description: Starts a fight centred on a chosen tile, pulling in every actor within a radius of it and switching the game into turn-based combat. If an action is still resolving or the player is busy, the fight is held until they are free. Nothing happens in a zone where acting is disabled, and if a fight is already running the actors are simply added to it.

optional.name: strings[0]
optional.description: The ID of the actor treated as having started the fight, which decides who acts first and who is blamed for it. Defaults to nobody.

optional.name: floats[0]
optional.description: How far from the centre, in tiles, actors are pulled into the fight. Defaults to 18.

optional.name: tileCoords[0]
optional.description: The tile the battlefield is centred on. If omitted it defaults to (-1,-1), centring the battlefield off the map.

tasks.officialDescription: Enter combat at X,Y with radius 'fValue' (or default radius if unspecified). 'sValue' is which actor intiated combat, if any.

tasks.name: enterCombat_timer

uses.description: Starts a fight immediately with a battlefield large enough to swallow the whole map, and schedules an action to go off on a tile after a number of combat turns. This is the delayed-detonation setup: a bomb, a collapsing ceiling or a ritual that fires partway through the fight. The fight starts at once whether or not anything else was still resolving.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The ID of the action that goes off when the timer runs out.

optional.name: floats[0]
optional.description: How many combat turns to wait before the action goes off. Defaults to 0, which fires it at the first opportunity.

optional.name: tileCoords[0]
optional.description: The tile the battlefield is centred on and where the timed action goes off. If omitted it defaults to (-1,-1), off the map.

tasks.officialDescription: Enters combat at X,Y, with a radius of 999 and sets action 'sValue' to be executed at X,Y after 'fValue' actTime.

tasks.name: exitCombat

uses.description: Ends the fight in progress at once, whether or not either side has actually won, and returns the game to ordinary movement. Whether the party counts as victorious decides what rewards and consequences follow. It only does anything while a fight is actually running.

optional.name: bools[0]
optional.description: When true the fight ends as a defeat rather than a victory. Defaults to false, which ends it as a victory.

tasks.officialDescription: Exits combat

tasks.name: offerRest

uses.description: Asks the player whether they would like to rest here, and rests them if they agree. If any hostile actor is alive within fifteen tiles, or a timed hazard is about to go off, the player is told it is not safe instead and nothing happens. It only works while walking around, not in combat or menus.

tasks.officialDescription: Opens dialog box allowing player to rest and heal party, if nothing threatening is nearby.

tasks.name: advanceTimers

uses.description: Fast-forwards the zone's combat timers, firing anything already due and then ticking the clock forward a number of turns so slower timers come round. This is how a scene skips ahead through burning fires, ticking bombs and charging spells without the player taking turns. Timers on items that only advance while on screen are held back as usual.

required.name: floats[0]
required.description: How many turns to advance, used as both the minimum and the maximum, so exactly this many turns pass if there are timers to advance.

tasks.officialDescription: Advance all actTimers by fValue.

tasks.name: scoreScreen

uses.description: Puts up the end-of-run report: the party's coins are tallied away one clink at a time, every piece of special loot they carry is cashed in or converted into a permanent unlock, and the surviving members are shown with the experience they earned. The purse is emptied into the long-term reserves, the run's total value is recorded, and a successful run is counted toward the mission tally. The report is presented as a full-screen conversation.

tasks.officialDescription: Brings up score screen, converts consumables into cash.

tasks.name: setupGraveyard

uses.description: Lays out the party's permanently dead in rows as petrified statues, each standing on its own plinth, starting from a chosen tile and wrapping into new rows as it fills up. Each one drops what it was carrying, is healed and turned to face the same way, and stops being controllable. At most a hundred and twenty-two are laid out.

optional.name: tileCoords[0]
optional.description: The tile the first grave is placed at, with the rows running right and down from there. If omitted it defaults to (-1,-1), starting the rows one tile up and left of the map origin.

tasks.officialDescription: DO NOT USE.

tasks.name: endGame

uses.description: Ends the current game and returns to the main menu. If extra options or races were unlocked during this session, the unlock is applied a second later so it takes effect on the menu. Anything not already saved is lost.

tasks.officialDescription: Sends the player to the main menu.

tasks.name: handleDeaths

uses.description: Finishes off every actor in the zone that has been lying incapacitated with its dying timer run out, turning it from merely downed into permanently dead. Player-controlled characters get a drawn-out death scene, staggered so several deaths play one after another rather than at once; everyone else simply puffs into black smoke. Actors that cannot be revived, are already dead, or are not dying are left alone, and nothing happens while a death scene is already playing.

tasks.officialDescription: DO NOT USE. Updates 'dying' and 'dead' AVs for each actor in the current zone.

tasks.name: getResponse_combat

uses.description: Asks the actor the task is running on how it answers a demand to fight, weighing its confidence against the party's strength, its honour and aggression, how hostile you have made it, and how much it stands to lose. The answer is written in as the next node of the conversation this task came from, so the dialog continues straight into the reply the actor chose. Both sides' fighting strength are compared, and an actor of the same kind as the player is judged a little more generously.

required.name: floats[0]
required.description: How hostile the actor is toward the party, feeding into how likely it is to refuse. It must be supplied. If several numbers are given, only the last one is used.

tasks.officialDescription: DO NOT USE. Sets the currentDialogNode's nextNodeID to the response for combat. Used in auto dialog.

tasks.name: getResponse_peace

uses.description: Asks the actor the task is running on how it answers an offer of peace, weighing its confidence against the party's strength, its honour and aggression, how hostile you have made it, and how much it stands to lose. The answer is written in as the next node of the conversation this task came from, so the dialog continues straight into the reply the actor chose. Both sides' fighting strength are compared, and an actor of the same kind as the player is judged a little more generously.

required.name: floats[0]
required.description: How hostile the actor is toward the party, feeding into how likely it is to refuse. It must be supplied. If several numbers are given, only the last one is used.

tasks.officialDescription: DO NOT USE. Sets the currentDialogNode's nextNodeID to the response for wanting peace. Used in auto dialog.

tasks.name: getResponse_bribe

uses.description: Asks the actor the task is running on how it answers an offer of a bribe, weighing its confidence against the party's strength, its honour and aggression, how hostile you have made it, and how much it stands to lose. The answer is written in as the next node of the conversation this task came from, so the dialog continues straight into the reply the actor chose. Both sides' fighting strength are compared, and an actor of the same kind as the player is judged a little more generously.

required.name: floats[0]
required.description: How hostile the actor is toward the party, feeding into how likely it is to refuse. It must be supplied. If several numbers are given, only the last one is used.

tasks.officialDescription: DO NOT USE. Sets the currentDialogNode's nextNodeID to the response for being bribed. Used in auto dialog.

tasks.name: getBribeAmount

uses.description: Rewrites the first line of the conversation this task came from so it names the price of buying off the enemy, worked out from the fighting strength of the group the contextual actor belongs to. The bigger the enemy force, the larger the sum quoted. It only changes the wording; nothing is paid.

tasks.officialDescription: DO NOT USE. Sets the currentDialogNode's statements[0] to reflect a bribe amount used for auto dialog.

tasks.name: subtractBribeAmount

uses.description: Takes the bribe out of the player's purse and puts the coins into the contextual actor's own inventory, so the money really changes hands. The amount is worked out the same way the quoted price was, from the fighting strength of the group that actor belongs to. The player's purse can be driven negative if they cannot afford it.

tasks.officialDescription: DO NOT USE. Subtracts the bribe amount used for auto dialog from the player's gold.

tasks.name: add50gp

uses.description: Adds fifty coins to the player's purse. It is a fixed amount with nothing to configure. Use it for a small flat reward.

tasks.officialDescription: Gives 50 gold to the player.

tasks.name: addgp

uses.description: Adds coins to the player's purse, with the amount worked out from a formula so it can scale with the party, the world or a quest's difficulty. The result is rounded down to whole coins and the formula sees the player as its target.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The formula giving how many coins to add. Leaving it empty adds a flat number instead.

uses.description: Adds a flat number of coins to the player's purse. Use it for a fixed reward. Negative values take money away.

required.name: floats[0]
required.description: How many coins to add. It must be supplied, or nothing happens at all.

tasks.officialDescription: Gives 'fValue' gold to the player. If 'sValue' is set, it should be a formula, with the result of that formula being the amount to give.

tasks.name: subtractgp

uses.description: Takes coins out of the player's purse, with the amount worked out from a formula so a price can scale with the party, the world or how much they can afford. The result is rounded down to whole coins and the formula sees the player as its target. The purse can be driven negative.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The formula giving how many coins to take. Leaving it empty takes a flat number instead.

uses.description: Takes a flat number of coins out of the player's purse. Use it for a fixed price. The purse can be driven negative.

optional.name: floats[0]
optional.description: How many coins to take. Defaults to 0.

tasks.officialDescription: Removes 'fValue' gold from the player. If 'sValue' is set, it should be a formula, with the result of that formula being the amount to remove.

tasks.name: subtract10gp

uses.description: Takes 10 coins out of the player's purse. It is a fixed amount with nothing to configure, and the purse can be driven negative. Use it for a fixed price.

tasks.officialDescription: Subtracts 10 from the player's gold.

tasks.name: subtract5000gp

uses.description: Takes 5000 coins out of the player's purse. It is a fixed amount with nothing to configure, and the purse can be driven negative. Use it for a fixed price.

tasks.officialDescription: Subtracts 5,000 from the player's gold.

tasks.name: subtract10000gp

uses.description: Takes 10000 coins out of the player's purse. It is a fixed amount with nothing to configure, and the purse can be driven negative. Use it for a fixed price.

tasks.officialDescription: Subtracts 10,000 from the player's gold.

tasks.name: subtractAllgp

uses.description: Empties the player's purse completely, leaving them with nothing on hand. Money already in the long-term reserves or cargo is untouched. Use it when the party is robbed or has to hand everything over.

tasks.officialDescription: Sets the player's gold to 0.

tasks.name: giveGlobalVarGP

uses.description: Adds however many coins a global variable currently holds to the player's purse. This is how a reward worked out earlier and stashed in a variable gets paid out. The variable's value is rounded down to whole coins, and a negative value takes money away.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The name of the global variable holding the number of coins to add.

tasks.officialDescription: Adds the value set in 'sValue' globalVar of gold to the player.

tasks.name: enterSellMode

uses.description: Switches the game into trading mode and opens every party member's pack side by side, so the player can drag things out to sell them. Prices are shown on items while trading mode is on. This is the on-foot merchant view.

tasks.officialDescription: DO NOT USE. Opens player actor inventories and sets tradeMode=true.

tasks.name: openCargo

uses.description: Opens the ship's cargo hold window, as though the player had clicked the cargo button. Trading mode is not switched on, so this is for looking and rearranging rather than selling. Use it to show the hold during a scene.

tasks.officialDescription: Shows the player's cargo inventory window.

tasks.name: autobuy_food

uses.description: Spends the player's coins on as much food as will fit in the cargo hold, buying at the going rate and stowing it away in one step. It buys whichever is smaller: what the hold can take, or what they can afford. Use it for a resupply option that skips the shopping.

tasks.officialDescription: Forces the player to buy as much food as will fit into their cargo, or that they can afford, whichever is lower.

tasks.name: enterSellMode_cargo

uses.description: Switches the game into trading mode and opens the ship's cargo hold, so the player can sell what they are shipping. Prices are shown on items while trading mode is on. This is the harbour trade view.

tasks.officialDescription: DO NOT USE. Opens player cargo inventory and sets tradeMode=true.

tasks.name: enterSellMode_stash

uses.description: Switches the game into trading mode and opens the party's stash, so the player can sell what they have put away rather than what they are carrying. Prices are shown on items while trading mode is on.

tasks.officialDescription: DO NOT USE. Opens player stash inventory and sets tradeMode=true.

tasks.name: enterBuyMode

uses.description: Opens a shopping view against the actor the task is running on: their goods on the left and the party's stash on the right, with trading mode on so prices are shown. If that actor carries a dedicated shop container, its contents are offered and sorted for sale; otherwise their whole inventory is laid out around them. Controller and keyboard players are switched into item-picking mode.

tasks.officialDescription: Enters buy/sell mode with the currentActorTalkingTo (or current task actor if not in dialog).

tasks.name: enterBuyMode_location

uses.description: Opens a shopping view against the town or port the party is inside: its trade cargo on the left and the ship's own cargo hold on the right, with trading mode on so prices are shown. The location's stock is sorted for sale first. Nothing happens if the party is not inside a location.

tasks.officialDescription: Enters buy/sell mode for the current location's cargo inventory.

tasks.name: enterBuyMode_locationItems

uses.description: Opens a shopping view against the town or port the party is inside, offering its shop stock rather than its bulk trade goods, with the party's stash on the right. Trading mode is switched on so prices are shown, and the location's stock is sorted for sale first. Nothing happens if the party is not inside a location.

tasks.officialDescription: Enters buy/sell mode for the current location's stash inventory.

tasks.name: enterBuyMode_fleet

uses.description: Opens a shopping view against the fleet the actor the task is running on belongs to: that fleet's cargo on the left and the player's own cargo hold on the right, with trading mode on so prices are shown. This is the trade window for dealing with a merchant convoy at sea. The fleet's cargo is sorted for sale first.

tasks.officialDescription: Enters buy/sell mode with the fleet currentActorTalkingTo (or current task actor if not in dialog) belongs to.

tasks.name: setBuyPriceMult

uses.description: Sets the multiplier applied to prices while buying, so a shop can be made cheap or extortionate for the rest of the trade. A value of 1 is the normal price. It stays in force until something changes it or the conversation resets it.

required.name: floats[0]
required.description: The price multiplier, where 1 is the normal price.

tasks.officialDescription: Sets Globals.buyPriceMult to 'fValue'. Item prices are multiplied by this. Reset to 1 before and after dialog mode.

tasks.name: buyItem_confirmWindow

uses.description: Opens the quantity slider for buying a named item, letting the player choose how many to take before confirming. Once it closes, the cargo hold is opened if the item is a trade good and the stash otherwise, so they can see what they bought. A quantity of zero is treated as one.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The ID of the item type being bought.

required.name: floats[0]
required.description: How many the slider starts at; zero is treated as one. It must be supplied. If several numbers are given, only the last one is used.

tasks.officialDescription: DO NOT USE.

tasks.name: buyGoods_confirmWindow

uses.description: Opens the quantity slider for buying the trade good the current town or port deals in, letting the player choose how many barrels to take before confirming. A quantity of zero is treated as one. The party must be inside a location for there to be a trade good to buy.

required.name: floats[0]
required.description: How many the slider starts at; zero is treated as one. It must be supplied. If several numbers are given, only the last one is used.

tasks.officialDescription: DO NOT USE.

tasks.name: buyFood_fillCargo

uses.description: Buys exactly enough food to fill the ship's cargo hold to the brim and stows it, paying the base price for the lot. If the player cannot afford the whole amount, nothing at all is bought. This is the top-up-the-larder option.

tasks.officialDescription: Adds as much food as the player can hold to their cargo, if they can afford it, and subtracts the cost from their gold.

tasks.name: buyFood

uses.description: Buys a set number of units of food at the base price and stows them in the cargo hold. If the player cannot afford them, nothing is bought and no money changes hands. The hold's capacity is not checked.

required.name: floats[0]
required.description: How many units of food to buy. It must be supplied. If several numbers are given, only the last one is used.

tasks.officialDescription: Adds 'fValue' food to the player's cargo, if they can afford it, and subtracts the cost from their gold.

tasks.name: buyGoods

uses.description: Buys a set number of units of whatever trade good the current zone's town or port deals in, at the base price, and stows them in the cargo hold. If the player cannot afford them, nothing is bought. The hold's capacity is not checked.

required.name: floats[0]
required.description: How many units of the local trade good to buy. It must be supplied. If several numbers are given, only the last one is used.

tasks.officialDescription: Adds 'fValue' of the current location's tradeGood_itemTypeID to the player's cargo, if they can afford it, and subtracts the cost from their gold.

tasks.name: giveFood

uses.description: Puts a number of units of food straight into the ship's cargo hold for free. Use it for a gift or a resupply from a story event. The hold's capacity is not checked.

required.name: floats[0]
required.description: How many units of food to give. It must be supplied. If several numbers are given, only the last one is used.

tasks.officialDescription: Adds 'fValue' food to the player's cargo, if it can fit.

tasks.name: lose10Food

uses.description: Takes ten units of food out of the ship's cargo hold. It is a fixed amount with nothing to configure. Use it for a spoilage or theft event.

tasks.officialDescription: Removes 10 food from the player's cargo inventory.

tasks.name: removeCargo

uses.description: Takes a number of a named item out of the ship's cargo hold and destroys it. Use it to consume shipped goods on delivery. Nothing happens if the hold does not hold that item.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The ID of the item type to take out of the cargo hold.

optional.name: floats[0]
optional.description: How many to take. Defaults to 0.

tasks.officialDescription: Removes 'fValue' quantity of item ID 'sValue' from the player's cargo inventory.

tasks.name: removeCargo_g

uses.description: Takes a number of an item out of the ship's cargo hold, with the item chosen by whatever a global variable currently names. Use it when the goods to be delivered were decided at runtime. Nothing happens if the hold does not hold that item.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The name of the global variable holding the item type ID to remove. Its contents, not this name, choose the item.

optional.name: floats[0]
optional.description: How many to take. Defaults to 0.

tasks.officialDescription: Removes 'fValue' quantity of the item ID set in globalVar 'sValue' from the player's cargo inventory.

tasks.name: removeItem_g

uses.description: Takes a number of an item away from the party, with the item chosen by whatever a global variable currently names. Use it when a quest item decided at runtime has to be handed over. Nothing happens if the party does not have it.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The name of the global variable holding the item type ID to remove. Its contents, not this name, choose the item.

optional.name: floats[0]
optional.description: How many to take. Defaults to 0.

tasks.officialDescription: Removes 'fValue' quantity of the item ID set in globalVar 'sValue' from the player's available inventory. Tries to remove from the stash, cargo, and any crew inventories until the quantity is fully removed.

tasks.name: removeItemFromParty

uses.description: Takes a number of a named item away from the party. Use it when a quest item has to be handed over or consumed. Nothing happens if the party does not have it.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The ID of the item type to take from the party.

optional.name: floats[0]
optional.description: How many to take. Defaults to 0.

tasks.officialDescription: Removes 'fValue' quantity of item ID 'sValue' from the player's available inventory. Tries to remove from the stash, cargo, and any crew inventories until the quantity is fully removed.

tasks.name: refreshStatMods

uses.description: Recalculates every actor's stat bonuses from scratch — everyone in the zone, everyone in the party and everyone waiting in the barracks. Do this after changing equipment, abilities or classes behind the scenes, so the numbers on the character sheet catch up. Nothing else about them changes.

tasks.officialDescription: Resets all enemy stat multipliers, player stat modifiers, boat mods and day bonuses for every actor in the current zone.

tasks.name: grantXPShare_5percent

uses.description: Hands every party member and every reserve in the barracks a twentieth of the shared experience pool in each class, so characters who were not present still make progress. It only does anything while the shared-experience feature is switched on. Party members only receive it for classes with more than a hundred experience banked, and the award ignores fatigue and party size.

tasks.officialDescription: DO NOT USE. Gives 5% of each class's XP globalVar to every current partyActor if globalVar 'XPShare' is set to 1.

tasks.name: hostile

uses.description: Turns the actor the task is running on hostile to the player, so it will fight the party and can be attacked. Nothing else about it changes — it does not start a fight by itself. Use it at the end of a conversation that goes badly.

tasks.officialDescription: Sets the current task actor to hostile = true.

tasks.name: playerInitiateCombat

uses.description: Starts a fight with the actor the task is running on, counted as the player having thrown the first punch. Both sides drop back to their idle stances and the conversation window closes first. Being the aggressor affects who acts first and who is blamed for the fight.

tasks.officialDescription: Causes the player to initiate combat with the currentActorTalkingTo (or current task actor if not in dialog).

tasks.name: enemyInitiateCombat

uses.description: Starts a fight with the actor the task is running on, counted as that actor having thrown the first punch. Both sides drop back to their idle stances and the conversation window closes first. Being attacked rather than attacking affects who acts first and who is blamed.

tasks.officialDescription: Causes the currentActorTalkingTo (or current task actor if not in dialog) to initiate combat with the player.

tasks.name: giveQuestItemReward

uses.description: Pays the player the full value of whatever item the current tavern quest asked for, as though they had sold it, and adds the sum to their lifetime earnings. The item itself is not taken; this is only the payment half of handing in a quest.

tasks.officialDescription: DO NOT USE. Gives gold equal to the value of the item ID set in globalVar 'tavern_questItem'.

tasks.name: reassignQuestItem

uses.description: Rolls a fresh quest item for the tavern board and records what it is, so the next job asks for something different. The choice is made from the quest loot table's own substitution rules. Nothing is created or given to anyone.

tasks.officialDescription: DO NOT USE. Sets globalVar 'tavern_questItem' to a random ID from the 'loot_quest' item's toMake list.

tasks.name: gotoNodeIf

uses.description: Jumps the conversation to a named dialog node, but only if a formula comes out at one or more. This is the branching test that lets one line of dialog lead to different follow-ups depending on the world state. The formula sees the actor the task is running on as its target.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The dialog node to jump to when the test passes.

required.name: strings[1]
required.description: The condition to test. The jump happens when it comes out at 1 or more.

tasks.officialDescription: Must be used in dialog. Tries to go to dialogNode 'sValue' if formula 'sValue2' passes.

tasks.name: gotoNodeDelay

uses.description: Waits a while and then opens a named dialog node with the actor the task is running on, locking the player out of interacting for the same length of time so the pause reads as deliberate. Use it to let an animation or an effect play out between lines. The conversation resumes on its own when the wait ends.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The dialog node to open once the wait is over.

optional.name: floats[0]
optional.description: How many seconds to wait. Defaults to 0, which opens the node almost immediately.

tasks.officialDescription: Tries to go to dialogNode 'sValue' after 'fValue' seconds. Uses the currentActorTalkingTo (or current task actor if not in dialog) as the talker.

tasks.name: delayDialog

uses.description: Hides the conversation window for a while and then brings it back where it left off, locking the player out of interacting for the same length of time. Use it to clear the screen while something plays out mid-conversation. The dialog resumes on its own when the wait ends.

optional.name: floats[0]
optional.description: How many seconds to hide the conversation for. Defaults to 0, which brings it straight back.

tasks.officialDescription: If in dialog mode, delays showing the current dialogNode for fValue seconds.

tasks.name: incOnNewDay

uses.description: Moves the actor the task is running on to the next numbered dialog node, but only once a full day of world time has passed since the last time this was used on that node, and only from the second use onward. Use it for a character whose greeting advances a step each day. When it does advance, the conversation jumps straight to the new node.

required.name: floats[0]
required.description: A number handed to the conversation as it opens, for nodes that take one. It must be supplied. If several numbers are given, only the last one is used.

tasks.officialDescription: Increases the number at the end of the dialogNodeID of the task actor by 1 if at least 1 day has passed since this task was called for the task actor.

tasks.name: incDefaultNode

uses.description: Moves the actor the task is running on to the next numbered dialog node, so the next time the player talks to them they get the following scene. The name is advanced by incrementing the number on its end. Nothing happens if the actor has no dialog node set.

tasks.officialDescription: Increases the number at the end of the dialogNodeID of the task actor by 1.

tasks.name: setAsDialogNode

uses.description: Sets which conversation the actor the task is running on opens with from now on. Naming no node instead uses the node this task was invoked from, which is the way a scene pins itself as the character's new default. The change sticks until something else moves them on.

optional.name: strings[0]
optional.description: The dialog node the actor should open with. Defaults to the node this task was invoked from.

tasks.officialDescription: Sets the dialogNodeID for the currentActorTalkingTo (or current task actor if not in dialog) to 'sValue', or the currentDialogNode if unset.

tasks.name: setDefaultNodeIf

uses.description: Sets which conversation the actor the task is running on opens with from now on, but only if a formula comes out at one or more. Use it to advance a character's default scene conditionally at the end of a conversation. The formula sees that actor as its target.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The dialog node the actor should open with when the test passes.

required.name: strings[1]
required.description: The condition to test. The change happens when it comes out at 1 or more.

tasks.officialDescription: Sets the dialogNodeID for the currentActorTalkingTo (or current task actor if not in dialog) to 'sValue' if the formula in 'svalue2' passes.

tasks.name: clearDialogNode

uses.description: Clears the conversation the actor the task is running on opens with, so talking to them does nothing from then on. Use it to silence a character once their part is played out. It can be set again later.

tasks.officialDescription: Clears the dialogNode of the currentActorTalkingTo (or current task actor if not in dialog).

tasks.name: flee

uses.description: Makes the actor the task is running on run away from the battle: they vanish in a puff with a rustle of cloth, the party is credited with nine tenths of the experience they were worth, and a message announces that they have fled. The fight is put on hold until the player dismisses the message. Use it for a single enemy breaking off.

optional.name: strings[1]
optional.description: The visual effect played as the actor vanishes. Defaults to the standard fleeing puff. Reaching this slot means filling the first string slot too, with anything at all.

tasks.officialDescription: The currentActorTalkingTo (or current task actor if not in dialog) is removed from the zone.

tasks.name: enemyFlee

uses.description: Makes the whole enemy side run away: every actor of the contextual actor's faction within eighteen tiles vanishes in a puff, the screen darkens for a moment, and the party is awarded experience for the group as though they had beaten it. Use it when a fight is broken off by the losing side. Nobody is left behind to keep fighting.

tasks.officialDescription: All actors in the combat area that are the same faction as the currentActorTalkingTo (or current task actor if not in dialog) are removed from the zone, then the playerParty is awarded XP.

tasks.name: playerFlee

uses.description: Covers the party's escape: every actor of the contextual actor's faction within eighteen tiles forgets its target, turns to face the player and drops any automatic greeting, while the party is made invisible for a spell — twelve seconds for the first member and three more for each after. Use it when the party breaks off a fight and runs. The enemies are left standing.

tasks.officialDescription: Ends combat with any actors within the combat area that have the same faction as the currentActorTalkingTo (or current task actor if not in dialog), then gives 'invisible' AV to playerParty.

tasks.name: enemyMoraleUp

uses.description: Lifts the spirits of the contextual actor's whole side, giving every actor of its faction within eighteen tiles a lasting morale boost. Higher morale makes them fight on rather than break. The boost wears off after a long while.

tasks.officialDescription: Increases the morale by 1 stage for actors within the combat area that are the same faction as the currentActorTalkingTo (or current task actor if not in dialog).

tasks.name: enemyMoraleDown

uses.description: Shakes the confidence of the contextual actor's whole side, giving every actor of its faction within eighteen tiles a lasting morale penalty. Lower morale makes them more likely to break and run. The penalty wears off after a long while.

tasks.officialDescription: Lowers the morale by 1 stage for actors within the combat area that are the same faction as the currentActorTalkingTo (or current task actor if not in dialog).

tasks.name: playerMoraleUp

uses.description: Lifts the spirits of every member of the player's party, giving each of them a lasting morale boost. Higher morale improves how they hold up under pressure. The boost wears off after a long while.

tasks.officialDescription: Increases the morale stage by 1 for all partyActors.

tasks.name: crewMorale

uses.description: Changes how the ship's crew feel about the voyage, which affects their performance and the events that befall the ship. Negative values make them unhappier. It is the fleet-wide morale rather than any individual's.

optional.name: floats[0]
optional.description: How much to change crew morale by; negative values reduce it. Defaults to 0, which changes nothing.

tasks.officialDescription: Increases (or decreases) player crew morale by fValue.

tasks.name: peace

uses.description: Ends the fight peacefully with the contextual actor's side: every actor of its faction within eighteen tiles stops being hostile, forgets its target, stops being worth experience, and switches to its peaceful greeting. The party is still awarded experience for the group as though they had won. Use it when a negotiation succeeds.

tasks.officialDescription: Ends combat with any actors within the combat area that have the same faction as the currentActorTalkingTo (or current task actor if not in dialog), sets their hostile to false and awards the playerParty with XP.

tasks.name: peaceXPrewardOnly

uses.description: Awards the party the experience they would have earned for beating the contextual actor's group, without changing anyone's hostility or ending the fight. Use it alongside another way of resolving a confrontation. Nobody's behaviour changes.

tasks.officialDescription: Gives the XP to the playerParty that would be rewarded with the 'peace' task, but doesn't change any actors.

tasks.name: moveCamXY

uses.description: Nudges the camera by an offset from wherever it is heading, in tiles. Unlike pointing the camera somewhere this is relative, so it works without knowing where the view currently sits. Both offsets are needed.

required.name: floats[0]
required.description: How far to shift the camera horizontally, in tiles.

required.name: floats[1]
required.description: How far to shift the camera vertically, in tiles.

tasks.officialDescription: Must be used as a taskString. Adds floats[0], floats[1] to the camera's current X,Y position.

tasks.name: moveXY

uses.description: Slides the actor the task is running on by an offset from where it stands, in tiles. The actor glides there rather than teleporting. Nothing happens if there is no contextual actor, and both offsets are needed.

required.name: floats[0]
required.description: How far to slide horizontally, in tiles.

required.name: floats[1]
required.description: How far to slide vertically, in tiles.

tasks.officialDescription: Must be used as a taskString. Moves the currentActorTalkingTo (or current task actor if not in dialog) by floats[0] X and floats[1] Y, with no restrictions.

tasks.name: moveX1

uses.description: Slides the actor the task is running on one tile right from where it stands. The actor glides there rather than teleporting. Nothing happens if there is no contextual actor, and there is nothing to configure.

tasks.officialDescription: Moves the currentActorTalkingTo (or current task actor if not in dialog) to the right 1 tile, with no restrictions.

tasks.name: moveY1

uses.description: Slides the actor the task is running on one tile down from where it stands. The actor glides there rather than teleporting. Nothing happens if there is no contextual actor, and there is nothing to configure.

tasks.officialDescription: Moves the currentActorTalkingTo (or current task actor if not in dialog) down 1 tile, with no restrictions.

tasks.name: moveXNeg1

uses.description: Slides the actor the task is running on one tile left from where it stands. The actor glides there rather than teleporting. Nothing happens if there is no contextual actor, and there is nothing to configure.

tasks.officialDescription: Moves the currentActorTalkingTo (or current task actor if not in dialog) to the left 1 tile, with no restrictions.

tasks.name: moveYNeg1

uses.description: Slides the actor the task is running on one tile up from where it stands. The actor glides there rather than teleporting. Nothing happens if there is no contextual actor, and there is nothing to configure.

tasks.officialDescription: Moves the currentActorTalkingTo (or current task actor if not in dialog) up 1 tile, with no restrictions.

tasks.name: playerFacingRot

uses.description: Turns the player to face a given direction, in degrees, and re-applies the turn a moment later so it sticks even if something else moves them in the meantime. Nothing happens if there is no player actor. Use it to line the player up before a scene.

required.name: floats[0]
required.description: The direction the player faces, in degrees.

tasks.officialDescription: Sets the current player actor's facingRot to 'fValue'.

tasks.name: playerAnim

uses.description: Plays an animation on the player, replacing whatever they were doing. Nothing happens if there is no player actor or the animation does not exist. The player is not held busy, so they can be interrupted immediately.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The ID of the animation to play on the player.

tasks.officialDescription: Makes the current player actor play animation 'sValue'.

tasks.name: facingRot90

uses.description: Turns the actor the task is running on to face 90 degrees, and turns them again a moment later so the change sticks even if something else moves them in between. There is nothing to configure. Use it to line a character up before a scene.

tasks.officialDescription: Sets currentActorTalkingTo (or current task actor if not in dialog) to 90 facingRot.

tasks.name: facingRot180

uses.description: Turns the actor the task is running on to face 180 degrees, and turns them again a moment later so the change sticks even if something else moves them in between. There is nothing to configure. Use it to line a character up before a scene.

tasks.officialDescription: Sets currentActorTalkingTo (or current task actor if not in dialog) to 180 facingRot.

tasks.name: facingRot0

uses.description: Turns the actor the task is running on to face 0 degrees, and turns them again a moment later so the change sticks even if something else moves them in between. There is nothing to configure. Use it to line a character up before a scene.

tasks.officialDescription: Sets currentActorTalkingTo (or current task actor if not in dialog) to 0 facingRot.

tasks.name: facingRot270

uses.description: Turns the actor the task is running on to face 270 degrees, and turns them again a moment later so the change sticks even if something else moves them in between. There is nothing to configure. Use it to line a character up before a scene.

tasks.officialDescription: Sets currentActorTalkingTo (or current task actor if not in dialog) to 270 facingRot.

tasks.name: facingRotPrev

uses.description: Turns the actor the task is running on back to the direction that was stashed away earlier as their previous facing, a moment after this runs. Use it at the end of a conversation to put a character back the way they were standing. Nothing is stashed by this task itself.

tasks.officialDescription: Sets currentActorTalkingTo (or current task actor if not in dialog) to talkerPreviousFacingRot rot.

tasks.name: setPrevFacingRot

uses.description: Stashes a facing direction away so a later task can turn a character back to it, which is how a conversation remembers how someone was standing before they turned to talk. By default it records the current facing of the actor the task is running on, but a direction can be given instead. Only one such direction is remembered at a time.

optional.name: strings[0]
optional.description: The direction to stash, in degrees, written as text. Because a plain number written in a taskString would be taken as a number rather than a string, it has to be forced into a text slot. Defaults to the contextual actor's current facing.

optional.name: floats[0]
optional.description: The direction to stash, in degrees, wrapped into the 0-360 range. It is only used when no text value is given, and only when it is above 0. Defaults to the contextual actor's current facing.

tasks.officialDescription: Sets the talkerPreviousFacingRot to the current rotation of the currentActorTalkingTo (or current task actor if not in dialog). If sValue is set, it should be the rotation to set it to instead. If sValue isn't set, but fValue is > 0, it will be set to that rotation instead (360 == 0). The talkerPreviousFacingRot is the rotation the currentActorTalkingTo will be set to once dialog finishes.

tasks.name: lookAtTalker

uses.description: Turns the player to face the actor the task is running on, snapping to the nearest quarter turn. If the player is walking, the turn is re-applied twice more over the next second or so, so it holds once they stop. With no contextual actor the player simply faces south.

tasks.officialDescription: Makes the player look at the currentActorTalkingTo (or current task actor if not in dialog).

tasks.name: lookAtPlayer
