uses.description: Turns the actor the task is running on to face the player, snapping to the nearest quarter turn. If that actor is moving, the turn is re-applied twice more over the next second or so, so it holds once they stop. With no contextual actor the turn defaults to south.

tasks.officialDescription: Makes the currentActorTalkingTo (or current task actor if not in dialog) look in the direction of the current player actor.

tasks.name: setAI_idle

uses.description: Switches the actor the task is running on to the plain idle AI script, so it stops whatever routine it was following and simply stands about. It restarts at the top of that script and forgets what it was waiting on. Use it to settle a character after a scripted sequence.

tasks.officialDescription: Sets the ai_lua script for the currentActorTalkingTo (or current task actor if not in dialog) to 'idle'.

tasks.name: setAI_idle_flag

uses.description: Switches the actor the task is running on to the flag-carrying idle AI script, the standing-about routine used by actors that hold a banner. It restarts at the top of that script and forgets what it was waiting on.

tasks.officialDescription: Sets the ai_lua script for the currentActorTalkingTo (or current task actor if not in dialog) to 'idle_flag'.

tasks.name: die

uses.description: Kills the actor the task is running on outright by stripping its unkillable protection and taking away all its health at once. This is a hard kill rather than a knockout, and it goes through even for actors that would otherwise survive anything. It fires all the usual death reactions.

tasks.officialDescription: Kills the currentActorTalkingTo (or current task actor if not in dialog), even if they have unkillable set.

tasks.name: escapeGate

uses.description: Sends the actor the task is running on out through an escape gate, casting the gate's own action on their tile so they disappear with its effect. If this happens during combat and the actor was hostile, the party is credited with the experience it was worth. The next action is held back for a second so the exit reads clearly.

tasks.officialDescription: Executes action 'escapeGate_act' on the currentActorTalkingTo (or current task actor if not in dialog), which removes them from the zone.

tasks.name: removeTalker

uses.description: Deletes the actor the task is running on from the world with no death, no corpse and no effect, taking them out of the party, the turn order and any open windows. Use it to make a character walk out of the story. They disappear on the next frame.

tasks.officialDescription: Removes the currentActorTalkingTo (or current task actor if not in dialog) from the zone.

tasks.name: setOnlyNPCDialogWindowSizeY

uses.description: Sets the height in pixels of the speech box the other party in a conversation talks from, so a long passage gets more room. It stays that size until it is changed or reset. The player's own reply box is untouched.

required.name: floats[0]
required.description: The height of the speech box in pixels. It must be supplied. If several numbers are given, only the first one is used.

tasks.officialDescription: Sets the dialog window height to 'fValue'. If unset in a dialog specialEffect, or set to 0, sets the size to default (200).

tasks.name: setDialogWindowSizeYAuto

uses.description: Sizes the speech box the other party talks from to fit whatever text is currently in it, rather than holding a fixed height. Use it to undo a manual height once a long passage is over.

tasks.officialDescription: Sets the dialog window height based on the text in the current dialogNode statements text if it overflows the default height.

tasks.name: setPCDialogWindowSizeY

uses.description: Sets the height in pixels of the box the player's own replies appear in, so a long list of options gets more room. It stays that size until it is changed or reset. The other party's speech box is untouched.

required.name: floats[0]
required.description: The height of the reply box in pixels. It must be supplied. If several numbers are given, only the first one is used.

tasks.officialDescription: Sets the dialog options window height to 'fValue'. If unset in a dialog specialEffect, or set to 0, sets the size to default (200).

tasks.name: resetPCDialogWindowSizeY

uses.description: Puts the box the player's replies appear in back to its normal height, undoing any height set for it. Use it once a long list of options is done with.

tasks.officialDescription: Sets the player's dialog window height to default (200).

tasks.name: showCharstats

uses.description: Brings the character stats panel back on screen and forces it to appear immediately rather than waiting for the usual conditions. Use it to draw the player's attention to a character's numbers during a scene.

tasks.officialDescription: Unhides the character stats window, if it was hidden.

tasks.name: showQuickslots

uses.description: Brings the quickslot bar back on screen, clears the game's hidden-interface setting, and forces the bar to appear immediately rather than waiting for the usual conditions. Use it to point the player at their items during a tutorial.

tasks.officialDescription: Unhides character stats and quickslots.

tasks.name: hideQuickslots

uses.description: Hides the quickslot bar, leaving the rest of the interface alone. Use it to keep the item bar out of the way during a scene without stripping the whole screen.

tasks.officialDescription: Hides character stats and quickslots window.

tasks.name: setCombatUIVisible

uses.description: Shows or hides the combat interface — the turn order and the panels that go with it — without leaving combat. Use it to clean up the screen for a scripted moment in the middle of a fight.

optional.name: bools[0]
optional.description: True shows the combat interface, false hides it. Defaults to false.

tasks.officialDescription: Sets the turn order window and combat commands window visibility to bValue1. Also hides quickslots and character stats windows if bValue1 is false.

tasks.name: showEscFactionWindow

uses.description: Opens the faction standings panel from the escape menu on its own, without the rest of the menu, and arranges for the conversation window to be hidden when the dialog next moves on. Use it to show the player where they stand with the factions during a conversation.

tasks.officialDescription: Shows just the faction part of the escMenu and sets nextDialogNode_hideWindow = true.

tasks.name: hideEscWindows

uses.description: Closes the escape menu and both of its side panels, clearing them off the screen. Use it to tidy up after showing one of them during a scene.

tasks.officialDescription: Hides all windows used for the escMenu.

tasks.name: unlockGem

uses.description: Grants the player the hint gem, makes it usable straight away, and — the first time it is granted — plays a burst of sparkles and a chime over the player. Use it as the reward moment when the hint button becomes available. It stays unlocked for the rest of the save.

tasks.officialDescription: DO NOT USE.

tasks.name: scoreScreenResponse

uses.description: Picks the closing remark for the end-of-run report and points the conversation at it. The choice is narrowed by how profitable the run was and how many characters died, then the least-used matching line is taken so remarks do not repeat, and its use is counted. If nothing matches, or the chosen line leads nowhere, the conversation falls through to returning to town.

tasks.officialDescription: DO NOT USE.

tasks.name: research_report

uses.description: Builds the researcher's payout speech into a named dialog node: every unsold journal entry the player knows is tallied up, the common ones summarised by rarity and the rare ones called out individually with their titles, each line paying out money and exploration renown as it is read. The rarest discoveries also earn favour with every faction that tracks it. All the counted entries are marked sold so they cannot be handed in twice, and if there is nothing new the node simply says so.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The dialog node whose lines are replaced with the payout speech. Its existing lines and options are cleared first.

tasks.officialDescription: Sets 'sValue' dialogNode's statements based on journalEntries that have yet to be sold to a researcher.

tasks.name: cartographer_report

uses.description: Builds the cartographer's payout speech into a named dialog node, working out how much of the world map the player has uncovered and how much of that is new since they were last paid. The lines pay out money for the new territory as they are read, and record the new total so the same ground cannot be sold twice. If too little new territory has been explored the node simply says so.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The dialog node whose lines are replaced with the payout speech.

tasks.officialDescription: Sets up the 'sValue' dialogNode to be used with a cartographer's report. Also sets the 'mapPercentPaid globalVar to the currently explored overworld percentage.

tasks.name: donate

uses.description: Records a donation to the town or port the party is currently inside, earning favour with the faction that holds it and a little trade renown, while reducing their reputation for piracy. Both are worked out as a thousandth of the sum donated. If the location belongs to no faction only the renown changes, and nothing happens at all if the party is not inside a location.

optional.name: floats[0]
optional.description: The amount donated. Defaults to 0, which changes nothing.

tasks.officialDescription: Acts as if the player had donated 'fValue' gold to the current location, which increases its favor and gives trade fame.

tasks.name: jobDialogOptions

uses.description: Builds the guild job board for the town or port the party is inside: one dialog option per job the location is currently offering, each leading to a description node and an acceptance node that are generated on the spot. Accepting a job records its type, goal, reward and log line into the quest variables, notes who gave it, and for some kinds also creates the monster den or treasure map the job points at. A dismissal option is added at the bottom, and nothing happens if the party is not inside a location.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The dialog node the job options are built into. Its existing options are cleared first.

tasks.officialDescription: Sets up the dialogNode ID 'sValue' dialogOptions for the current location's set questTypes.

tasks.name: refreshLocQuests

uses.description: Throws away the jobs the town or port the party is inside is currently offering and rolls a fresh set. Use it when time has passed and the board should have moved on. The party must actually be inside a location.

tasks.officialDescription: Randomizes the available questTypes for the current location, if it is a port and has 'sign_icon_letter' in its tooltipIcons.

tasks.name: stealloc

uses.description: Hands every port on the world map that can change hands over to the player's own faction at once, by investing an unlimited sum in each without touching their wealth. This is a sweeping takeover rather than a normal investment. Nothing happens unless the player's faction has been set to a real faction.

tasks.officialDescription: Converts all port locations in the overworld that can be converted to the player's current faction, as set in globalVar 'playerFaction'.

tasks.name: cancelQuest

uses.description: Abandons the player's current job: every variable recording its type, goal, reward, giver and log line is cleared, and any monster dens the job had revealed are hidden away again. Use it when a job is given up or fails. The job cannot be resumed afterwards.

tasks.officialDescription: Resets all quest-related globalVars and hides all overworld locations with a 'monsterden' tag.

tasks.name: cancelRoyalQuest

uses.description: Abandons the player's current job, but only if it is a royal commission rather than an ordinary guild job. Every variable recording its type, goal, reward, giver and log line is cleared, and any monster dens the job had revealed are hidden away again. An ordinary job is left untouched.

tasks.officialDescription: Resets all quest-related globalVars and hides all overworld locations with a 'monsterden' tag, if globalVar 'questRoyal' is > 0.

tasks.name: cleanUpQuest

uses.description: Clears out the player's current job record once it is finished with: every variable recording its type, goal, reward, giver and log line is emptied, and any monster dens the job had revealed are hidden away again. Unlike abandoning a job this is the tidy-up after one has been handed in.

tasks.officialDescription: Resets all quest-related globalVars and hides all overworld locations with a 'monsterden' tag.

tasks.name: royalJobDialogOptions

uses.description: Builds the royal commission offer into a named dialog node: a single option describing the commission the crown is currently offering, leading to a description node and an acceptance node generated on the spot. Accepting it records the commission's type, goal and log line into the quest variables, marks it as royal, notes who gave it, and for some kinds also makes the target location findable. The offering faction is the one that holds the current location, or the contextual actor's own faction if the party is not inside one.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The dialog node the commission option is built into. Its existing options are cleared first.

tasks.officialDescription: Sets up the dialogNode ID 'sValue' and its dialogOptions for the current royal quest, set in globalVar 'royalQuestType'.

tasks.name: refreshRoyalQuests

uses.description: Rolls a fresh royal commission, replacing whatever the crown was previously offering. Use it when enough time has passed that the standing offer should have changed. Nothing about an accepted commission is affected.

tasks.officialDescription: Randomizes the current royal quest, if one isn't already set.

tasks.name: refreshRoyalTitle

uses.description: Clears the player's noble title, so they are addressed plainly again until a new title is granted. Use it when a rank is stripped or before granting a different one.

tasks.officialDescription: Sets globalVar 'playerTitle' to an empty string.

tasks.name: investigator_nearestLoc

uses.description: Works out the nearest monster den the player has not yet discovered and writes an informant's answer naming it and its map bearing into a variable keyed to whoever the player is talking to, ready for that character's next line to read out. If nothing is left undiscovered the answer says so instead. The search starts from the location the party is currently inside.

tasks.officialDescription: Sets the currentActorTalkingTo investigator's response for when finding the nearest undiscovered location.

tasks.name: investigator_tradespecial

uses.description: Works out where the next surge in demand will be and for what goods, and writes an informant's answer naming the port and the commodity into a variable keyed to whoever the player is talking to. If no next surge has been decided yet, one is rolled first while the current surge is left untouched.

tasks.officialDescription: Sets the currentActorTalkingTo investigator's response for when finding out next month's trade special.

tasks.name: investigator_slainenemy

uses.description: Looks through the kinds of creature the player has killed for one whose journal entry they have not yet learned, and sets up an informant to hand it over: the entry is queued to be added to the journal and an answer naming it is written into a variable keyed to whoever the player is talking to. If the player has already researched everything they have killed, the answer says so and nothing is granted.

tasks.officialDescription: Sets the currentActorTalkingTo investigator's response and task to perform for when checking for unexamined monsters.

tasks.name: investigator_fleetpos

uses.description: Sets up an informant to sell the player thirty days of tracking on one faction's fleet movements: a task granting the tracking is queued and an answer naming the faction is written into a variable keyed to whoever the player is talking to. If the faction does not exist, the answer is a shrug and nothing is granted.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The ID of the faction whose fleets are to be tracked.

tasks.officialDescription: Sets the currentActorTalkingTo investigator's response and task to perform for when tracking faction ID 'sValue's fleets.

tasks.name: investigator_setupportselect

uses.description: Builds a list of dialog options, one per discovered port in a chosen quarter of the world map that has something worth unlocking by investment, each option previewing what investing there would eventually make available. Ports with nothing left to unlock at their current wealth are left off the list. The options are arranged in rows and the dialog windows are resized to fit however many there are, with a back option at the bottom.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The dialog node the port options are built into. Its existing options and effects are cleared first.

required.name: floats[0]
required.description: Which side of the world map's centre to include, as -1 for west, 1 for east, or 0 for the centre column. It must be supplied.

required.name: floats[1]
required.description: Which half of the world map's centre to include, as -1 for north, 1 for south, or 0 for the centre row. It must be supplied.

tasks.officialDescription: Must be used as a taskString. Sets the port selection dialogOptions the investigator uses for investment information, for the dialogNode set in strings[0]. floats[0] and floats[1] specify which quadrant to select ports from (-1,-1 specifies northwest, through to 1,1 specifying southeast).

tasks.name: investigator_setupfleetposselect

uses.description: Builds a list of dialog options, one per faction whose fleets can be tracked, each offering thirty days of tracking for three hundred coins and greyed out into a cannot-afford option when the player is short. Choosing one grants the tracking for that faction. The options are arranged in rows with a back option at the bottom, and the reply box is resized to fit them.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The dialog node the faction options are built into. Its existing options and effects are cleared first.

tasks.officialDescription: Sets up the dialogNode ID 'sValue' dialogOptions for selecting which faction's fleets to track for use with an investigator.

tasks.name: setupBuyShipDialog

uses.description: Builds the shipwright's catalogue into a named dialog node: one option per hull the town or port the party is inside offers, each showing the ship's picture and name and carrying its stat sheet as a tooltip. The options are laid out in one or two columns depending how many there are, with a farewell option at the bottom. Nothing happens if the party is not inside a location.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The dialog node the ship options are built into. Its existing options are cleared first.

tasks.officialDescription: Sets up the dialogOptions for dialogNode 'sValue' for purchasing ships from the current location, based on its set shipwright_boatTypes list.

tasks.name: crash

uses.description: Deliberately crashes the game by looking up a key that does not exist. It is a debugging aid for testing how the game behaves when something goes badly wrong, and has no place in a shipped mod.

tasks.officialDescription: DO NOT USE. Crashes the game with a missing dictionary index error.

tasks.name: buyShip

uses.description: Charges the player the list price of a ship and adds a brand new one of that kind to their fleet, flying their colours and under their control. If they had no fleet, this becomes its first vessel. A count of ships bought is kept, and a fanfare plays.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The kind of ship to buy. Its listed value is deducted from the player's purse.

tasks.officialDescription: Adds the ship actor with the ID of 'sValue' to the player's fleet and subtracts the cost of it from their gold.

tasks.name: giveShip

uses.description: Adds a brand new ship of a given kind to the player's fleet for free, flying their colours and under their control. If they had no fleet, this becomes its first vessel. A count of ships given is kept, and a fanfare plays.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The kind of ship to give.

optional.name: strings[1]
optional.description: The exact ID to give the new ship, so later tasks can find it by name. Defaults to a generated unique ID; supplying a name already in use will cause trouble.

tasks.officialDescription: Adds ship actorType ID 'sValue' to the player's fleet, if it can fit. Uses ID 'sValue2' for the ship actor if specified.

tasks.name: renameShip

uses.description: Opens the naming window for the most recently added ship in the player's fleet, with no way to close it without choosing a name. Use it straight after buying or being given a vessel.

tasks.officialDescription: Shows the charEdit window for the last ship in the player's fleet.

tasks.name: addToFleet

uses.description: Takes the ship the task is running on into the player's fleet and out of the world, so it stops being a moored vessel and becomes one of theirs. If it was offering the option to unmoor, that dialog is cleared first. The ship remains in the party rather than being removed from it.

tasks.officialDescription: Adds the currentActorTalkingTo (or current task actor if not in dialog) to the player's fleet. If the actor is iAmABoat, they are added to the player's fleet ships, otherwise they are added to the player's crew and landing party if there is room.

tasks.name: addToFleet_andSwapWithFleet_slot

uses.description: Swaps a ship in the player's fleet for the one the task is running on: the fleet vessel is pulled out, its crew moved across to the new ship, and the new ship takes its place in the fleet order. The displaced vessel is moored at the harbour's mooring point, stripped of its crew and cargo bonuses, tied up so it can be unmoored again later, and made unable to despawn. If there is no free tile to moor it on, an error is reported and the swap leaves it nowhere.

required.name: floats[0]
required.description: Which fleet slot to swap out, counted from 0. It must be supplied.

tasks.officialDescription: Swaps the ship in slot 'fValue' of the player's fleet with the currentActorTalkingTo (or current task actor if not in dialog), if they are iAmABoat. Any crew on the swapped out ship will be transferred to the currentActorTalkingTo ship. The swapped out ship actor will try to be placed within the 9 tiles surrounding travel_point9 and be given the 'boat_unmoor' dialogNodeID.

tasks.name: removeFromParty_slot

uses.description: Dismisses one of the player's party members by their slot number, standing them on a free crew-dismissal spot in the zone, healing them, tipping everything they carried into the stash, and setting them up so they can be rehired later. They are taken out of both the party and the fleet. If there is no free spot to stand them on, the conversation is diverted to a no-room reply instead.

required.name: floats[0]
required.description: Which party slot to dismiss, counted from 0. It must be supplied.

tasks.officialDescription: Removes the actor in slot 'fValue' of the player's current partyActors and adds them to the first unoccupied travelPoint set D item. Also changes their dialogNodeID to 'crew_rehire'.

tasks.name: researchFromFleet_slot

uses.description: Hands one of the player's ships over to the shipwright of the town or port they are in for study, so that hull becomes buyable there after a long wait. The player pays the ship's value, its cargo is tipped into their hold, and the vessel leaves the fleet. The conversation is diverted to a suitable reply if that hull is already being studied, already sold there, or the shipwright's catalogue is full.

required.name: floats[0]
required.description: Which fleet slot to hand over, counted from 0. It must be supplied.

tasks.officialDescription: Removes the ship in slot 'fValue' of the player's fleet and adds it as an unlockable ship for the current location. Also removes the ship actorType's value from the player's gold.

tasks.name: removeFromFleet_slot

uses.description: Moors one of the player's ships by its fleet slot: it is placed on a free tile at the harbour's mooring point, stripped of its crew and cargo bonuses, tied up so it can be unmoored again later, taken out of the fleet and made unable to despawn. If there is no free tile to moor it on, the conversation is diverted to a no-room reply and the ship stays in the fleet.

required.name: floats[0]
required.description: Which fleet slot to moor, counted from 0. It must be supplied.

tasks.officialDescription: Removes the ship actor in slot 'fValue' of the player's fleet and places it around travelPoint 9 in the current zone, if it can fit.

tasks.name: enterPort

uses.description: Takes the party into the nearest port within four tiles of the player, loading its interior. Only harbours count, so a non-port settlement standing nearby is ignored. Nothing happens if there is no port that close.

tasks.officialDescription: Forces the player to enter the closest port location that is in the current zone, within 4 tiles of them.

tasks.name: enterLocation

uses.description: Takes the party into the nearest location of any kind within four tiles of the player, loading its interior. Unlike entering a port this includes settlements, ruins and other places that are not harbours. Nothing happens if there is nothing that close.

tasks.officialDescription: Forces the player to enter the closest non-port location that is in the current zone, within 4 tiles of them.

tasks.name: buyLocationFood

uses.description: Buys a meal for the whole crew at the town or port the party is inside, charging for one serving per crew member. Crew morale rises by the dish's own strength, and any effects the dish carries are applied to every ship or to every sailor aboard, depending what the effect touches. The dish is remembered as the last meal eaten and the party is stood back on the eatery's own spots.

tasks.officialDescription: Goes through the process of buying and applying the effects of the current location's cafeFood_itemTypeID to the player's crew.

tasks.name: invest

uses.description: Invests a sum in the town or port the party is inside, raising its wealth and building the player's faction's hold over it. Investing in a place held by someone else costs a little standing with its current owner and earns the same with the player's own faction; with no player faction the money simply raises the location's wealth and earns extra trade renown. Every investment raises trade renown and lowers piracy renown, and if the investment actually flips the place to a new owner, a fanfare plays and the change is announced.

optional.name: floats[0]
optional.description: How much to invest. Defaults to 0.

tasks.officialDescription: Acts as if the player had invested 'fValue' gold into the current location.

tasks.name: modTalkerFavor

uses.description: Changes the player's standing with the faction the actor the task is running on belongs to. Use it to reward or punish the player through the character they are dealing with. Nothing happens if that actor is missing or belongs to no real faction.

required.name: floats[0]
required.description: How much to change standing by; negative values reduce it. Without it nothing happens at all.

tasks.officialDescription: Adds 'fValue' to the player's 'favor_' faction ID globalVar matching the currentActorTalkingTo's set faction (or current task actor if not in dialog).

tasks.name: modLocFavor

uses.description: Changes the player's standing with the faction that holds the town or port the party is currently inside. Use it for deeds done inside a settlement. The party must actually be inside a location.

optional.name: floats[0]
optional.description: How much to change standing by; negative values reduce it. Defaults to 0.

tasks.officialDescription: Adds 'fValue' to the player's 'favor_' faction globalVar for the current location's favored faction. Also shows associated favor icons and sounds.

tasks.name: modLocWealthLevel

uses.description: Changes how wealthy a location is, which decides what its shops stock and what can be unlocked there. The new wealth is clamped between nothing and full, and anything the location can now afford to offer is unlocked immediately and quietly. By default it affects the location the party is inside.

optional.name: strings[0]
optional.description: The ID of the location to change. Defaults to the one the party is currently inside; a name that matches no location falls back to that too.

optional.name: floats[0]
optional.description: How much to change the wealth by; negative values reduce it. Defaults to 0.

tasks.officialDescription: Adds 'fValue' to the current location's wealthLevel, which won't go below 0 or above 100. If sValue is set, adds to that location's wealthLevel instead.

tasks.name: setLocDiscoverable

uses.description: Makes a location findable, so it can appear on the map once its condition is met, and optionally changes that condition. It can also be marked as already discovered outright, in which case its map markers are dug up around it and, for modded locations, a sight-blocker is placed on its tile. By default it acts on the location the party is inside.

optional.name: strings[0]
optional.description: The ID of the location to make findable. Defaults to the one the party is currently inside; a name that matches no location falls back to that too.

optional.name: strings[1]
optional.description: The condition that must pass for the location to be discovered. Leaving it empty keeps whatever condition the location already had. Omitting the slot entirely leaves the condition untouched as well.

optional.name: bools[0]
optional.description: When true the location is marked discovered straight away and its map markers are revealed, but only if the party is in the zone the location sits in. Defaults to false.

tasks.officialDescription: Sets a location's discoverable bool to true. 'sValue' is the ID of the location. If ID is not set, uses current location instead. If 'sValue2' is set, it will be the new formula for the location's discoverable_fReq. If b1 is set and the player is in zoneThisLocationIsIn, will set discovered to true and unbury the location.

tasks.name: createMonsterDenNearby

uses.description: Creates a monster den on the world map at the site of the nearest existing den to the town or port the party is inside, replacing whatever was there with a fresh one built from a chosen recipe, and makes it findable. This is how a den-clearing job places its target. The party must be inside a location and at least one den site must already exist.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The ID of the level-data recipe describing the den to generate.

tasks.officialDescription: Sets up an overworld monster den that is closest to the current location using levelData 'sValue'.

tasks.name: bezoar_setupportselect

uses.description: Builds a teleport menu into a named dialog node, listing every discovered port in a chosen quarter of the world map apart from one excluded harbour and the one the party is currently in. Choosing a port hums and whisks the party straight to it, marking the journey as having used the gate. The options are arranged in rows with a back option at the bottom, and the dialog windows are resized to fit however many there are.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The dialog node the port options are built into. Its existing options and effects are cleared first.

required.name: floats[0]
required.description: Which side of the world map's centre to include, as -1 for west, 1 for east, or 0 for the centre column. It must be supplied.

required.name: floats[1]
required.description: Which half of the world map's centre to include, as -1 for north, 1 for south, or 0 for the centre row. It must be supplied.

tasks.officialDescription: Must be used as a taskString. Sets the fast travel dialogOptions the Ruluorn Bezoar uses, for the dialogNode set in strings[0]. floats[0] and floats[1] specify which quadrant to select ports from (-1,-1 specifies northwest, through to 1,1 specifying southeast).

tasks.name: cameraAtPlayer

uses.description: Snaps the camera onto the player's tile without following them afterwards. Use it to bring the view back to the party after showing something else. It does nothing if the camera is currently locked.

tasks.officialDescription: Points the camera at the tile the current player actor is on.

tasks.name: cameraAtTalker

uses.description: Snaps the camera onto the tile of the actor the task is running on, without following them afterwards. Use it to cut to a character during a conversation. It does nothing if the camera is currently locked.

tasks.officialDescription: Points the camera at the currentActorTalkingTo (or current task actor if not in dialog).

tasks.name: cameraAtPoint

uses.description: Snaps the camera onto one of the zone's numbered travel points and holds it there rather than following anyone. Travel points are items placed in the map data, so this frames a spot without hard-coding coordinates. It does nothing if the camera is currently locked.

required.name: floats[0]
required.description: Which numbered travel point to look at. It must be supplied.

required.name: floats[1]
required.description: Which travel point set to take it from. It must be supplied.

tasks.officialDescription: Must be used as a taskString. Points the camera at travel point #floats[0], set floats[1].

tasks.name: cameraAtPointLock

uses.description: Snaps the camera onto one of the zone's numbered travel points and then bolts it there, so nothing else can move it until another camera task explicitly releases it. Use it for a scripted shot that must hold still on a fixed spot.

required.name: floats[0]
required.description: Which numbered travel point to look at. It must be supplied.

required.name: floats[1]
required.description: Which travel point set to take it from. It must be supplied.

tasks.officialDescription: Must be used as a taskString. Points the camera at travel point #floats[0], set floats[1], and locks it there until the camera is pointed at something else with the 'pointCameraAt' task.

tasks.name: talkToOtherActor

uses.description: Starts a conversation with whoever else is standing on the same tile as the actor the task is running on, preferring one who is still on their feet. This is how a character hands the conversation over to their companion or mount. Nothing happens if nobody else shares the tile.

tasks.officialDescription: Enters dialog with the other actor that is currently on the same tile as the currentActorTalkingTo (or current task actor if not in dialog).

tasks.name: giveItem

uses.description: Gives the party a number of a named item, routing it to wherever that kind of item belongs — a pack, the cargo hold or the stash — and announcing it the way a normal pickup is announced. Nothing happens if the item type does not exist.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The ID of the item type to give.

optional.name: floats[0]
optional.description: How many to give. Defaults to 1, and 0 is also treated as 1.

tasks.officialDescription: Adds 'fValue' quantity of item ID 'sValue' to the player's cargo or stash inventory, depending on the item. If can't fit, added to held items. fValue 0 gives 1, -1 is default quantity, -2 is infinite, -11 through -19 is % chance to keep.

tasks.name: triggerEffect

uses.description: Waits a number of seconds and then runs a second task, handing that task one number and one piece of text as its arguments. The delayed task always runs on the player, centred on the player's tile, rather than on whatever actor scheduled it. Scheduling a delay of this kind cancels any earlier still-pending delayed task that had longer left to wait, so overlapping delays replace one another instead of stacking. All six values only fit in the full comma-separated task form; a trigger effect cannot carry this many.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: How many seconds to wait before running the delayed task, written as text. Because a plain number written in a taskString would be taken as a number rather than a string, it has to be forced into a text slot, and text that does not read as a number stops the task with an error.

required.name: strings[1]
required.description: The name of the task to run once the wait is over.

required.name: strings[2]
required.description: The number handed to the delayed task as its first number argument, written as text. Because a plain number written in a taskString would be taken as a number rather than a string, it has to be forced into a text slot, and text that does not read as a number stops the task with an error.

required.name: strings[3]
required.description: The text handed to the delayed task as its first text argument. The delayed task's second text argument is always empty.

required.name: strings[4]
required.description: Read as a number and carried alongside the delayed task, but nothing ever looks at it, so it has no effect. It still has to be text that reads as a number, or the task stops with an error.

required.name: strings[5]
required.description: Unused in this branch but must be provided as a placeholder, because this form of the task is only chosen when six or more text values are supplied.

uses.description: Waits a number of seconds and then runs a second task that takes no arguments of its own. The delayed task always runs on the player, centred on the player's tile, rather than on whatever actor scheduled it. Scheduling a delay of this kind cancels any earlier still-pending delayed task that had longer left to wait, so overlapping delays replace one another instead of stacking.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: What to run once the wait is over: normally just the name of a task, but when the value contains commas it is run as a whole comma-separated task with its own arguments. Only the trigger effect form can supply a value containing commas.

required.name: floats[0]
required.description: How many seconds to wait before running the delayed task.

tasks.officialDescription: DO NOT USE.

tasks.name: dialogEffect

uses.description: Waits a number of seconds and then runs a dialog effect: the named thing is tried first as a global trigger, then as one of the current zone's triggers, and finally run as a task in its own right. Because the wait detaches it from the conversation, the delayed effect runs with nobody registered as the actor being talked to and no dialog node attached, so effects that act on the talker or on node-named variables will not find them; triggers reached this way fire on the player. The effect is also handed -1 as a trailing number argument. Scheduling another delayed dialog effect cancels any earlier one that still had longer to wait.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The effect to run once the wait is over: a global trigger name, a zone trigger alias, or a whole task written as one comma-separated value. Only the trigger effect form can supply a value containing commas.

required.name: floats[0]
required.description: Unused in this branch but must be provided as a placeholder, because the wait time is taken from the second number slot.

required.name: floats[1]
required.description: How many seconds to wait before running the effect. This slot is beyond what a trigger effect can supply, so this task needs the full comma-separated form.

tasks.officialDescription: Must be used as a taskString. Executes strings[0] as a dialog specialEffect string after a delay of floats[1] seconds.

tasks.name: nextDialogNode_hideWindow

uses.description: Arms a one-shot flag so that the next dialog node to be displayed shows no speech window at all: the node's lines still run and its effects still fire, but the NPC's text box stays hidden. The flag is consumed by that one node and clears itself immediately afterwards, so following nodes display normally. Starting a fresh conversation also clears it before the first node appears, so it only takes effect within a conversation that is already under way.

tasks.officialDescription: Sets nextDialogNode_hideWindow to true, which hides the next dialog window.

tasks.name: closeCharEdit

uses.description: Closes the character customisation window if it is open, returning the player to whatever was behind it. Nothing else about the character is changed, and nothing happens if the window was not showing.

tasks.officialDescription: Closes the actor name/appearance editor window, if it is open.

tasks.name: gameOver

uses.description: Ends the run: a thunderclap and the game-over music play, the party's held actor and carried items are dropped, the game pauses and blocks input, the count of games lost is bumped by one, and the screen fades out to the main menu. A zone can be marked as one where losing is not possible, and in that zone this instead fires every trigger in the zone that reacts to the game-over element, leaving the player where they are so the mod can handle defeat its own way.

tasks.officialDescription: Ends the game for the player and returns them to the main menu. If the zone has cantGameOver=true, reacts all triggers in the zone with Element.gameOver.

tasks.name: autosaveASAP

uses.description: Asks the game to autosave at the next safe moment rather than immediately. The save waits until combat is over, no queued action is still resolving, the player is not busy, input is not being blocked and no tile effects are running, so it will not interrupt a cutscene or a fight. When that moment arrives an "Autosaved!" message floats up and the autosave is written; if the difficulty rules forbid saving at that point the request is quietly dropped instead. Entering combat is also checked first, so a pending autosave is held back while a battle is starting.

tasks.officialDescription: Creates an autosave if the player is able to save.

tasks.name: speechFX

uses.description: Plays the contextual actor's talking effect at their position, the same blip that accompanies a line of their dialog. Which effect is used comes from the actor's type, so different kinds of character sound different. The task requires a contextual actor to exist, and fails outright if there is none.

tasks.officialDescription: Plays the set fxSpeech FX for the actorType of the currentActorTalkingTo (or current task actor if not in dialog).

tasks.name: fxOnPlayerRank

uses.description: Plays a visual effect at the spot on screen where the player's faction rank is displayed in the escape menu, slightly up and to the left of the rank readout. It is meant to draw the eye to a promotion or a change in standing while that menu is open. The effect is drawn in white and ignores the zone's darkness, and it is placed by screen position, so it appears wherever that panel sits regardless of where the camera is looking.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The ID of the visual effect to play.

tasks.officialDescription: Plays fx 'sValue' at the screen position where the player's rank is on the escMenu.

tasks.name: returnMissingPartyMembers

uses.description: Brings every party member who has gone missing back to the player, placing each on the nearest free tile within three tiles of the player and putting them back on the party roster. Returned members arrive in a bad way: down to a single hit point, with the knocked-out penalty applied, drowning cleared, and briefly invisible for five seconds so they are not immediately attacked. No teleport effect is shown. Nothing happens if nobody is missing.

tasks.officialDescription: Adds any partyActors that fell off of a cliff or drowned back to the player's current party.

tasks.name: modPlayerFactionFavor

uses.description: Changes the player's standing with whichever faction the player currently belongs to, by an amount worked out from a formula. This is the form used whenever no number is given, or the number given is zero. A floating icon with an up or down arrow appears in the middle of the screen and a chime plays for a gain, and the royal quest is re-checked afterwards. Standing is capped at 99 below and at the faction's own ceiling above, and factions that do not track standing ignore the change entirely.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: A formula giving how much to raise or lower the player's standing; negative values lower it. It is evaluated without any actor attached, so it can only use values that do not depend on a particular character.

uses.description: Changes the player's standing with whichever faction the player currently belongs to, by a fixed amount. A floating icon with an up or down arrow appears in the middle of the screen and a chime plays for a gain, and the royal quest is re-checked afterwards. Standing is capped at 99 below and at the faction's own ceiling above, and factions that do not track standing ignore the change entirely. Once the player has reached rank 9 in their own faction, gains are doubled.

required.name: floats[0]
required.description: How much to raise or lower the player's standing; negative values lower it. Zero is not usable here, since it switches the task over to reading the amount from a formula in the first text slot instead.

tasks.officialDescription: Adds 'fValue' or the result of the formula set in sValue to the player's 'favor_' + 'playerFaction' globalVar, if the 'playerFaction' gVar is set.

tasks.name: modTalkerFactionFavor

uses.description: Changes the player's standing with the faction of whoever the player is currently talking to, which lets a conversation reward or punish the player in the eyes of that character's own people. A floating faction icon with an up or down arrow appears in the middle of the screen, and a chime plays for a gain. Standing is capped at 99 below and at that faction's own ceiling above, and factions that do not track standing ignore the change. The task requires a conversation to be in progress with someone present in the zone, and fails outright otherwise.

required.name: floats[0]
required.description: How much to raise or lower the player's standing with that faction; negative values lower it. A value of zero does nothing at all.

tasks.officialDescription: Must be used in dialog. Adds 'fValue' to the player's 'favor_' faction ID globalVar matching the currentActorTalkingTo's set faction.

tasks.name: refreshStatModifiers

uses.description: Recalculates the difficulty-driven stat bonuses on every actor in the zone, and on their crews. Enemy characters have their hidden difficulty bonuses to maximum health, magic, attack and defence stripped and reapplied at the current difficulty multiplier, and the extra ability that harder difficulties grant is added or removed to match. Characters exempt from difficulty adjustment simply have their bonuses removed. Use it after changing the difficulty mid-game so existing characters pick up the new settings instead of keeping the ones they spawned with.

tasks.officialDescription: Resets all enemy stat multipliers, player stat modifiers, boat mods and day bonuses for every actor in the current zone.

tasks.name: storeBoost

uses.description: Remembers that the player's ship was under way at boosted speed, so the boost comes straight back the moment the ship starts moving again instead of needing the usual run-up of continuous sailing. This is meant to be used just before something interrupts sailing, such as a conversation, so the interruption does not cost the player their speed. It only does anything if the ship is actually boosting at the time; otherwise nothing is remembered. The stored boost is used up the first time the player moves again.

tasks.officialDescription: Sets playerActor_storedBoost to true, which will reapply the speed boost the player's ship may have had before being interrupted by a dialog.

tasks.name: recoverOverboardPartyActors

uses.description: Cleans up after a disaster at sea: any of the player's ships that have been sunk or disabled are struck from the fleet, and every party member left in the water is fished out and put aboard the fleet's flagship as crew. The overboard list is emptied, so those characters are back under the player's control. The game normally does this by itself once a battle ends and the player is out of danger; this forces it to happen there and then. It requires the player's fleet to still have at least one ship, and fails outright if every ship was just removed.

tasks.officialDescription: Removes any dead ship actors from the player's fleet and moves their crew to the flagship.

tasks.name: talkToCommodore

uses.description: Switches the conversation over to the commodore of whichever fleet the contextual actor belongs to, which is the first crew member aboard that fleet's flagship. The new conversation opens on the same dialog node that is currently running, and the camera frames the two speakers, so it reads as the same scene continuing with a different speaker. Nothing happens if the player is already talking to that commodore. It requires the contextual actor to belong to a fleet that has a commodore, and fails outright otherwise.

tasks.officialDescription: Enter dialog with the commodore of the fleet the currentActorTalkingTo (or current task actor if not in dialog) is part of, using the currentDialogNodeID.

tasks.name: talkToFirstMate

uses.description: Switches the conversation over to the player's first mate, whose identity is held in the game's "firstmate" global variable. The new conversation opens on the same dialog node that is currently running and the camera frames the two speakers, so the scene reads as continuing with a different speaker. Nothing happens if the player is already talking to them, or if that character is not present in the world or is in no state to talk.

tasks.officialDescription: Enter dialog with the actor ID set in globalVar 'firstmate', using the currentDialogNodeID.

tasks.name: talkToFlagship

uses.description: Switches the conversation over to the flagship of whichever fleet the contextual actor belongs to, continuing on the same dialog node that is currently running with the camera framing both speakers. Nothing happens if the player is already talking to that flagship. If the contextual actor belongs to no fleet the conversation instead falls back to a wordless "..." with nobody. A fleet whose faction is not a defined one is treated as a special case: the smuggler fleet led by Lagan turns pirate on the spot, dropping its merchant status and its normal fleet behaviour, and its flagship opens the aggressive-attack conversation; any other undefined-faction fleet just gets the wordless response.

tasks.officialDescription: Enter dialog with the actor that is the flagship of the fleet the currentActorTalkingTo (or current task actor if not in dialog) is part of.

tasks.name: setupFleetLooting

uses.description: Prepares the spoils after a sea battle. Every surviving, still-crewed enemy ship has its hold emptied and everything lying loose on its deck swept up into the defeated fleet's cargo, which is the pile the player then loots; loose items from any allied fleet's ships and from the player's own ships are gathered into that same pile. Achievements for beating a smuggler, merchant, regular or elite fleet are awarded as appropriate. The boarding view is closed at the end, since the battle is over.

tasks.officialDescription: Sets up the current enemyFleet's cargo inventory to also contain any assist fleet cargo and any items left on player ships, for use with 'lootFleet_afterCombat' task after fleet combat.

tasks.name: captureShips_afterCombat

uses.description: Rewrites an existing dialog node into a menu of the ships the player can take as prizes after a sea battle. Every enemy or allied ship still afloat and still crewed gets a row showing its portrait and name, which captures that ship when picked, alongside a question-mark button that opens its statistics without leaving the menu; a "Done" row at the bottom moves on to looting the fleet. The node's opening line is replaced with a count of the ships on offer, or a note that there are none, and the player's fleet window is opened alongside so they can see what they already have. The changes are written into the node itself, so the node is expected to be a scratch node kept for this purpose rather than one with authored content.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The ID of the dialog node to rebuild as the capture menu. It must already exist and have at least one line of text, since its first line is overwritten and its options are cleared.

tasks.officialDescription: DO NOT USE. Sets up the dialogOptions for the 'sValue' dialogNode with all the ships captured during fleet combat.

tasks.name: captureShipNum

uses.description: Takes one of the ships left over from a sea battle as a prize and adds it to the player's fleet. The ship stops being hostile, joins the player's faction, comes to a halt, has its crew emptied, is repainted in the player's colours, permanently loses two points of maximum hull, and is barred from despawning; it is struck from whichever fleet it belonged to and given a fresh unique ID, so anything that referred to it by its old ID will no longer find it. The player's tally of captured ships goes up and the fleet window refreshes. Nothing happens at all if the player's fleet is already at its limit of nine ships.

required.name: floats[0]
required.description: Which ship to take, counting from 0 through the surviving, still-crewed ships of the defeated fleet and then any allied fleet, in that order. A number past the end of that list stops the task with an error.

tasks.officialDescription: DO NOT USE. Adds the ship actor in slot 'fValue' of the ships captured during fleet combat to the player's fleet, if there are any available slots.

tasks.name: lootFleet_afterCombat

uses.description: Opens the looting screen after a sea battle: the player's own cargo hold appears on one side and the defeated fleet's spoils on the other, side by side and without close buttons, so the only way out is through the conversation that opened them. Anything an allied fleet gathered is folded into the same pile first, so it can all be taken in one go. The list-view toggle on the spoils panel is hidden and the conversation window shrinks out of the way.

tasks.officialDescription: Opens the enemyFleet cargo inventory so the player can loot it.

tasks.name: openFleetWindow

uses.description: Opens the fleet panel showing the player's ships, each with its crew, health and the buttons for editing, scrapping or selling it. A soft thunk plays and the panel pops into view if it was not already showing; if it was, its contents are simply brought up to date. Nothing happens if the player has no ships.

tasks.officialDescription: Shows the player's fleet information window.

tasks.name: openFleetWindow_delay

uses.description: Opens the fleet panel showing the player's ships a tenth of a second later rather than at once, which lets whatever is closing or changing on screen settle first before the panel appears. Apart from the short pause it does the same thing as opening the panel immediately, and nothing happens if the player has no ships. Queuing another delayed open replaces any earlier one that still had longer to wait.

tasks.officialDescription: Shows the player's fleet information window after a 0.1s delay.

tasks.name: openFleetWindow_talker

uses.description: Opens the fleet panel showing the ships of whichever fleet the contextual actor belongs to, rather than the player's own, so a conversation with a captain can show off the fleet they command. Each ship is listed with its crew and health. A soft thunk plays as the panel appears if it was not already open. Nothing happens if the contextual actor belongs to no fleet or that fleet has no ships.

tasks.officialDescription: Shows the fleet information window for the fleet the currentActorTalkingTo (or current task actor if not in dialog) is part of.

tasks.name: closeFleetWindow

uses.description: Hides the fleet panel. It refuses to close while the player is sailing the world map and holding a character picked up from the panel, so a character being moved between ships cannot be stranded by closing the panel out from under them.

tasks.officialDescription: Closes the fleet information window, if it is open and the player isn't holding an actor.

tasks.name: showFleetInfo

uses.description: Rewrites an existing dialog node into a browsable list of the ships in the contextual actor's fleet. Each ship gets a row with its portrait, its name and a question-mark icon that opens that ship class's own information page, with the ship's statistics shown as a tooltip; a "Done" row at the bottom returns to the fleet conversation and doubles as the escape option. The node's text is replaced with the game's own fleet summary and the conversation window is enlarged to fit the list. The changes are written into the node itself, so it should be a scratch node kept for this purpose. It requires the contextual actor to belong to a fleet, and fails outright otherwise.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The ID of the dialog node to rebuild as the fleet listing. It must already exist and have at least one line of text, since its first line is overwritten and its options and effects are cleared.

tasks.officialDescription: Sets up the dialogOptions for dialogNode 'sValue' for selecting ships to inspect when inspecting the fleet the currentActorTalkingTo belongs to.

tasks.name: repairFleet_pay

uses.description: Charges the player for repairs and then patches up every ship in their fleet to full health, also wiping the saved damage inside each ship's interior so nothing is left broken below decks. The bill is ten coins for every point of hull missing across the whole fleet, discounted by the player's standing and rank with the faction that runs the port they are in, down to a minimum of one coin per point. The money is taken whether or not the player can afford it, so this is meant to sit behind a conversation option that has already checked their purse.

tasks.officialDescription: Repairs all ships in the player's fleet and removes the repair cost from their gold.

tasks.name: repairFleet_free

uses.description: Patches up every ship in the player's fleet to full health at no cost, and wipes the saved state of each ship's interior so nothing is left damaged below decks. Anything the player left lying about inside their ships is cleared away along with it.

tasks.officialDescription: Repairs all ships in the player's fleet, for free.

tasks.name: help

uses.description: Prints the description of one developer console command as an on-screen debug message, which stays up for about ten seconds. Nothing is printed if the name given is not a console command. This is a debugging aid rather than something to use in shipped content.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The name of the console command to describe. It must match a console command name exactly; anything else produces no output.

uses.description: Prints the full list of developer console command names as an on-screen debug message, wrapped to the width of the screen, along with a reminder that naming one of them shows more detail about it. The message stays up for about ten seconds. This is a debugging aid rather than something to use in shipped content.

tasks.officialDescription: prints a description of the command (ex: help revive)

tasks.name: csave

uses.description: Writes a full save of the current game under a name of your choosing, complete with a preview image, and renames the running game to match so later saves continue under that name. It is a debugging convenience rather than the save the game makes for the player, and it overwrites any existing save of the same name.

optional.name: strings[0]
optional.description: The name to save under. Trailing spaces are trimmed off. Defaults to "consoleSave".

tasks.officialDescription: DO NOT USE. Forces a save to be made named 'sValue', or 'consoleSave' if not specified.

tasks.name: testitemload

uses.description: Drops one of a chosen item on every single tile of the current zone, forcing them to fit even where they normally could not. It exists to stress-test item handling, and on a large zone it will litter the map with thousands of items, so it is a debugging tool rather than something to use in content.

optional.name: strings[0]
optional.description: The ID of the item type to scatter. Defaults to the toy boat.

tasks.officialDescription: puts 1 item on every tile. Default ID: toyboat.

tasks.name: howmanyitems

uses.description: Counts the items lying on the ground across the whole zone and shows the total as an on-screen debug message for about ten seconds. Naming an item type counts how many of that item there are, adding up stack sizes; leaving it out counts every separate pile on the ground instead, regardless of what is in them. It is a debugging aid rather than something to use in content.

optional.name: strings[0]
optional.description: The ID of the item type to count. Leave it out, or give an empty value, to count every pile on the ground instead of the quantity of one item.

tasks.officialDescription: counts items in the zone. Counts all items if ID not specified.

tasks.name: convertRGB

uses.description: Takes a PNG image sitting on the desktop of whoever is running the game, forces every pixel down to whichever of red, green or blue was strongest in it, and writes the result back to the desktop with "_rgb" added to the name. Pure white pixels are left alone. It is an art tool for turning a shaded sprite into the flat three-channel mask the palette system expects, and it does nothing to the running game.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The name of the image file on the desktop, without the .png extension. The converted copy is written next to it under the same name with "_rgb" appended.

tasks.officialDescription: loads (param).png from desktop and palettizes it (removes excess RGB so all pixels are only R, G, or B) then saves to desktop

tasks.name: screenshot

uses.description: Loads a second map as an overlay, photographs it centred on a chosen tile, and writes the picture to the desktop of whoever is running the game as a PNG named after how long the game has been running. Before saving, the picture is flattened so every pixel becomes pure red, green or blue and is then recoloured through a single palette, which is how the game's own ship and structure artwork is produced. The overlay is discarded afterwards and its wavy drawing style is turned off for the shot. Interface elements are left out of the picture.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The palette used to recolour the flattened picture. The same palette is applied to all three colour channels.

required.name: strings[1]
required.description: The ID of the zone to load as the overlay and photograph. Supplying this second text value is what switches the task from photographing the current map to photographing an overlay.

required.name: floats[0]
required.description: The horizontal tile the picture is centred on.

required.name: floats[1]
required.description: The vertical tile the picture is centred on.

optional.name: floats[2]
optional.description: The width of the picture in pixels. Defaults to the width of the game window, and is only read when a height is supplied as well.

optional.name: floats[3]
optional.description: The height of the picture in pixels. Defaults to the height of the game window. This slot is beyond what a trigger effect can supply.

optional.name: floats[4]
optional.description: How far the camera is zoomed in for the picture. Defaults to the camera's current zoom. This slot is beyond what a trigger effect can supply.

optional.name: bools[0]
optional.description: Whether port and settlement markers are drawn into the picture. Defaults to true.

tasks.name: anim

uses.description: Makes the player's character perform a named animation, clears any developer messages currently on screen, and drops the game back into ordinary overworld control. It is a console convenience for previewing animations rather than a way to animate characters in content. Nothing visible happens if no animation by that name exists, and leaving the name out prints a reminder of how to use it instead.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The ID of the animation for the player to perform.

tasks.officialDescription: makes the player perform the specified animation (ex: anim crouch)

tasks.name: fullheal

uses.description: Puts the whole party back to perfect condition. Everyone is revived and stands up, all status effects and morale penalties are cleared, the maximum health lost to being knocked out is given back, health and magic are refilled, anything being charged or cast is cancelled, and fatigue is wiped out entirely. It is the same restoration a night's rest provides, applied at once and in full.

tasks.officialDescription: Fully heals playerParty, including HPMax lost from being KO'd.

tasks.name: testboatanim

uses.description: Returns control to whatever mode the game was in before the current one, then replays the ship-boarding sequence: the camera locks onto the join between the two vessels and a shuffled selection of the boarding ship's crew leap across one after another onto the boarded deck, landing on its boarding points and turning to face the fight. It is a preview tool for that cutscene. It requires a boarding already set up, with both ships chosen and the boarded ship loaded as an overlay, and fails outright otherwise.

tasks.officialDescription: DO NOT USE.

tasks.name: bighead

uses.description: Turns the novelty big-head display on or off for every character in the game: heads and faces are drawn at double size and nudged upward to sit properly on the body. Called with nothing it flips the setting, so running it twice returns everything to normal. It only changes how characters are drawn and has no effect on the game itself.

optional.name: bools[0]
optional.description: Pass true to force big heads on regardless of the current setting. Passing false does not force it off; the setting is flipped first either way, so false leaves the flip in place.

tasks.officialDescription: reveals the true self

tasks.name: screenscale

uses.description: Pins the game's pixel magnification to a fixed factor instead of letting it be chosen automatically from the window height, and applies it straight away. The setting is remembered in the save. Passing -1 hands control back to the automatic sizing, which picks half, single, one-and-a-half or double magnification depending on how tall the window is.

required.name: floats[0]
required.description: The magnification factor to pin the display to, where 1 is one screen pixel per game pixel. Pass -1 to return to picking the factor automatically from the window size.

tasks.officialDescription: Sets the forcedScreenScale game option to 'fValue'. Set it to -1 to disable it.

tasks.name: res

uses.description: Switches the game to a windowed 1920 by 959 display. The size is fixed and cannot be changed by the task; it is a shortcut for getting the window to a known size while testing, particularly for capturing footage.

tasks.officialDescription: Changes the game window's size to 1920x959, which is the highest resolution before the screen scale changes.

tasks.name: go

uses.description: Fades out and loads another map, dropping the party on an exact tile of your choosing. The arrival is marked as a debug entry, so the destination's entry triggers, zone effects, weather spawns, merged-in zone pieces and first NPC turn are all skipped and the map is simply there. Nothing happens if the zone name contains a backslash.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The ID of the zone to load.

required.name: floats[0]
required.description: The horizontal tile to place the party on in the new zone.

required.name: floats[1]
required.description: The vertical tile to place the party on in the new zone.

uses.description: Fades out and loads another map, dropping the party at its first arrival point, the same spot an ordinary entrance would use. The arrival is marked as a debug entry, so the destination's entry triggers, zone effects, weather spawns, merged-in zone pieces and first NPC turn are all skipped and the map is simply there. Nothing happens if the zone name contains a backslash.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The ID of the zone to load.

tasks.officialDescription: transitions to specified zone (ex: go zoneName)

tasks.name: gob

uses.description: Fades out, loads another map and drops straight into the map editor there, with the party placed on an exact tile of your choosing. The arrival is marked as a debug entry, so the destination's entry triggers, zone effects, weather spawns, merged-in zone pieces and first NPC turn are all skipped; building mode additionally freezes characters and actions and holds back the lighting, item timers and crew upkeep that a normal arrival runs. Nothing happens if the zone name contains a backslash.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The ID of the zone to load.

required.name: floats[0]
required.description: The horizontal tile to place the party on in the new zone.

required.name: floats[1]
required.description: The vertical tile to place the party on in the new zone.

The arrival is marked as a debug entry, so the destination's entry triggers, zone effects, weather spawns, merged-in zone pieces and first NPC turn are all skipped; building mode additionally freezes characters and actions and holds back the lighting, item timers and crew upkeep that a normal arrival runs. Nothing happens if the zone name contains a backslash.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The ID of the zone to load.

tasks.officialDescription: transitions to specified zone and enters build mode (ex: gob zoneName)

tasks.name: p

uses.description: Generates a fresh randomly built map from a named level recipe, then fades out and loads it, placing the party ten tiles in from the top-left corner. The generated map is named after the recipe with "p_" in front, and any record of triggers already used up in a map of that name is wiped so it starts clean. By default the arrival is treated as a debug entry, so the new map's entry triggers, effects and weather spawns are skipped. It requires the level recipe to exist and fails outright otherwise.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The ID of the level recipe to build the map from. The generated map takes this name with "p_" prefixed.

optional.name: bools[0]
optional.description: Whether to arrive quietly as a debug entry, skipping the new map's entry triggers, effects and weather spawns. Defaults to true; pass false to arrive as a player normally would.

tasks.officialDescription: Creates an example procedurally generated zone using 'sValue' levelData, then transfers the player to it at TC 10,10. If b1, acts as if entering via console.

tasks.name: world

uses.description: Generates a whole multi-map region from a named level recipe — a grid of connected maps, with the recipe's required centrepieces and set pieces scattered through it at random — discarding any previously saved version of those maps, then fades out and loads the region's first map with the party twelve tiles in from the corner. The arrival is treated as a debug entry, so entry triggers, effects and weather spawns are skipped. If no recipe by that name exists, an error is shown on screen and nothing else happens.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The ID of the level recipe describing the region to build. The maps are named after it, and the one loaded is its top-left corner.

tasks.officialDescription: DO NOT USE.

tasks.name: loads

uses.description: Fades out and loads a saved game by name from the game's own internal save folder rather than the player's save slots. Any pending confirmation prompt is dismissed and queued movement orders are cleared before the load begins. It is a debugging shortcut for jumping into a known save state.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The name of the save to load, as it appears in the game's internal save folder.

tasks.officialDescription: DO NOT USE.

tasks.name: z

uses.description: Lists the hand-built maps available in the game's zone data, printed on screen as a debug message wrapped to the width of the window. Randomly generated maps, set pieces, groves, dens and ship interiors are left out, so what remains is the authored maps you can jump to. It is a debugging aid for finding a map name.

optional.name: strings[0]
optional.description: Narrows the list to maps whose names begin with "z" followed by this text, ignoring capitalisation. Leave it out to list them all.

tasks.officialDescription: show list of all saved zones. Returns results that start w/ given param. (ex: z house)

tasks.name: sp

uses.description: Lists the set pieces available in the game's zone data — the prefabricated chunks that randomly generated maps are assembled from — printed on screen as a debug message wrapped to the width of the window. Ordinary hand-built maps are left out. It is a debugging aid for finding a set piece name.

optional.name: strings[0]
optional.description: Narrows the list to set pieces whose names begin with "sp" followed by this text, ignoring capitalisation. Leave it out to list them all.

tasks.officialDescription: show list of all saved setPieces. Returns results that start w/ given param. (ex: sp puzzle)

tasks.name: bz

tasks.officialDescription: show list of all saved zones that start with 'bz'.

tasks.name: listfx

It is a debugging aid for inspecting how an effect is set up. Naming an effect that does not exist falls back to listing every effect name instead.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The ID of the visual effect to describe.

tasks.officialDescription: lists all FX. (scroll using mousewheel) Specify an FX to view its data.

tasks.name: listav

uses.description: Prints the full definition of one character statistic on screen as a debug message, listing every property it was defined with and its current value. It is a debugging aid for inspecting how a statistic is set up. Naming a statistic that does not exist falls back to listing every statistic name instead.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The ID of the character statistic to describe.
