Statistics that only exist to track ranks and experience are left out, so what remains is the ones worth reading or changing. This is also what happens if a name is given that matches no statistic.

tasks.officialDescription: lists all ActorValues. (scroll using mousewheel) Specify an ActorValue to view its data.

tasks.name: k

uses.description: Prints the player's running tally of kills by kind of creature on screen as a debug message, each kind followed by how many have been killed, wrapped to the width of the window. It is a debugging aid for checking progress on kill-count conditions.

tasks.officialDescription: show kills

tasks.name: kill

uses.description: Instantly kills every hostile character in the zone that the player does not control, by dealing them an unsurvivable amount of damage. Characters marked invincible are left alone, and so is anyone whose ID you list. It is a debugging shortcut for ending a fight.

optional.name: strings[0+]
optional.description: Any number of actor IDs to spare. Each text value is one ID; a character whose ID appears among them is not killed. Leave them out to kill every eligible hostile character.

tasks.officialDescription: kill everything but the party

tasks.name: killall

uses.description: Instantly kills every character in the zone that the player does not control, friendly and hostile alike, by dealing them an unsurvivable amount of damage. Only characters marked invincible survive. It is a debugging shortcut for clearing a map.

tasks.officialDescription: Incaps all non-controllable actors in the zone that don't have the 'invincible' AV.

tasks.name: killcrew

uses.description: Kills the entire crew aboard every ship in the zone that the player does not control, then marks each of those ships as crewless so it stops fighting and drifts. The ships themselves take no damage. It is a debugging shortcut for disabling an enemy fleet without sinking it.

tasks.officialDescription: kill all crew on non-player ships

tasks.name: reviveall

uses.description: Brings every fallen character in the zone back to their feet in perfect condition: revived, fully healed, all status effects and fatigue cleared, maximum health restored and anything they were busy with cancelled. Characters whose IDs you list are left where they fell. Nobody is allowed to vanish partway through the revival, so characters that would normally despawn stay put.

optional.name: strings[0+]
optional.description: Any number of actor IDs to leave down. Each text value is one ID; a fallen character whose ID appears among them is not revived. Leave them out to revive everyone.

tasks.officialDescription: Revives all incapacitated actors in the current zone except any actors whose ID is set in strings[], then fully heals them.

tasks.name: win

uses.description: Ends the current battle immediately as a victory, no matter what is still standing on the field. Experience owed for the fight is handed out, everyone stops charging and casting, and the reactions that normally fire at the end of combat run as usual. Because the ending is forced, restrictions that would normally hold the battle open are bypassed and the usual post-battle autosave is skipped. It is a debugging shortcut for skipping a fight.

tasks.officialDescription: win the current combat

tasks.name: setk

uses.description: Sets or bumps the player's recorded kill count for one kind of character, the tally that decides how much experience that kind is still worth and that kill-count conditions read. If no tally exists for that kind yet, one is started at zero first. It is a debugging shortcut for putting the kill records into a particular state.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The ID of the kind of character whose kill count is being changed.

required.name: strings[1]
required.description: The number to set the kill count to, written as text. Leave it empty to add one to the existing count instead of replacing it. Because a plain number written in a taskString would be taken as a number rather than a string, it has to be forced into a text slot, and text that does not read as a number stops the task with an error.

tasks.officialDescription: sets kill count to # (ex: set antiair 1)

tasks.name: set

uses.description: Writes a piece of text into a named global variable, the game's own store of remembered facts. Everything after the variable name is joined together with single spaces, so a value containing spaces can be typed as several separate values. Spaces in the stored value are kept as an escape sequence rather than literal spaces, which is how the game stores them. The royal quest is re-checked afterwards in case the change affects it.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The name of the global variable to write.

required.name: strings[1+]
required.description: The text to store. Any further text values after this one are appended onto it with a single space between each. An empty first value falls back to storing a number, or 1 if no number is given.

uses.description: Writes a number into a named global variable, the game's own store of remembered facts. This is the form used when no text value follows the variable name. The royal quest is re-checked afterwards in case the change affects it.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The name of the global variable to write.

required.name: floats[0]
required.description: The number to store. It is only used when no text value was supplied for the variable, or the text value was empty.

uses.description: Sets a named global variable to 1, the game's usual way of marking a fact as true. This is the form used when neither a text value nor a number follows the variable name. The royal quest is re-checked afterwards in case the change affects it.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The name of the global variable to set to 1.

tasks.officialDescription: sets a global variable to # (ex: set rescuedShroom 1)

tasks.name: get

uses.description: Looks up a name and prints what it holds as an on-screen debug message. A global variable prints its stored value; a zone name prints the numbers of the triggers already used up in that zone; anything else is evaluated as a formula, worked out with the player as both the caster and the target, and its result is printed. A long formula also has its result repeated on a separate line so it can be read.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The name to look up. It is tried first as a global variable, then as the name of a zone whose used-up triggers should be listed, and failing both it is evaluated as a formula.

uses.description: Prints every global variable and its value on screen as a debug message, one per line. Variables whose names begin with the dialog bookkeeping prefix are left out, so the list stays readable. It is a debugging aid for seeing the whole remembered state at once.

tasks.officialDescription: prints value of global variable - or prints flagged triggers of given zoneName (ex: get zTown1)

tasks.name: formulas

uses.description: Prints every named shared formula the game has loaded on screen as a debug message, each under its own name with the expression it stands for. It is a debugging aid for seeing what the reusable formulas expand to.

tasks.officialDescription: lists out all globalFormulas

tasks.name: sanitizecheck

uses.description: Shows what a piece of text looks like after the game strips it down for loose comparison — spaces, colons, minus signs, arithmetic operators, full stops and commas removed and everything lowercased — printed on screen as a debug message. It is how the game decides whether two names the player typed mean the same thing, so this is the way to check why two spellings do or do not match. The values given are joined together first, separated by spaces when typed at the console and by commas otherwise.

optional.name: strings[0+]
optional.description: Any number of text values to join together and sanitise. Supplying none prints an empty result.

tasks.officialDescription: shows what the provided string would look like when formatted for formula checks.

uses.description: Takes whatever was typed after the command name at the developer console, parses it as a task, and prints the result broken down piece by piece: which task it resolved to, its delay, its requirement formula, and every text, number, true/false and coordinate value it produced, each labelled with its slot. It is the way to check how a comma-separated task will actually be read before relying on it. Existing debug messages are cleared first so only the breakdown is showing. Outside the developer console it prints an error and does nothing.

tasks.name: calc

uses.description: Works out a formula and prints its result on screen as a debug message, labelled with the expression that produced it. The formula is evaluated with the player's character as the one performing it and nobody as the target, so anything that reads the target's properties comes out as nothing. It is a debugging aid for checking what an expression evaluates to in the current game state.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The formula to evaluate.

tasks.officialDescription: prints result of specified formula (ex: calc c:PhysAtk)

tasks.name: resetfog

uses.description: Closes the fog of war back over the whole of the current map, marking every tile as never having been seen. The map and minimap go dark again outside what is currently in view, as though the player had just arrived. It is a debugging shortcut for testing exploration.

tasks.officialDescription: sets entire zone's fog of war to unknown

tasks.name: clearfog

uses.description: Lifts the fog of war from the whole of the current map, marking every tile as already seen, and rebuilds the minimap so the change shows straight away. On the world map it additionally marks every discoverable place there as found, so ports and settlements appear on the chart. It is a debugging shortcut for revealing a map.

tasks.officialDescription: sets entire zone's fog of war to known

tasks.name: hidemapicons

uses.description: Hides every place marker on the world map by marking all of the places on it as undiscovered, so ports and settlements disappear from the chart until the player finds them again. It only does anything while the player is actually on the world map; in any other zone it does nothing at all.

tasks.officialDescription: If the player is currently in the overworld zone, sets all locations to discovered = false.

tasks.name: removeitems

uses.description: Sweeps the ground clean across the whole of the current map, removing items from every tile. Naming an item type removes only that item; leaving the name out removes everything lying about. Items held by characters or stored in containers are not touched.

optional.name: strings[0]
optional.description: The ID of the item type to remove. Leave it out to remove every item on the ground instead.

tasks.officialDescription: removes all items (or all items of the ID specified in sValue) from the zone.

tasks.name: clearroofs

uses.description: Removes every roof piece from the whole of the current map, so all interiors are left open to the sky and nothing is hidden from view above the player. It is a debugging shortcut for seeing inside buildings.

tasks.officialDescription: removes all roof items

tasks.name: clearactors

uses.description: Removes every character from the current map, leaving the party behind. A formula can be given to narrow it down, in which case only characters the formula comes out positive for are removed and the rest are left alone. The characters are taken out of the world rather than killed, so nothing dies and no death effects fire.

optional.name: strings[0]
optional.description: A formula deciding which characters to remove, evaluated for each candidate with that character as both the one performing it and the target; a result above zero means remove them. Leave it out, or give an empty value, to remove every non-party character.

tasks.officialDescription: Removes all non-party actors from the current zone. If sValue is set, it should be an fReq that will get checked for each actor.

tasks.name: deleteZone

uses.description: Permanently deletes a map's source files from the game's zone data, both its layout image and its accompanying text, and says so on screen. This is not an undo-able change to a save; the authored map itself is gone. It only works while the developer console is open, and does nothing anywhere else.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The ID of the zone whose source files are to be deleted.

tasks.officialDescription: permanently deletes original zone data. Do not use.

tasks.name: forget

uses.description: Throws away everything the save remembers about one map — its stored layout changes, its explored fog, and the record of which of its triggers have already fired — so the next visit builds it fresh from the authored map. Anything the player left lying there, and any changes they made, are lost. The map's own source files are untouched. With the developer console open it also reports whether the map was found; otherwise it works silently and does nothing if there is no such map.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The ID of the zone to forget.

tasks.officialDescription: clears saved memory of specified zone.

tasks.name: resetlocation

uses.description: Restores one place on the world map to the state it was defined with, throwing away whatever it had accumulated, and runs its first-visit setup again so it is stocked and populated as though the player had never been there. Every other place is left exactly as it was. Item timers are held back while it is rebuilt so nothing spoils or expires during the rebuild.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The ID of the place to restore to its defined state.

tasks.officialDescription: Resets location ID 'sValue' or all ports/locations to their default data if not specified.

tasks.name: resetlocations

uses.description: Wipes every place on the world map and rebuilds the whole set from the game's own location definitions, including any a mod adds, then regenerates the randomly placed ones and discards the stored copies of set-piece maps. Everything the player had changed about any place is lost. It is a heavy debugging reset for the world map's contents.

tasks.officialDescription: Resets all ports/locations to their default data.

tasks.name: refreshloc

uses.description: Adds any places that are defined but missing from the current game, without touching the ones already there, which is how a save picks up locations newly added by a mod or a game update. Nothing is reset or restocked; only genuinely absent places are added. It does nothing at the main menu or before a map has loaded.

tasks.officialDescription: Loads any missing locations and adds their locationItems to the zoneThisLocationIsIn.

tasks.name: resetprocgen

uses.description: Scatters the world map's randomly placed locations afresh: the counts of groves found and encounters used are zeroed, every set piece is marked as not yet placed, and the random placement runs again from scratch, discarding the stored copies of the maps it had generated. A note confirming this appears on screen. It only works while the player is on the world map, and prints an error anywhere else.

tasks.officialDescription: Recreates all procedurally generated groves in the overworld.

tasks.name: resetwaypoints

uses.description: Rebuilds the current map's travel network from scratch, discarding the existing one. Every waypoint marker on the ground becomes a node, every place on the map becomes a node, and the connections between them are worked out again. Use it after adding or moving waypoint markers so wandering characters and ships start using the new routes.

tasks.officialDescription: re-initializes waypoints for the current zone.

tasks.name: build

uses.description: Switches the game into the map editor. The terrain and item palettes open, the game pauses, the camera stops following the player, fog of war and line of sight are turned off so the whole map is visible, buried items and trigger outlines are drawn, and the usual play interface is hidden. Nothing happens if the editor is already open.

tasks.officialDescription: force build mode (such as during combat)

tasks.name: overseer

uses.description: Switches the game into overseer mode, the detached view used when the player commands a settlement or a fleet rather than walking around as one character. There is no player character to follow, the character stats, quickslots and minimap are hidden, the stash and open-all buttons appear in place of the map and wait buttons, and the party roster is refreshed. Nothing happens if the game is already in that mode.

tasks.officialDescription: Forces overseerMode on.

tasks.name: godmode

uses.description: Makes the player's character effectively unkillable and fully equipped: 999 is added to their health and magic and to both maximums, 99 to each defence, and every ability belonging to every playable class is raised by nine ranks, so the character can use anything in the game. Nothing happens if there is no player character at the time. It is a debugging shortcut and the changes are permanent additions, not a toggle.

tasks.officialDescription: Maxes out the player's HP/MP and other stats and learns all actions from every selectable class.

tasks.name: abil

uses.description: Raises every ability belonging to every playable class on the player's character, so they can use anything in the game. The amount added is the same for each ability. It is a debugging shortcut, and the increase is added on top of what the character already has rather than setting a level.

optional.name: floats[0]
optional.description: How many ranks to add to each ability. Fractions are dropped. Defaults to 9.

tasks.officialDescription: learn all abilities (up to rank #)

tasks.name: xp

uses.description: Awards experience to every member of the party, in their current class, with the usual floating numbers and level-up handling. The amount is shared out the way experience normally is, so a larger party earns less each. It is a debugging shortcut for levelling the party up quickly.

optional.name: floats[0]
optional.description: How much experience to award each party member. Fractions are dropped, and zero or less awards nothing. Defaults to 9999.

tasks.officialDescription: add # XP in current class

tasks.name: crewxp

uses.description: Awards experience to the whole party at once as an area effect centred on where they stand, complete with rising sparkles and a chime over each group. Party members sharing a tile with someone else are handled separately so nobody is missed. Awarding zero or less does nothing.

optional.name: floats[0]
optional.description: How much experience to award. Fractions are dropped. Defaults to 0, which awards nothing at all, so a value is needed for this to do anything.

tasks.officialDescription: Gives 'fValue' XP to all of the player's crew members.

tasks.name: allxp

uses.description: Awards experience to every member of the party once for each playable class in the game, so everyone advances in all classes at once rather than only the one they are currently in. The usual floating numbers, level-ups and party-size scaling all apply, once per class. It is a debugging shortcut for producing a fully developed party.

optional.name: floats[0]
optional.description: How much experience to award in each class. Fractions are dropped, and zero or less awards nothing. Defaults to 9999.

tasks.officialDescription: add # XP in all classes

tasks.name: xpcosts

uses.description: Prints, for each playable class that has any abilities, the total experience it takes to learn all of them, shown on screen as a debug message labelled with the class name. Classes with no abilities are skipped. It is a balancing aid for comparing how expensive the classes are relative to one another.

tasks.officialDescription: lists total XP required to master each class (not including passives)

tasks.name: testskillcost

uses.description: Works out and prints the first twelve steps of a cost curve, so a designer can see what an ability's rank costs would look like before committing to the numbers. Each step is the base plus the increment times the step number, all multiplied by the multiplier raised to that step, rounded down to a whole number, and the twelve results are printed on screen as a comma-separated debug message. Supplying fewer than three numbers prints a reminder of what is needed instead.

required.name: floats[0]
required.description: The base cost of the first step. Fractions are dropped.

required.name: floats[1]
required.description: How much is added to the base for each step beyond the first.

required.name: floats[2]
required.description: The factor each step is multiplied by, compounding over the steps; 1 gives a straight line.

tasks.officialDescription: DO NOT USE.

tasks.name: allclass

uses.description: Unlocks every playable class. Each class's unlock condition is satisfied — by setting the global variable the class checks, or a variable named after the class where the condition is not a simple check — and every class is added to the list of ones the party knows about. On top of that a blanket override is turned on that makes every class count as known, usable and stat-requirement-met regardless of who is asking, and the class display is refreshed so the change shows at once.

tasks.officialDescription: unlocks all classes

tasks.name: gp

uses.description: Adds money to the player's purse. A negative amount takes money away, and it is not stopped from going below zero. It is a debugging shortcut for testing prices and purchases.

optional.name: floats[0]
optional.description: How much money to add. Fractions are dropped. Defaults to 500.

tasks.officialDescription: adds # GP (or gives 500 if unspecified)

tasks.name: tfl

uses.description: Flips the frame rate limit on or off at the start of the next frame. With the limit off the game runs as fast as the machine allows and no longer waits for the display refresh; with it on it is capped to a fixed step. It is a debugging tool for performance testing, and running it again puts it back.

tasks.officialDescription: toggles 60 fps limit

tasks.name: tm

uses.description: Flips the whole interface on or off while the player is walking around, sailing or fighting: the windows, panels and readouts stop being drawn, leaving a clean view of the world. Floating experience effects are suppressed while it is hidden as well. Menus still show in other modes, such as the map editor. Running it again brings the interface back.

tasks.officialDescription: toggles menus & many other elements

tasks.name: tt

uses.description: Flips tooltips on or off. With them off, hovering over a button, item or ability shows no explanatory box at all. Running it again brings them back.

tasks.officialDescription: toggles tooltips

tasks.name: tdm

uses.description: Flips the floating numbers on or off — the damage, healing and status figures that pop up over characters as things happen. With them off the effects still occur, they are simply not announced on screen. Running it again brings them back.

tasks.officialDescription: toggles damage numbers

tasks.name: tq

uses.description: Flips a hard override that keeps the quickslot bar, the character stat readouts, the travel information panel and the travel and combat command bars hidden no matter what else would show them. It overrules the game's normal rules about when those panels appear. Running it again releases the override.

tasks.officialDescription: toggles quickslots & charstats

tasks.name: tc

uses.description: Flips whether battles are allowed to start at all, and reports the new setting on screen. With combat disabled, nothing can pull the party into a fight — hostile characters simply never initiate one. Running it again allows battles once more.

tasks.officialDescription: toggles being able to enter combat

tasks.name: tcui

uses.description: Flips a hard override that keeps the combat interface and the travel information panel hidden throughout a battle, leaving a clean view of the field. It overrules the game's normal rules about when those panels appear. Running it again releases the override.

tasks.officialDescription: toggles combat ui

tasks.name: tw

uses.description: Flips the drawing of trigger outlines on or off, painting a coloured box over every trigger area in the map so their extents can be seen while playing. It is the same overlay the map editor shows. Running it again hides them.

tasks.officialDescription: toggles wires

tasks.name: realtime

uses.description: Flips real-time mode on or off. In real-time mode the world does not wait for the player between actions: characters that are not in a battle act as soon as they are able rather than taking turns in step with the player, and timed effects run on the clock rather than on turns. Running it again returns to the normal turn-based pacing. The change only takes hold in maps loaded afterwards, since each map takes a copy of the setting when it loads.

tasks.officialDescription: toggles realtime mode (probably very buggy)

tasks.name: hideparty

uses.description: Makes every party member invisible for what amounts to forever, hiding them from view so the map can be looked at or photographed without them in the way. They are still present and can still be interacted with; only their drawing is suppressed. There is no matching command to undo it, so it is a one-way debugging tool.

tasks.officialDescription: hides the party forever

tasks.name: mpos

uses.description: Flips a readout of the mouse pointer's position on screen, updated every frame as a debug message. It is an aid for lining things up while building or debugging. Running it again hides it.

tasks.officialDescription: toggle show mouse screen (not world) coordinates.

tasks.name: rankstyle

uses.description: Flips how an ability's rank is drawn on its icon between two styles: small gems, or notches. It is purely a display choice and changes nothing about the abilities themselves. Running it again switches back.

tasks.officialDescription: Toggles class action rank's notch style on/off. Does not get saved.

tasks.name: clearjournal

uses.description: Empties the player's journal completely, then puts back only the entries the game starts every new game with, silently and without the usual new-entry alert. Everything the player had discovered is forgotten. It is a debugging shortcut for testing how the journal fills up.

tasks.officialDescription: remove all journal entries

tasks.name: filljournal

uses.description: Adds every journal entry in the game to the player's journal at once, skipping any already known, and sorts the result back into its usual categories. No alerts or sounds are played for the additions. It is a debugging shortcut for reading or checking the whole journal.

tasks.officialDescription: add all journal entries

tasks.name: debug

uses.description: Flips developer debugging on or off and reports the new setting on screen. While it is on, the game complains loudly about problems in mod files, such as missing semicolons, reports formula and fleet trouble, shows the AI's decision thresholds, and puts the frame rate in the window's title bar. It is the setting to turn on while writing a mod. Running it again turns it back off.

tasks.officialDescription: Toggles debugMode on/off.

tasks.name: debugMessage

uses.description: Prints a message on screen as a debug message under a label of your choosing, staying up for about ten seconds. Printing again under the same label replaces the previous message rather than adding a second one, which makes it useful for a value that keeps changing.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The label the message is filed under. Reusing a label replaces whatever was shown under it before.

required.name: strings[1]
required.description: The text to show.

uses.description: Prints a message on screen as a debug message under the label "Debug", staying up for about ten seconds. Printing again this way replaces the previous message rather than adding a second one.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The text to show.

tasks.officialDescription: Displays a debug message using 'sValue' as the type and 'sValue2' as the message.

tasks.name: errors

uses.description: Flips whether the game shows a crash report when something goes badly wrong, and reports the new setting on screen. With it off, an unhandled failure is swallowed silently instead of raising a report. The setting is remembered in the save.

tasks.officialDescription: Toggles crash error reporting on/off.

tasks.name: resize

uses.description: Resizes the game window to an exact number of pixels wide and tall. The change is applied on the next frame, and the pixel magnification is then recalculated from the new height unless it has been pinned. It is a debugging tool for getting the window to a known size.

required.name: floats[0]
required.description: The new window width in pixels. Fractions are dropped.

required.name: floats[1]
required.description: The new window height in pixels. Fractions are dropped.

tasks.officialDescription: Must be used as a taskString. Changes the game window's size to floats[0] pixels by floats[1] pixels.

tasks.name: setBPC

uses.description: Adjusts, in the running game, where one body part is attached on a body layout when the character is facing a particular way. The direction it applies to is whichever way the player's character is currently facing, rounded to the nearest quarter turn, and the adjustment is stored against the first frame of the part it hangs off. Any existing offset for that direction is replaced. It is a live art-tuning tool: the change affects every character using that body layout, and is not written back to the mod files.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The ID of the body layout to adjust.

required.name: strings[1]
required.description: The name of the body part within that layout whose attachment point is being moved.

required.name: floats[0]
required.description: The horizontal offset in pixels from the part it attaches to.

required.name: floats[1]
required.description: The vertical offset in pixels from the part it attaches to.

tasks.officialDescription: set [BodyStructure]'s [BodyPart] connection position, of the player actor's facingRot, to [X][Y]. (ex: setBPC human armL 3 4

tasks.name: setBP

uses.description: Moves the origin point of one body part on a body layout in the running game — the spot the sprite pivots and is positioned around. It applies to every direction at once, unlike the per-direction attachment offsets. It is a live art-tuning tool: the change affects every character using that body layout, and is not written back to the mod files.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The ID of the body layout to adjust.

required.name: strings[1]
required.description: The name of the body part within that layout whose origin is being moved.

required.name: floats[0]
required.description: The horizontal position of the origin, in pixels within the part's sprite.

required.name: floats[1]
required.description: The vertical position of the origin, in pixels within the part's sprite.

tasks.officialDescription: set [BodyStructure]'s [BodyPart] origin position to [X][Y]. (ex: setBP human armL 3 4

tasks.name: time

uses.description: Pushes the world clock forward by a number of hours and refreshes the travel readout so the new time shows. Because it adds to the clock directly rather than letting time pass, none of the usual consequences of time passing happen: no food is eaten, no morale is lost, and nothing that ticks over per hour is run. It is a debugging shortcut for reaching a particular time of day.

optional.name: floats[0]
optional.description: How many hours to add to the world clock; twenty-four is a full day. Negative values wind the clock back. Defaults to 0, which changes nothing, so a value is needed for this to do anything.

tasks.officialDescription: advance world time by # hours (does not consume food or affect morale).

tasks.name: wind

uses.description: Sets which way the wind is blowing, which decides how sails carry a ship and which way wind-driven scenery leans. The direction is given in degrees, with 0 pointing east and the angle increasing clockwise; the game itself normally only uses multiples of 45. It replaces the wind outright rather than nudging it, and the weather system may change it again on its own later.

optional.name: floats[0]
optional.description: The wind direction in degrees, with 0 east, 90 south, 180 west and 270 north. Defaults to 0.

tasks.officialDescription: sets the wind direction to # degrees (0 = East)

tasks.name: weather

uses.description: Sets the current weather outright, changing what falls from the sky and what the weather system does next. The change takes effect immediately and lasts until the weather system moves on by itself. Giving a name that is not one of the game's weather kinds stops the task with an error.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The name of the weather to switch to. Capitalisation does not matter.

tasks.officialDescription: sets weather (none, rain, snow, storm)

tasks.name: resetachievements

uses.description: Wipes the player's achievements and statistics on the online service the game is running through, so they can be earned again from scratch. It does nothing at all if the game is not connected to that service. It is a debugging tool for testing achievement conditions, and the reset cannot be undone.

tasks.officialDescription: Resets all Horizon's Gate achievements for the current player's Steam account.

tasks.name: howmany

uses.description: Counts things in the current map and shows the total on screen as a debug message. Given a name, it counts both the items of that type lying on the ground, adding up stack sizes, and the characters of that type present, and adds the two together. Given nothing, it counts every separate pile of items on the ground instead. It is a debugging aid for checking what a map actually contains.

optional.name: strings[0]
optional.description: The ID to count. It is matched against item types on the ground and against character types in the map, so a name shared by both counts both. Leave it out to count every pile on the ground instead.

tasks.officialDescription: Displays a debug message with how many items are in the current zone. Only counts items with ID 'sValue' if set.

tasks.name: howmanyWorld

uses.description: Searches the data files of every hand-built map in the game for a piece of text and reports how many times it appears, listing each map that contains it alongside its count and finishing with a grand total, all as debug messages on screen. It is a plain text search rather than an understanding of the data, so what it counts depends on exactly what you type. Randomly generated maps, set pieces and ship interiors are not searched.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The text to search each map's data for. It is matched literally, so something like a property assignment finds only that exact spelling.

uses.description: Searches the data files of every hand-built map in the game for whatever is under the mouse pointer and reports how many times it appears, listing each map that contains it alongside its count and finishing with a grand total. If a character is under the pointer it searches for that character's type; otherwise it searches for the first item lying on that tile. If the tile holds neither, nothing happens.

tasks.officialDescription: Displays a debug message with how many times 'sValue' appears in each zone file in the ZoneData folder. If mouse is pointing at an item or actor, checks for that ID.

tasks.name: setMainMenuUIVisible

uses.description: Shows or hides the main menu's interface. Missing values are treated as false, so calling it bare hides the menu. A second flag can additionally force the main menu backdrop and the whole interface layer back on, which is how the menu is brought up from a state where drawing had been switched off.

optional.name: bools[0]
optional.description: Whether the main menu's interface is shown. Defaults to false, which hides it.

optional.name: bools[1]
optional.description: When true, also forces the main menu backdrop and the interface layer to be drawn. Defaults to false, which leaves both as they are.

tasks.officialDescription: DO NOT USE. Sets the main menu visibility to b1. If b2, force-draws main menu BG and UIManager windows.

tasks.name: markTrainerLocDone

uses.description: Marks the place the player is currently at as having had its training used up, by advancing the book icons on its map marker one step: a plain book becomes a used book, and a used one becomes a doubly-used one, with the same progression for the two-book icon. It is how a settlement's sign shows at a glance that its lessons have been taken. Nothing happens if the player is not at a place on the world map.

tasks.officialDescription: Changes the 'sign_icon_book' or 'sign_icon_2book' icon to its '_done' or '_done_done' version in the current location's tooltipIcons, if they exist.

tasks.name: markDojoLocDone

uses.description: Marks the place the player is currently at as having had its training used up, by changing the muscle icon on its map marker to the used version. It is how a settlement's sign shows at a glance that its lessons have been taken. Unlike the book markers this only advances one step, so repeating it changes nothing further. Nothing happens if the player is not at a place on the world map.

tasks.officialDescription: Changes the 'sign_icon_muscle' icon to 'sign_icon_muscle_done' in the current location's tooltipIcons, if it exists.

tasks.name: createTreasureMap

uses.description: Draws a treasure map of the world around a chosen spot and puts it in the player's hands. The world map is photographed for sixteen tiles in every direction with ships, storms, squalls, lightning and floating loot stripped out and the sky and wave styling turned off, then flattened to a single ink colour, stamped with a cross in the middle, cropped and framed like a chart. The finished picture is saved into the current game so it survives a reload, and the buried treasure's coordinates are remembered so the spot can later be dug up.

required.name: floats[0]
required.description: The horizontal tile on the world map the treasure is buried at, and the centre of the drawn map.

required.name: floats[1]
required.description: The vertical tile on the world map the treasure is buried at, and the centre of the drawn map.

tasks.officialDescription: Must be used as a taskString. Creates the texture 'treasureMap' for use with salvage quests. The texture is created for overworld X,Y set in floats[0], floats[1].

tasks.name: tMapTest

uses.description: A development tool for eyeballing treasure map rendering. It loads the world map as an overlay if one is not already loaded, strips out the hazards and floating loot, photographs a thirty-two tile square around a spot at double zoom, and then queues itself to run again a tenth of a second later so it repeats endlessly until something stops it. The picture is thrown away rather than shown or saved, so its only visible effect is the repeated work.

optional.name: floats[0]
optional.description: The horizontal tile on the world map to centre on. Defaults to 100, and is only read when a vertical tile is supplied as well.

optional.name: floats[1]
optional.description: The vertical tile on the world map to centre on. Defaults to 100.

tasks.officialDescription: DO NOT USE.

tasks.name: addTreasuresToZone

uses.description: Buries the treasure a treasure map points to, at the spot the map was drawn around: a shipwreck hidden under the ground holding a purse of ninety to two hundred and twenty coins, a crate of lost cargo, two pieces of randomly chosen loot and a bundle of lost documents. The remembered spot is then cleared, so the treasure is only ever placed once. Nothing happens if no treasure is currently waiting to be placed.

tasks.officialDescription: Adds a buried location_shipwreck item, with loot added to it, to the current zone at the X,Y set in gVar 'treasureTCX' and 'treasureTCY'. Fails if the gVars aren't set.

tasks.name: replaceTriggerWithZoneSeries

uses.description: Stamps the next map in a numbered series into the area the trigger covers, then advances the series. The map loaded is the base name with a counter appended, the counter being a global variable of that same base name, so repeated firings lay down successive pieces. Before being merged in, the piece has its random terrain replacements and chance item removals applied, and afterwards the whole map's tile artwork is rebuilt so the seams blend. Nothing happens if no map by that name and number exists.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The base name shared by the series: the map loaded is this name with the current value of the global variable of the same name appended, and that variable is then increased by one. So a base of "cave" loads "cave0", then "cave1", and so on.

optional.name: strings[1]
optional.description: The level recipe supplying the terrain the piece's placeholder tiles are replaced with. Leave it out to skip terrain replacement and only apply the chance item removals.

tasks.officialDescription: Replaces this trigger with a zone loaded from sValue ID + the value of sValue gVar. sValue2 specifies the levelData to use for replacing terrain when applying terrain replacer items.

tasks.name: applyTerrainReplacersAndItemRemovers

uses.description: Runs the random dressing pass over the whole of the current map: placeholder items marked as terrain replacers each get their chance to turn the tile they sit on into terrain drawn from a level recipe, and items marked as chance removals each get their chance to clear the tile they sit on. The odds come from each item's quantity, one percent per point, so the same map comes out differently each time. Afterwards the map's tile artwork is rebuilt so the new terrain blends with its neighbours, unless that is suppressed.

optional.name: strings[0]
optional.description: The level recipe supplying the terrain the placeholders are replaced with. Leave it out to skip terrain replacement entirely and only apply the chance item removals.

optional.name: bools[0]
optional.description: Pass true to skip rebuilding the tile artwork afterwards, which is worth doing only if something else is going to rebuild it. Defaults to false, meaning the artwork is rebuilt.

tasks.officialDescription: Item and terrain replacer items in the zone are calculated and apply their results. sValue specifies the levelData to use for replacing terrain. If b1, don't update tile sprites.

tasks.name: setupPartyFromGVars

uses.description: Rebuilds the party from a list of remembered names, in the order given, replacing whoever was in it before. Each name is a global variable: if the variable holds a whole number it is read as a position in the existing party, and otherwise as the ID of a character in the world. The order the names are given in becomes the new party order, so this is how a scripted scene can reshuffle or pare down the party. Supplying no names at all empties the party entirely.

required.name: strings[0+]
required.description: Any number of global variable names, one per party slot, in the order the new party should be in. Each variable's value is read as a position in the current party if it is a whole number, or as an actor ID otherwise.

tasks.officialDescription: Must be used as a taskString. Sets the player's current party to consist of actors with IDs specified in each strings[] entry as a globalVar, which could also be the slot number of the the actor in the current partyActors list. An example: setupPartyFromGVars,gVar1,gVar2,gVar3,aFourthGVar,andSoOn

tasks.name: healfaction

uses.description: Fully restores every character in the map belonging to one faction: they are revived and stood up, all status effects and morale penalties are cleared, health and magic are refilled and anything being charged or cast is cancelled. Maximum health lost to being knocked out is not given back, so a badly beaten character comes back with a lowered ceiling. Fatigue is not cleared either.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The ID of the faction whose members should be restored. Only characters whose faction matches exactly are affected.

tasks.officialDescription: Heals all actors in the current zone with the faction 'sValue'. Does not restore HPMax lost from being KO'd.

tasks.name: removeTempPartyActors

uses.description: Sends home everyone travelling with the party only temporarily — guests, escorts and hangers-on the player cannot fully command. They are taken out of the world rather than killed, and are also struck from the lists of party members who went missing or fell overboard, so they will not be recovered later. Party members the player fully controls are untouched.

tasks.officialDescription: Removes all actors from the zone that are in the player's current partyActors and have canControlFullyIfControllable = false.

tasks.name: removeExcessLandingPartyActors

uses.description: Takes out of the world every party member who was not chosen for the landing party, so only the selected few are present. They are removed from the map rather than killed, which is how the game clears the rest of the crew away when the player goes ashore with a picked group.

tasks.officialDescription: Removes any actors from the player's partyActors that aren't in their landingParty.

tasks.name: getItemsFromZone

uses.description: Strips every pickable item out of another map and dumps them all onto one tile of the current map, then discards the borrowed map. Items that cannot be picked up, such as scenery and terrain pieces, are left behind. Nothing happens if no map by that name exists in the current game.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The ID of the map to take the items from. It must exist in the current game's data.

optional.name: tileCoords[0]
optional.description: The tile in the current map to pile the items onto. If omitted it defaults to just off the map's corner, where the items will not be reachable.

tasks.officialDescription: removes all items that can be picked up from sValue zone and places them at XY

tasks.name: location_tryUnlockItems

uses.description: Checks the place the player is currently at for new goods and ships that have become available, and stocks them. Each thing a port holds back has a condition attached — typically the port reaching a certain level of wealth — and anything whose condition is now met is added to the port's cargo hold, its shop stock or its shipwright's list, then struck off the waiting list so it is only stocked once. If anything was added, a chime plays and a banner announces what kind of new stock has arrived. It requires the player to actually be at a place on the world map, and fails outright otherwise.

tasks.officialDescription: Checks for any unlockable items in the current location and displays a message if anything was unlocked.

tasks.name: resetFleetAI

uses.description: Clears the current plans of every fleet in the world: each forgets the waypoint it was heading for, its flagship's queued path is emptied, and the working numbers its behaviour was tracking are zeroed. The fleets then work out fresh destinations on their next turn. It is a way to unstick fleets that have got themselves into a bad route.

tasks.officialDescription: Resets the current travel path for every AI fleet.

tasks.name: adjustFleetAlliegances

uses.description: Turns the ships that were escorting the player into enemies. Any ship in the map belonging to the opposing fleet's faction that is still marked as an escort is repainted in the enemy fleet's colours, made hostile, and given a red exclamation mark over its head; the record of the player having an escort is wiped at the same time. It is the moment a supposed ally reveals itself. Nothing happens if there is no opposing fleet in the map.

tasks.officialDescription: If the player is in a fleet battle, this turns all actors in the zone that are the same faction as the enemy fleet hostile, clears the playerEscort gVar and plays FX on the changed actors.

tasks.name: openJournal

uses.description: Opens the journal and shows a chosen entry, with both facing pages displayed. It is opened for reading rather than browsing: the controller cursor is not placed on it, so it cannot be paged through with a gamepad, and the buttons along its edge can be hidden entirely. If the journal was already open the pages turn over with the usual flick and sound. Nothing happens if the player knows no journal entries yet.

optional.name: floats[0]
optional.description: Which entry to turn to, counting from 0 through the entries the player knows in the order the journal lists them. Defaults to -1, meaning stay on whatever page was showing.

optional.name: bools[0]
optional.description: Pass true to hide the journal's buttons entirely, leaving only the page. Defaults to false.

tasks.officialDescription: Opens the journal and flips to entry number 'fValue'. If b1, hides the journal's arrows and close buttons.

tasks.name: openJournal_interactive

uses.description: Opens the journal at a chosen entry and leaves it fully usable: the buttons are shown and the controller cursor is placed on it, so the player can page through and follow links. If the journal was already open the pages turn over with the usual flick and sound. Nothing happens if the player knows no journal entries yet.

optional.name: floats[0]
optional.description: Which entry to turn to, counting from 0 through the entries the player knows in the order the journal lists them. Defaults to -1, meaning stay on whatever page was showing.

tasks.officialDescription: Opens the journal and flips to entry number 'fValue'.

tasks.name: closeJournal

uses.description: Closes the journal window. Its contents are brought up to date first, so reopening it later shows the correct page.

tasks.officialDescription: Closes the journal window, if it is open.

tasks.name: learnJournalEntry

uses.description: Teaches the player a journal entry and, by default, opens the journal on it so they can read it straight away. The entry is filed into its category, marked as unread so it stands out, and optionally announced with a chime. Nothing is learned if the entry does not exist or the player already knows it, though the journal is still opened. Learning three hundred entries earns an achievement.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The ID of the journal entry to teach the player.

optional.name: bools[0]
optional.description: Whether to play the chime announcing a new entry. Defaults to false, so it is learned quietly.

optional.name: bools[1]
optional.description: Pass true to leave the journal closed instead of opening it on the new entry. Defaults to false, meaning the journal opens.

tasks.officialDescription: Adds the journalEntry ID in sValue to the known journals list. If b1, play a sound. If b2, don't open journal to show the entry.

tasks.name: moveJournal

uses.description: Slides the journal window to a spot on the screen, so a scene can place it out of the way of whatever else is being shown. The destination can be given directly, mirrored so it is measured from the right edge instead of the left, or overridden entirely to sit dead centre. The window glides there over time rather than jumping, unless the speed is left at its default of zero.

optional.name: floats[0]
optional.description: How fast the window glides to its new spot. Defaults to 0.

optional.name: bools[0]
optional.description: Pass true to measure the horizontal position from the right edge of the screen rather than the left, with the window's own width taken into account. Defaults to false.

optional.name: bools[1]
optional.description: Pass true to ignore the given position entirely and centre the window on the screen. Defaults to false.

optional.name: tileCoords[0]
optional.description: Where to move the window to, in screen pixels from the top-left corner rather than in tiles. If omitted it defaults to (-1,-1), tucking the window just off the top-left corner.

tasks.officialDescription: Moves the journalWindow to screen position X,Y at speed 'fValue'. If b1, X position is offset from screen center. If b2, moves journalWindow to screen center.

tasks.name: addJournalGoal

uses.description: Writes a new goal onto the journal's goal pages. The goal list is tidied first, then the goal is placed in the first free slot, or failing that over the oldest already-completed goal, and any tick against that slot is cleared. Nothing is added if a goal with effectively the same wording is already listed, ignoring differences in spacing and punctuation, and the list holds fifty-four goals in all, eighteen to a page. Unless suppressed, the journal opens on the page the goal landed on with a flash across the new line and a pair of chimes.

required.name: strings[0+]
required.description: The text of the goal. Any further text values are joined onto it with commas between, which is how a goal containing commas is written in a comma-separated task; empty values are skipped.

optional.name: bools[0]
optional.description: Pass true to add the goal quietly, with no flash, chimes or journal opening; the journal is still brought up to date if it happens to be open. Defaults to false.

tasks.officialDescription: Adds 'sValue' as a journal goal to the first available 'goal' gVar, then opens the journal and plays a new goal FX on the goal text. If b1, journal isn't opened and the new goal FX doesn't play.

tasks.name: completeJournalGoal

uses.description: Ticks off a goal on the journal's goal pages by striking a line through it. The goal list is tidied first and then searched for a goal with effectively the same wording, ignoring differences in spacing and punctuation; nothing happens if none is found or it was already struck through. Unless suppressed, the journal opens on that page with a flash across the line and a completion chime, the player is held from acting for a moment, and the whole party is awarded fifty experience.

required.name: strings[0+]
required.description: The text of the goal to tick off; it must match a listed goal apart from spacing and punctuation. Any further text values are joined onto it with commas between, which is how a goal containing commas is written in a comma-separated task; empty values are skipped.

optional.name: bools[0]
optional.description: Pass true to hide the journal's buttons while it is opened, and to skip the experience award and the pause. Defaults to false.

optional.name: bools[1]
optional.description: Pass true to tick the goal off quietly, with no flash, chime, journal opening or experience award; the journal is still brought up to date if it happens to be open. Defaults to false.

tasks.officialDescription: Completes the journal goal found with the same text as set in 'sValue'. This will open the journal, put a line through the goal, play FX and award 50 XP to all player crew. If b1, hides all interactive buttons (used for credits). If b2, doesn't give XP, open journal or play completion FX. The journal goal gVars will be stripped of spaces and special chars when checked against sValue. The check will be done in a case-insensitive manner.

tasks.name: removeJournalGoal

uses.description: Takes a goal off the journal's goal pages entirely, rather than ticking it off, and closes up the gap so the remaining goals shift along. The goal is found by matching its wording, ignoring differences in spacing and punctuation, and nothing is removed if none matches. If the journal happens to be open it is brought up to date without being forced into view.

optional.name: strings[0+]
optional.description: The text of the goal to remove; it must match a listed goal apart from spacing and punctuation. Any further text values are joined onto it with commas between, which is how a goal containing commas is written in a comma-separated task; empty values are skipped. Leaving it out matches a goal whose text is empty, which normally means nothing is removed.

tasks.officialDescription: Removes the first journal goal that matches the string in 'sValue' from the list of journal 'goal' gvars, then reassigns all 'goal' gVars to be in order with no gaps. If sValue is blank, just reassigns journal goals. The journal goal gVars will be stripped of spaces and special chars when checked against sValue. The check will be done in a case-insensitive manner.

tasks.name: setGlobalVar_toJournalGoalVar

uses.description: Finds a goal on the journal's goal pages by its wording and stores the name of the variable holding it into a global variable of your choosing, so later tasks can read or change that goal without knowing which slot it landed in. Matching ignores differences in spacing and punctuation. If no goal matches, the destination variable is set to empty text instead.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The name of the global variable to write the answer into.

optional.name: strings[1]
optional.description: The text of the goal to look for; it must match a listed goal apart from spacing and punctuation. Defaults to empty text, which matches no goal and leaves the destination variable empty.

optional.name: bools[0]
optional.description: Pass true to name the goal's completion variable rather than the goal itself, which is what a task would read to find out whether the goal has been ticked off. Defaults to false.

tasks.officialDescription: Sets gVar 'sValue' to the gVar name for the first journal 'goal#' gVar that matches 'sValue2', or a blank string if that journal goal doesn't exist. If b1, will set the gVar in sValue to the 'goal#Done' gVar name instead. The journal goal gVars will be stripped of spaces and special chars when checked against sValue2. The check will be done in a case-insensitive manner.

tasks.name: setTerrainType_spriteOffsetMult

uses.description: Changes, in the running game, how strongly a terrain type's artwork shifts frame with position across the map, which is what makes fields ripple and water flow in patterns. Larger values make the pattern change faster from tile to tile; zero makes every tile of that terrain look the same. It affects every tile of that terrain everywhere at once and is not written back to the mod files, so it is a live tuning tool.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The ID of the terrain type to adjust. An unknown ID stops the task with an error.

optional.name: tileCoords[0]
optional.description: The horizontal and vertical strength of the shift, as a pair. If omitted it defaults to (-1,-1), which reverses the pattern's direction on both axes.

tasks.officialDescription: Sets the spriteXOffsetMult and spriteYOffsetMult of terrainType 'sValue' to X and Y.

tasks.name: setTerrainType_spriteOffsetModulo

uses.description: Changes, in the running game, how often a terrain type's artwork repeats across the map — the number of tiles before the pattern comes back round. It is what sets the wavelength of rippling fields and flowing water. Setting it to zero or less switches the positional pattern off entirely for that axis. It affects every tile of that terrain everywhere at once and is not written back to the mod files, so it is a live tuning tool.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The ID of the terrain type to adjust. An unknown ID stops the task with an error.

optional.name: tileCoords[0]
optional.description: The horizontal and vertical repeat lengths in tiles, as a pair. If omitted it defaults to (-1,-1), which switches the positional pattern off on both axes.

tasks.officialDescription: Sets the spriteXOffsetModulo and spriteYOffsetModulo of terrainType 'sValue' to X and Y.

tasks.name: setTerrainTypes_spriteOffsetModulo

uses.description: Changes, in the running game, how often the artwork repeats across the map for every terrain type whose ID starts with a given piece of text, so a whole related family of terrains can be retuned in one go. The repeat length is the number of tiles before the pattern comes back round, and zero or less switches the positional pattern off for that axis. The change affects every tile of every matching terrain everywhere at once and is not written back to the mod files.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The beginning of the terrain type IDs to adjust; every terrain whose ID starts with this is affected. Matching is case-sensitive, and an empty value affects every terrain in the game.

optional.name: tileCoords[0]
optional.description: The horizontal and vertical repeat lengths in tiles, as a pair. If omitted it defaults to (-1,-1), which switches the positional pattern off on both axes.

tasks.officialDescription: Sets the spriteXOffsetModulo and spriteYOffsetModulo of any terrainTypes whose ID starts with 'sValue', to X and Y.

tasks.name: discoverFog

uses.description: Lifts the fog of war around a tile as though someone had stood there and looked about, casting sight lines out to twenty tiles in every direction and revealing whatever they reach. The sweep is run four times over to fill in the gaps. How finely it sweeps depends on the contextual actor: for the player's own character it looks every three degrees, giving thorough coverage, and for anyone else only every forty-five, leaving a sparse spray of revealed tiles. Nothing happens in a map that has no fog of war.

optional.name: tileCoords[0]
optional.description: The tile to look out from. A position outside the map is pulled back to the nearest edge, so the default of (-1,-1) reveals from the map's top-left corner. This slot is always read, so the contextual actor's own position is never used as the viewpoint.

tasks.officialDescription: Reveals a small fogOfWar area at X,Y.

tasks.name: setFog

uses.description: Reveals or hides the fog of war over a square block of tiles, either in the current map or in one saved elsewhere, letting a scene uncover a region ahead of time or blot one out again. The block is centred on a tile and extends outward by a chosen number of tiles in each direction. With the defaults it covers no tiles at all, so a size is needed for it to do anything.

optional.name: strings[0]
optional.description: The ID of the map whose fog to change. Defaults to the current map. The map must have fog recorded in the save, or the task stops with an error.

optional.name: floats[0]
optional.description: How far the block reaches out from the centre tile, in tiles. Defaults to 0, which covers nothing at all.

optional.name: bools[0]
optional.description: True to reveal the block, false to hide it again. Defaults to false.

optional.name: tileCoords[0]
optional.description: The tile at the centre of the block. If omitted it defaults to (-1,-1), which with any size above zero reaches off the edge of the map and stops the task with an error.

tasks.officialDescription: Sets the fogOfWar known state of all tiles in a square radius of 'fValue' from X,Y to bValue1.

tasks.name: resetAllTileReactTimers

uses.description: Clears the cooling-off period on every tile in the map, so tiles that had recently triggered a reaction can trigger it again straight away. Nothing else about the tiles changes. It is useful when a scene needs a trap or trigger tile to fire again immediately rather than waiting out its normal delay.

tasks.officialDescription: Sets the lastTimeReacted and delayTime to 0 for every tile in the current zone.

tasks.name: changePlayerActor

uses.description: Hands control of the party over to a different character, who moves to the front of the marching order while the others fall in behind and follow. If they were not in the party they are added to it. No flourish is played and the rest of the order is otherwise left alone. It is refused if the character is not one the player can fully control, if the current leader is riding something, if the character stats display is hidden, or if the map is a ship interior and the character is not a ship. It requires the named character to exist, and fails outright otherwise.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The ID of the character to put in charge. They must be present in the map and fully controllable.

tasks.officialDescription: Changes the current player party leader to actor ID 'sValue'.

tasks.name: setGlobalVarToActorProperty

uses.description: Reads one named property off a character in the map and stores its current value into a global variable, so a later formula or piece of dialog can use it. If the character is not present, or the property name matches nothing on them, the variable is set to empty text or to false respectively rather than being left alone.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The name of the global variable to write the answer into.

required.name: strings[1]
required.description: The ID of the character to read from. They must be present in the map.

required.name: strings[2]
required.description: The name of the property to read, spelled exactly as the game names it. An unrecognised name yields false rather than an error.

uses.description: Reads one named property off a character in the map and stores its current value into a global variable, with the character and the property packed into a single value separated by a comma. This is the form to use from a trigger effect, which can only supply two text values. If the character is not present the variable is set to empty text instead.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The name of the global variable to write the answer into.

required.name: strings[1]
required.description: The character and the property together, as "actorID,propertyName". Everything after the last comma is taken as the property name and everything before it as the character's ID; all spaces are stripped out first, so neither part may contain a space. Without a comma nothing is read and the variable is set to empty text.

tasks.officialDescription: Sets gVar 'sValue' to an actor's property, set in sValue2 as 'actorID,property'.

tasks.name: setGlobalVarToPlayerFleetShipProperty

uses.description: Reads one named property off a ship in the player's fleet, picked by its position in the fleet order, and stores the value into a global variable. The property can be read either from that particular ship, reflecting the wear and cargo of the actual vessel, or from its class, giving the figures the design was built with. If the fleet has no ship in that position, the variable is set to empty text instead.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The name of the global variable to write the answer into.

required.name: strings[1]
required.description: The name of the property to read, spelled exactly as the game names it. An unrecognised name yields false rather than an error.

required.name: floats[0]
required.description: Which ship to read, counting from 0 through the fleet in order, where 0 is the flagship.

optional.name: bools[0]
optional.description: Pass true to read the property from the ship's class rather than the individual ship, giving the design's figures rather than the vessel's current state. Defaults to false.

tasks.officialDescription: Sets the gVar in sValue to the actor property specified in sValue2, of the player fleet's ship actor in slot fValue. If b1, the property is pulled from the actor's actorType instead of the actor.

tasks.name: setGlobalVar_toActorMostUsedActionID

uses.description: Finds out which ability a character leans on most and stores its ID into a global variable, which is how the game works out what someone is known for. The character's abilities are ranked by how many times they have been used, and the one at a chosen place down that ranking is picked. The ranking can be restricted to abilities that have to be learned with experience, or to those that come for free, so a character's signature learned skill can be told apart from their basic moves. If the character is not present, or the ranking runs out before reaching the chosen place, the variable is set to empty text.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The name of the global variable to write the ability's ID into.

optional.name: strings[1]
optional.description: The ID of the character whose usage record is read. Defaults to empty text, which matches no character and leaves the answer empty.

optional.name: floats[0]
optional.description: How far down the ranking to look, counting from 0 for the most used. Defaults to 0.

optional.name: bools[0]
optional.description: Pass true to consider only abilities that cost experience to learn or rank up. Defaults to false, which considers all of them.

optional.name: bools[1]
optional.description: Pass true to consider only abilities that cost no experience at all. Defaults to false. Setting both this and the previous flag leaves nothing to consider.

tasks.officialDescription: Sets the gVar in sValue to the action ID of the 'fValue'-th most-used action of the player actor whose ID is 'sValue2'. fValue = 0 would be most used, 1 would be second most used, etc. If b1, only selects actions that are part of an actor class. If b2, only selects actions NOT part of an actor class.

tasks.name: learnJournalEntry_silent

uses.description: Teaches the player a journal entry without any announcement: no chime, no unread marker and no journal opening, so the player simply finds it there next time they look. Nothing is learned if the entry does not exist or the player already knows it. The entry can additionally be marked as already sold, which stamps it as such in the journal and stops it being counted among the knowledge the player still has to trade away.

required.name: strings[0]
