If ID is not set, uses current location instead. If there is no item in the slot specified or the location hasn't been visited yet, an empty string is set.

tasks.name: setGlobalVar_toLocationCargoItemIDSlot

uses.description: Looks at one slot of a settlement's cargo hold — the bulk goods a port trades in, as opposed to its shop stock — and stores the ID of the item in it into a global variable. If the place is unknown, or the slot is empty or beyond the end of the hold, the variable is set to empty text.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The name of the global variable to write the item's ID into.

optional.name: strings[1]
optional.description: The ID of the place to look at. Leave it out, or give an empty value, to use the place the player is currently at.

optional.name: floats[0]
optional.description: Which cargo slot to look at, counting from 0. Defaults to 0.

tasks.officialDescription: Sets gVar 'sValue' to the itemType ID of a cargo item in slot 'fValue' of a location's cargo inventory. 'sValue2' is the ID of the location. If ID is not set, uses current location instead. If there is no item in the slot specified or the location hasn't been visited yet, an empty string is set.

tasks.name: setGlobalVar_toLocationShipIDSlot

uses.description: Looks at a settlement's shipwright and stores the kind of ship offered in one of its slots into a global variable, which is how a scene can ask what vessels are for sale here. If the place is unknown, or has nothing offered in that slot, the variable is set to empty text.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The name of the global variable to write the ship kind's ID into.

optional.name: strings[1]
optional.description: The ID of the place to look at. Leave it out, or give an empty value, to use the place the player is currently at.

optional.name: floats[0]
optional.description: Which of the shipwright's offerings to look at, counting from 0. Defaults to 0.

tasks.officialDescription: Sets gVar 'sValue' to the actorType ID of a ship in slot 'fValue' of a location's shipwright_boatTypes list. 'sValue2' is the ID of the location. If ID is not set, uses current location instead. If there is no item in the slot specified, an empty string is set.

tasks.name: setGlobalVar_toLocationFactionID

uses.description: Stores which faction runs a settlement into a global variable, so dialog can react to whose port the player is standing in. If the place is unknown the variable is set to empty text.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The name of the global variable to write the faction's ID into.

optional.name: strings[1]
optional.description: The ID of the place to ask about. Leave it out, or give an empty value, to use the place the player is currently at.

tasks.officialDescription: Sets gVar 'sValue' to the currently favored faction ID of a location. 'sValue2' is the ID of the location. If ID is not set, uses current location instead. Sets an empty string if the location is neutral or not a port.

tasks.name: modLocationIDFactionIDFavor

uses.description: Shifts how much a port favours one faction, which is what decides who ends up flying their flag over it: whichever faction stands highest owns the port. The shift is capped between fifty either way, and it is refused for a port that has been locked to a faction. The port's standings can first be wiped back to nothing for every faction, and a port can instead be locked to the named faction outright so nothing can change hands there again. Nothing happens away from a port, or if the named faction does not exist.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The ID of the faction whose standing at the port is being changed. An unknown faction stops the task after any wiping has been done.

optional.name: strings[1]
optional.description: The ID of the port to change. Leave it out, or give an empty value, to use the port the player is currently at.

optional.name: floats[0]
optional.description: How much to raise or lower that faction's standing at the port; negative values lower it. Defaults to 0.

optional.name: bools[0]
optional.description: Pass true to first wipe every faction's standing at the port back to nothing, so the change starts from a clean slate. Defaults to false.

optional.name: bools[1]
optional.description: Pass true to lock the port to the named faction permanently instead of shifting the numbers, putting them far beyond reach and everyone else far below. Defaults to false.

tasks.officialDescription: Adds 'fValue' faction_favor for 'sValue' faction ID to a port location. 'sValue2' is the ID of the location. If ID is not set, uses current location instead. If b1, resets every faction's favor to 0 before adding fValue to sValue (will unset ever-loyal ports). If b2, sets the port to be ever-loyal to sValue faction instead.

tasks.name: setLocZoneID

uses.description: Changes which map a settlement leads into, so entering that place from the world map takes the player somewhere different from before. Everything else about the place — its name, faction, stock and markers — is untouched. Nothing happens if the place is unknown.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The ID of the map the place should now lead into.

optional.name: strings[1]
optional.description: The ID of the place to change. Leave it out, or give an empty value, to use the place the player is currently at.

tasks.officialDescription: Sets a location's zoneID to 'sValue'. 'sValue2' is the ID of the location. If ID is not set, uses current location instead. Keep in mind that changing a location's zoneID while the player is in it might make it unable to be left, if unaccounted for.

tasks.name: setLocName

uses.description: Renames a settlement, changing what the player sees on the world map, in the travel readout and anywhere the place is mentioned. Nothing else about it changes. Nothing happens if the place is unknown.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The new name to display for the place.

optional.name: strings[1]
optional.description: The ID of the place to rename. Leave it out, or give an empty value, to use the place the player is currently at.

tasks.officialDescription: Sets a location's name to 'sValue'. 'sValue2' is the ID of the location. If ID is not set, uses current location instead.

tasks.name: removeIconFromLocationID

uses.description: Takes one icon off a settlement's map marker, the little symbols that show at a glance what services the place offers. Only the first matching icon is removed, so a place showing the same icon twice keeps the second. Nothing happens if the place is unknown or does not show that icon.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The name of the icon to remove, spelled exactly as it appears on the place's marker.

optional.name: strings[1]
optional.description: The ID of the place to change. Leave it out, or give an empty value, to use the place the player is currently at.

tasks.officialDescription: Removes 'sValue' icon from a location's tooltipIcons list, if it exists. 'sValue2' is the ID of the location. If ID is not set, uses current location instead.

tasks.name: swapIconForLocationID

uses.description: Replaces one icon on a settlement's map marker with another, which is how a place's advertised services change — a shop closing, a shipwright opening. Only the first matching icon is swapped. If the place is not showing the old icon nothing happens, unless the task is told to add the new icon anyway.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The name of the icon to replace, spelled exactly as it appears on the place's marker.

required.name: strings[1]
required.description: The name of the icon to put in its place.

required.name: strings[2]
required.description: The ID of the place to change. Give an empty value to use the place the player is currently at; the slot itself must still be filled, since supplying only two values switches the task to its packed form.

optional.name: bools[0]
optional.description: Pass true to add the new icon anyway when the old one is not there, so the place ends up showing it either way. Defaults to false.

uses.description: Replaces one icon on a settlement's map marker with another, with both icons packed into a single value separated by a comma. This is the form to use from a trigger effect, which can only supply two text values. Only the first matching icon is swapped, and if the place is not showing the old icon nothing happens unless the task is told to add the new icon anyway.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The old and new icons together, as "oldIcon,newIcon". Only the first two comma-separated parts are used and all spaces are stripped out. Without a comma the task misbehaves, setting the icon to the place's ID.

required.name: strings[1]
required.description: The ID of the place to change. Give an empty value to use the place the player is currently at.

optional.name: bools[0]
optional.description: Pass true to add the new icon anyway when the old one is not there, so the place ends up showing it either way. Defaults to false.

tasks.officialDescription: Changes an icon from a location's tooltipIcons list to another icon, specified in sValue as 'oldIcon, newIcon'. 'sValue2' is the ID of the location. If ID is not set, uses current location instead. If b1, 'newIcon' will be added to list even if 'oldIcon' doesn't exist.

tasks.name: addItemToLocationID

uses.description: Puts something new on sale at a settlement. Bulk goods go into the port's cargo hold and everything else into its shop stock, while naming a kind of ship instead adds it to the shipwright's offerings. It only works at places the player has already visited, since unvisited places have not had their stock set up yet, and item timers are held back so nothing spoils while it is added.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The ID of the item to put on sale. The ID of a kind of ship may be given instead, which adds it to the shipwright rather than the shop.

optional.name: strings[1]
optional.description: The ID of the place to stock. Leave it out, or give an empty value, to use the place the player is currently at.

optional.name: floats[0]
optional.description: How many to put on sale. Defaults to 1, and 0 is also treated as 1. A value of -2 clears out any existing stock of that item first, replacing rather than adding to it.

tasks.officialDescription: Adds 'sValue' as the ID of an itemType or actorType to the stash, cargo or shipwright of a location that has been visited by the player at least once. fValue is the quantity to add, defaulting to 1. If fValue is -2, removes all non-infinite versions of the item before adding an infinite one. 'sValue2' is the ID of the location. If ID is not set, uses current location instead.

tasks.name: removeItemFromLocationID

uses.description: Takes something off sale at a settlement, looking first in its shop stock, then in its cargo hold, then among the shipwright's offerings. Three reserved names clear a whole category instead: emptying the shop stock, emptying the cargo hold, or removing every ship on offer. It works at any place, visited or not.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The ID of the item to take off sale, or the ID of a kind of ship to remove from the shipwright. The reserved names "removeAllStash", "removeAllCargo" and "removeAllShips" instead empty the shop stock, the cargo hold or the ship list entirely.

optional.name: strings[1]
optional.description: The ID of the place to change. Leave it out, or give an empty value, to use the place the player is currently at.

optional.name: floats[0]
optional.description: How many to take away. Defaults to 1, and 0 is also treated as 1. Any negative number removes the whole stock of that item. It is ignored by the three reserved names.

tasks.officialDescription: Removes 'sValue' as the ID of an itemType or actorType from the stash, cargo or shipwright of a location. fValue is the quantity to remove, defaulting to 1. If fValue is negative, removes all. 'sValue2' is the ID of the location. If ID is not set, uses current location instead. 'sValue' can be a key word to remove everything of a type: removeAllStash, removeAllCargo, removeAllShips

tasks.name: addUnlockableItemToLocationID

uses.description: Adds something to a settlement's list of goods held back until a condition is met, so it appears on sale later once the port grows or the story moves on. The condition is checked immediately after being added, so anything already qualifying goes on sale at once, quietly and without the usual announcement. The same item can be added several times with different conditions, each unlocking its own batch.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The ID of the item to hold back. The ID of a kind of ship may be given instead, which will be offered by the shipwright when the condition is met.

required.name: strings[1]
required.description: The condition that must come out at 1 or more for the item to go on sale, evaluated against the player. Typically a check on the port's wealth.

required.name: strings[2]
required.description: The ID of the place to add it to. Give an empty value to use the place the player is currently at; the slot itself must still be filled, since supplying only two values switches the task to its two-value form.

optional.name: floats[0]
optional.description: How many go on sale when the condition is met. Defaults to 1, and 0 is also treated as 1. A value of -2 clears out any existing stock of that item first, replacing rather than adding to it.

uses.description: Adds something to a settlement's list of goods held back until a condition is met, with the item and its condition optionally packed into a single value separated by a comma. This is the form to use from a trigger effect, which can only supply two text values. The condition is checked immediately, so anything already qualifying goes on sale at once and quietly.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The item to hold back, or the item and its condition together as "itemTypeID,condition". Only the first two comma-separated parts are used and all spaces are stripped out. Without a comma the condition is simply 1, meaning it goes on sale immediately.

required.name: strings[1]
required.description: The ID of the place to add it to. Give an empty value to use the place the player is currently at.

optional.name: floats[0]
optional.description: How many go on sale when the condition is met. Defaults to 1, and 0 is also treated as 1. A value of -2 clears out any existing stock of that item first.

uses.description: Adds something to the list of goods held back at the place the player is currently at, with no condition, so it goes on sale immediately and quietly. It is the shortest form of the task, for simply stocking the port the player is standing in.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The ID of the item to put on sale. The ID of a kind of ship may be given instead, which is offered by the shipwright.

optional.name: floats[0]
optional.description: How many go on sale. Defaults to 1, and 0 is also treated as 1. A value of -2 clears out any existing stock of that item first.

tasks.officialDescription: Adds an itemType or actorType to a location's itemType_quantity_unlockable list with a formula, set in sValue as 'ID, formula'. fValue is the quantity of the unlockable, defaulting to 1, with -2 being infinite. 'sValue2' is the ID of the location. If ID is not set, uses current location instead.

tasks.name: removeUnlockableItemFromLocationID

uses.description: Takes an entry off a settlement's list of goods held back until a condition is met, so it will never go on sale. The entry is matched by item, and can be narrowed further by the quantity and the condition it was added with; where several entries match, all of them are removed. Nothing already on sale is touched — this only affects what is still waiting.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The ID of the held-back item to remove. An empty value matches every item, clearing the whole waiting list.

required.name: strings[1]
required.description: The condition the entry was added with, matched exactly apart from spaces. An empty value matches any condition.

required.name: strings[2]
required.description: The ID of the place to change. Give an empty value to use the place the player is currently at; the slot itself must still be filled, since supplying only two values switches the task to its two-value form.

optional.name: floats[0]
optional.description: The quantity the entry was added with, matched exactly. Defaults to 0, which matches any quantity.

uses.description: Takes an entry off a settlement's list of goods held back until a condition is met, with the item and the condition it was added with optionally packed into a single value separated by a comma. This is the form to use from a trigger effect, which can only supply two text values. Where several entries match, all of them are removed.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The held-back item to remove, or the item and the condition it was added with together as "itemTypeID,condition". Only the first two comma-separated parts are used and all spaces are stripped out. Without a comma any condition matches.

required.name: strings[1]
required.description: The ID of the place to change. Give an empty value to use the place the player is currently at.

optional.name: floats[0]
optional.description: The quantity the entry was added with, matched exactly. Defaults to 0, which matches any quantity.

uses.description: Clears entries off the list of goods held back at the place the player is currently at. Naming an item removes every entry waiting for that item; naming nothing at all empties the whole waiting list, so nothing more will ever come on sale there. Nothing already on sale is touched.

optional.name: strings[0]
optional.description: The ID of the held-back item to remove. Leave it out, or give an empty value, to clear every held-back entry at the place.

optional.name: floats[0]
optional.description: The quantity the entry was added with, matched exactly. Defaults to 0, which matches any quantity.

tasks.officialDescription: Removes an item from a location's itemType_quantity_unlockable list that matches an ID, formula and quantity, set in sValue as 'ID, formula' and fValue as quantity. 'sValue2' is the ID of the location. If ID is not set, uses current location instead. If any property to check isn't set, it will match all of that property (eg, fValue = 0 will match any quantity).

tasks.name: changeTradeGood

uses.description: Changes which commodity a settlement is known for producing, the good it sells cheaply and in quantity. Naming another place instead copies that place's trade good over, which is how two ports can be made to share a speciality. Nothing happens if the place being changed is unknown.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The ID of the commodity the place should now trade in. If this happens to be the ID of another place on the world map, that place's own trade good is copied instead.

optional.name: strings[1]
optional.description: The ID of the place to change. Leave it out, or give an empty value, to use the place the player is currently at.

tasks.officialDescription: Changes a location's tradeGood_itemTypeID to 'sValue'. If sValue is the ID of another location, it will use the tradeGood_itemTypeID of that location instead. 'sValue2' is the ID of the location to change. If ID is not set, uses current location instead.

tasks.name: addSpawnDataToLocationID

uses.description: Adds a spawn set to a settlement, so from now on the characters and creatures it describes will be placed there when the map is set up. Nothing happens if no spawn set by that name exists, or if the place is unknown. The same set can be added more than once, which stacks its spawns.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The ID of the spawn set to attach to the place.

optional.name: strings[1]
optional.description: The ID of the place to add it to. Leave it out, or give an empty value, to use the place the player is currently at.

tasks.officialDescription: Adds 'sValue' actorPrefab to the auto_spawnDataID list of a location. 'sValue2' is the ID of the location. If ID is not set, uses current location instead.

tasks.name: removeSpawnDataFromLocationID

uses.description: Takes a spawn set off a settlement so it no longer populates the place when the map is set up. Every copy of that set is removed, and naming nothing at all strips the place of all its spawn sets. Nothing happens if the place is unknown, and anything already spawned stays where it is.

optional.name: strings[0]
optional.description: The ID of the spawn set to remove; every copy of it is taken off. Leave it out, or give an empty value, to remove all of the place's spawn sets.

optional.name: strings[1]
optional.description: The ID of the place to change. Leave it out, or give an empty value, to use the place the player is currently at.

tasks.officialDescription: Removes all entries from a location's auto_spawnDataID list that match 'sValue'. If sValue isn't set, or is blank, every entry is removed. 'sValue2' is the ID of the location. If ID is not set, uses current location instead.

tasks.name: setLocMinimapIcon

uses.description: Changes the symbol a settlement is drawn with on the world map and minimap, which is how a place can visibly change character — a village becoming a fortress, a ruin becoming a port. Nothing happens if the place is unknown.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The name of the image to use as the place's map symbol.

optional.name: strings[1]
optional.description: The ID of the place to change. Leave it out, or give an empty value, to use the place the player is currently at.

tasks.officialDescription: Sets the minimapIcon of a location to 'sValue'. If a location's minimapIcon is not set, or is blank, and the location is a port, the icon of the faction controlling the port is used. 'sValue2' is the ID of the location. If ID is not set, uses current location instead.

tasks.name: setLocEnterable

uses.description: Decides whether a settlement can be entered from the world map, which is how a port is closed off or opened up as the story moves. Sailing to a place that cannot be entered simply does nothing. Nothing happens if the place is unknown.

optional.name: strings[0]
optional.description: The ID of the place to change. Leave it out, or give an empty value, to use the place the player is currently at, or to fall through to the second text slot if one is supplied.

optional.name: strings[1]
optional.description: An alternative place to change, used only when the first slot is left empty. It exists so a trigger effect that already needs its first text slot for something else can still name a place.

optional.name: bools[0]
optional.description: True to let the place be entered, false to close it off. Defaults to false, so calling this task bare closes the place.

tasks.officialDescription: Sets a location's enterable bool to b1. 'sValue' is the ID of the location. If ID is not set, uses current location instead.

tasks.name: setLocPort

uses.description: Decides whether a settlement counts as a port, which governs whether ships can dock there, whether it trades in bulk cargo and whether factions can contest ownership of it. Nothing happens if the place is unknown.

optional.name: strings[0]
optional.description: The ID of the place to change. Leave it out, or give an empty value, to use the place the player is currently at, or to fall through to the second text slot if one is supplied.

optional.name: strings[1]
optional.description: An alternative place to change, used only when the first slot is left empty. It exists so a trigger effect that already needs its first text slot for something else can still name a place.

optional.name: bools[0]
optional.description: True to make the place a port, false to stop it being one. Defaults to false, so calling this task bare strips the place of its port status.

tasks.officialDescription: Sets a location's port bool to b1. 'sValue' is the ID of the location. If ID is not set, uses current location instead.

tasks.name: setLocUndiscoverable

uses.description: Hides a place from the world map and stops it ever being found again: it is marked undiscovered and no longer discoverable, and if the player is standing on the map it sits in, the markers within two tiles of it are buried out of sight. A place added by a mod also has its sight-blocker removed, so the spot no longer obstructs the view. Optionally the place's discovery condition is reset to always-true, so it can be found again by other means. Nothing happens if the place is unknown.

optional.name: strings[0]
optional.description: The ID of the place to hide. Leave it out, or give an empty value, to use the place the player is currently at.

optional.name: bools[0]
optional.description: Pass true to also reset the place's discovery condition to always-true, so anything that re-enables discovery will find it. Defaults to false.

tasks.officialDescription: Sets a location's discovered and discoverable bool to false. 'sValue' is the ID of the location. If ID is not set, uses current location instead. If b1 is set, will set the location's discoverable_fReq formula to '1' (which is default).

tasks.name: clearLocationItemsFromZone

uses.description: Strips a settlement's marker pieces off the map — the signpost, buildings and decorations placed to represent it — and forgets that it ever had them, so the spot is left bare. A replacement piece can be named to stand in their place; if it is a place marker it is tied back to the settlement and buried if the settlement has not been found yet. Anything blocking sight at the spot is put back afterwards, so the view is unchanged. Nothing happens unless the player is on the map the place sits in.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The ID of the place whose marker pieces are to be cleared.

optional.name: strings[1]
optional.description: The ID of a single item to put down in their place, on the settlement's own tile. Leave it out to leave the spot bare; a name that is not a real item is ignored.

tasks.officialDescription: Removes all of a location's set locationItems from the zone, if the current zone is the location's zoneThisLocationIsIn. 'sValue' is the ID of the location. If 'sValue2' is set, it should be the ID of an itemType that will be the new locationItem, placed at offset 0,0.

tasks.name: addLocationItemToZone

uses.description: Places one of a settlement's marker pieces onto the map at an offset from the settlement itself — a building, a signpost, a bit of scenery — and records it as belonging to that place, so it is cleared away with the rest if the settlement is ever stripped. A piece that is itself a place marker is tied back to the settlement, and is buried while the settlement remains undiscovered so long as it sits within two tiles of it. Nothing happens unless the player is on the map the place sits in.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The ID of the place the piece belongs to. Its position on the map is what the offset is measured from.

optional.name: strings[1]
optional.description: The ID of the item to place. Leave it out, or give an empty value, and the game picks for you: a cluster of town buildings for a port, or a natural landmark otherwise.

optional.name: tileCoords[0]
optional.description: How far from the settlement to place the piece, in tiles across and down; negative values go up and left. If omitted it defaults to (-1,-1), placing it one tile up and left of the settlement.

tasks.officialDescription: Adds a new locationItem for a location to the current zone, if it is the location's zoneThisLocationIsIn. 'sValue' is the ID of the location and 'sValue2' is the itemType ID to add. X,Y specifies the locationItemOffset to use. If sValue2 is not set, or is blank, a default itemType of port_bighouses3 for ports or location_natural1 for non-ports will be used

tasks.name: removeLocationTag

uses.description: Takes a label off a settlement. Labels are the free-form marks the game and mods put on places to remember what kind of place they are or what has happened there, and conditions elsewhere test for them. Naming nothing at all strips every label from the place. Nothing happens if the place is unknown.

optional.name: strings[0]
optional.description: The label to remove, matched exactly. Leave it out, or give an empty value, to remove every label the place has.

optional.name: strings[1]
optional.description: The ID of the place to change. Leave it out, or give an empty value, to use the place the player is currently at.

tasks.officialDescription: Removes the 'sValue' tag from a location's tags list. 'sValue2' is the ID of the location. If ID is not set, uses current location instead. If sValue is not set, or is blank, all tags will be removed.

tasks.name: addLocationTag

uses.description: Puts a label on a settlement. Labels are the free-form marks the game and mods use to remember what kind of place somewhere is or what has happened there, and conditions elsewhere test for them. A label the place already carries is not added twice. Nothing happens if the place is unknown.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The label to add. An empty value does nothing.

optional.name: strings[1]
optional.description: The ID of the place to label. Leave it out, or give an empty value, to use the place the player is currently at.

tasks.officialDescription: Adds the 'sValue' tag to a location's tags list, if it doesn't already exist. 'sValue2' is the ID of the location. If ID is not set, uses current location instead.

tasks.name: setLocationLocation

uses.description: Moves a settlement to a different map, a different tile, or both, carrying everything that marks it on the ground along with it. Its buildings, signposts and scenery are torn up from the old spot and rebuilt around the new one at the same relative offsets, the sight-blocker on its tile moves too, and any map that is not the one the player is standing in is loaded, edited and saved behind the scenes. A place whose marker pieces were never recorded first adopts whatever place markers lie within two tiles of it. Nothing happens if the place is unknown, or if neither the map nor the tile actually changes.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The ID of the map to move the place to. Give an empty value to leave it on the map it is already on and only change its tile.

required.name: strings[1]
required.description: The ID of the place to move. Give an empty value to use the place the player is currently at.

optional.name: tileCoords[0]
optional.description: The tile on the destination map to move the place to. If either half is left at -1 the place keeps its current tile, which is also what the default of (-1,-1) does.

uses.description: Moves a settlement to a different tile of the map it already sits on, carrying everything that marks it on the ground along with it. Its buildings, signposts and scenery are torn up from the old spot and rebuilt around the new one at the same relative offsets, and the sight-blocker on its tile moves too. A place whose marker pieces were never recorded first adopts whatever place markers lie within two tiles of it. Nothing happens if the place is unknown or the tile does not actually change.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The ID of the place to move.

optional.name: tileCoords[0]
optional.description: The tile to move the place to. If either half is left at -1 the place keeps its current tile, which is also what the default of (-1,-1) does.

tasks.officialDescription: Sets a location's zoneThisLocationIsIn to 'sValue' if specified. If X/Y aren't -1, sets the location's xy to them. 'sValue2' is the ID of the location. If ID is not set, uses current location instead. If sValue is blank, zoneThisLocationIsIn isn't changed. If X/Y are -1, xy isn't changed. Any locationItems will be moved to the new location with their same offsets.

tasks.name: setLocTravelPoint

uses.description: Changes which arrival point a settlement drops the party at when they enter it, so the same map can be entered by a different door depending on the story. Nothing happens if the place is unknown.

optional.name: strings[0]
optional.description: The ID of the place to change. Leave it out, or give an empty value, to use the place the player is currently at, or to fall through to the second text slot if one is supplied.

optional.name: strings[1]
optional.description: An alternative place to change, used only when the first slot is left empty. It exists so a trigger effect that already needs its first text slot for something else can still name a place.

optional.name: floats[0]
optional.description: Which arrival point of the destination map to use, counting from 0. Fractions are dropped and negative numbers are treated as 0. Defaults to 0.

tasks.officialDescription: Sets a location's enterOnTravelPointNum to fValue. Defaults to 0 if negative. 'sValue' is the ID of the location. If ID is not set, uses current location instead.

tasks.name: breakAllStashItems

uses.description: Breaks every weapon and piece of armour in the player's stash at once, leaving them useless until repaired. Items already broken are left as they are, and anything marked unbreakable survives. Items tucked inside containers in the stash are not reached. Nothing happens if the player has no stash.

tasks.officialDescription: Sets broken = true for every item in the player's stash inventory that can be broken.

tasks.name: repairAllStashItems

uses.description: Repairs everything broken in the player's stash at once, putting weapons and armour back into working order. Items tucked inside containers in the stash are not reached. Nothing happens if the player has no stash.

tasks.officialDescription: Sets broken = false for every item in the player's stash inventory.

tasks.name: addItemToFleetCargo

uses.description: Puts an item into a fleet's cargo hold, which is how a fleet is stocked with goods to be looted or traded. Nothing happens if the item type does not exist, if there is no such fleet, or if that fleet has no hold.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The ID of the item to put into the hold.

required.name: strings[1]
required.description: Which fleet to stock, named by the ID of any ship or commodore in it. The special names "enemyFleet" and "assistFleet" pick out the opposing and allied fleets of the battle in progress.

optional.name: floats[0]
optional.description: How many to put in. Defaults to 1, and 0 is also treated as 1. Fractions are dropped.

tasks.officialDescription: Adds 'fValue' quantity of 'sValue' itemType ID to the cargo of the fleet identified by 'sValue2'. sValue2 can be the ID of the commodore of the fleet, or the ID of a ship within the fleet, or the key word 'enemyFleet' or 'assistFleet' for fleets the player is currently in combat with. If fValue is 0, it acts as 1.

tasks.name: removeItemFromFleetCargo

uses.description: Takes a quantity of one item out of a fleet's cargo hold. Nothing happens if there is no such fleet or it has no hold.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The ID of the item to take out of the hold.

required.name: strings[1]
required.description: Which fleet to take from, named by the ID of any ship or commodore in it. The special names "enemyFleet" and "assistFleet" pick out the opposing and allied fleets of the battle in progress.

optional.name: floats[0]
optional.description: How many to take out. Defaults to 1, and 0 is also treated as 1. Any negative number is treated as -1, which takes out the whole stock of that item.

uses.description: Empties out a fleet's cargo hold, taking a quantity of every item it holds, or clearing it entirely. It is the way to strip a fleet of its goods without naming each one. Nothing happens if there is no such fleet or it has no hold.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: Which fleet to empty, named by the ID of any ship or commodore in it. The special names "enemyFleet" and "assistFleet" pick out the opposing and allied fleets of the battle in progress. Supplying only this one text value is what switches the task from removing a single item to sweeping the hold.

optional.name: floats[0]
optional.description: How many of each item to take out. Defaults to 1, and 0 is also treated as 1. Any negative number empties the hold completely in one go.

tasks.officialDescription: Remove 'fValue' quantity of 'sValue' itemType ID from the cargo of the fleet identified by 'sValue2'. sValue2 can be the ID of the commodore of the fleet, or the ID of a ship within the fleet, or the key word 'enemyFleet' or 'assistFleet' for fleets the player is currently in combat with. If fValue is 0, will remove 1. If fValue is -1 or less, removes all of sValue itemType. If sValue isn't set or is blank, 'fValue' quantity of all items are removed.

tasks.name: setGlobalVar_toFleetCargoItemIDSlot

uses.description: Looks at one slot of a fleet's cargo hold and stores the ID of the item in it into a global variable, which is how a scene can ask what a fleet is carrying. If the slot is empty or beyond the end of the hold the variable is set to empty text; if there is no such fleet the variable is left untouched.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The name of the global variable to write the item's ID into.

required.name: strings[1]
required.description: Which fleet's hold to look in, named by the ID of any ship or commodore in it. The special names "enemyFleet" and "assistFleet" pick out the opposing and allied fleets of the battle in progress.

optional.name: floats[0]
optional.description: Which slot of the hold to look at, counting from 0. Defaults to 0.

tasks.officialDescription: Sets gVar 'sValue' to the itemType ID of the item in slot 'fValue' of the cargo belonging to the fleet identified by 'sValue2'. sValue2 can be the ID of the commodore of the fleet, or the ID of a ship within the fleet, or the key word 'enemyFleet' or 'assistFleet' for fleets the player is currently in combat with.

tasks.name: setGlobalVar_toFleetShipID

uses.description: Stores the ID of one of a fleet's ships into a global variable, picked by its place in the fleet order, so a later task can act on that particular vessel. If there is no such fleet, or no ship in that place, the variable is set to empty text.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The name of the global variable to write the ship's ID into.

required.name: strings[1]
required.description: Which fleet to look at, named by the ID of any ship or commodore in it. The special names "enemyFleet" and "assistFleet" pick out the opposing and allied fleets of the battle in progress.

optional.name: floats[0]
optional.description: Which ship to read, counting from 0 through the fleet in order, where 0 is the flagship. Defaults to 0.

tasks.officialDescription: Sets gVar 'sValue' to the ship actor ID in slot 'fValue' of the fleet identified by 'sValue2'. sValue2 can be the ID of the commodore of the fleet, or the ID of a ship within the fleet, or the key word 'enemyFleet' or 'assistFleet' for fleets the player is currently in combat with.

tasks.name: setGlobalVar_toFleetCommodoreID

uses.description: Stores the ID of a fleet's commodore into a global variable, so a later task or a piece of dialog can address the person in charge. The commodore is the first crew member aboard the fleet's flagship. If there is no such fleet, or it has no commodore, the variable is set to empty text.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The name of the global variable to write the commodore's ID into.

required.name: strings[1]
required.description: Which fleet to look at, named by the ID of any ship or commodore in it. The special names "enemyFleet" and "assistFleet" pick out the opposing and allied fleets of the battle in progress.

tasks.officialDescription: Sets gVar 'sValue' to the ID of the commodore of the fleet identified by 'sValue2'. sValue2 should be the ID of a ship within the fleet, or the key word 'enemyFleet' or 'assistFleet' for fleets the player is currently in combat with. If the fleet doesn't have a commodore, the gVar is set to a blank string.

tasks.name: setGlobalVar_toJournalNote

uses.description: Reads back what the player has typed on one of the journal's note pages and stores it into a global variable, so a mod can react to something the player wrote down. If there is no note page by that number the variable is set to empty text.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The name of the global variable to write the note's text into.

optional.name: floats[0]
optional.description: Which note page to read, counting from 0. Defaults to 0.

tasks.officialDescription: Sets gVar 'sValue' to the 'fValue'-th (starting at 0) journal Notes entry string.

tasks.name: setJournalNote

uses.description: Writes text onto one of the journal's note pages, as though the player had typed it there themselves. It overwrites whatever was on that page. Nothing happens if there is no note page by that number.

optional.name: strings[0]
optional.description: The text to write onto the page. Defaults to empty, which clears the page.

optional.name: floats[0]
optional.description: Which note page to write to, counting from 0. Defaults to 0.

tasks.officialDescription: Sets journal Notes entry 'fValue' (starting at 0) to 'sValue' string.

tasks.name: setGlobalVarTo_mousePointingAt

uses.description: Stores what the mouse pointer is over into a global variable, so an interface built out of the world itself can react to where the player is pointing. By default it reports the item under the pointer, but it can be told to report the character there instead, or the terrain of the tile. On a gamepad the cursor's position is used in place of the mouse. If the pointer is off screen or there is nothing of the asked-for kind under it, the variable is set to empty text.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The name of the global variable to write the answer into.

optional.name: bools[0]
optional.description: Pass true to report the ID of the character under the pointer instead of the item. Defaults to false.

optional.name: bools[1]
optional.description: Pass true to report the terrain of the tile under the pointer instead of the item, ignoring how tall anything on it is. Defaults to false, and it is ignored if the character flag is set.

tasks.officialDescription: Sets gVar 'sValue' to the itemTypeID of the item the player currently has their mouse over in the current zone. If b1, sets it to the Actor ID currently hovering over, if any. If b2, sets it to the terrainTypeID being hovered over. If b1 and b2, b1 takes priority. Sets a blank string if hovering over nothing.

tasks.name: setGlobalVarTo_mouseOverWindow

uses.description: Stores the name of the interface window the mouse is currently over into a global variable, so a mod can react to what part of the interface the player is looking at. When the player is using a gamepad, the window the on-screen cursor is on is reported instead. Hidden windows are ignored, and if the pointer is over none the variable is set to empty text.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The name of the global variable to write the window's name into.

tasks.officialDescription: Sets gVar 'sValue' to the ID of the window the mouse is currently hovering over, or a blank string if hovering over none.

tasks.name: testzones

uses.description: Runs an automated tour of every hand-built map in the game, travelling into each one in turn at a second and a half apart and announcing each with a floating counter showing how far through the tour it is. Randomly generated maps, set pieces, groves, dens and ship interiors are skipped. Control is handed back to ordinary overworld play as the tour begins. It is a soak test for catching maps that fail to load, and it can be told how many maps to visit and how many times to go round.

optional.name: floats[0]
optional.description: How many maps to visit in each pass. Defaults to all of them.

optional.name: floats[1]
optional.description: How many times to run through the tour. Defaults to 1. This slot is beyond what a trigger effect can supply.

tasks.officialDescription: DO NOT USE. Travels to all, or floats[1] number of zones found in the ZoneData folder floats[0] times, with a delay of 1.5 seconds per zone change.

tasks.name: stopCombatAIActing

uses.description: Freezes the enemy side of a battle: if a character the player does not control is taking their turn, that turn is ended at once, and the artificial opposition is barred from acting further. Every character's per-turn working state is also reset. Combat itself continues, so the player can still act; the other side simply stops. It stays frozen until the matching task lets them act again.

tasks.officialDescription: If in combat and it's not a player actor's turn, this ends the current AI actor's turn and resets its calculated action plan.

tasks.name: startCombatAIActing

uses.description: Lets the enemy side of a battle act again after it has been frozen, so uncontrolled characters resume taking their turns. It is the counterpart to freezing them, used to hand the fight back after a scripted interruption.

tasks.officialDescription: DO NOT USE. Technically does nothing.

tasks.name: relocateActors

uses.description: Shoves every character standing near a spot out to the edges of it, which is how the game clears a space in the middle of a crowd — for a cutscene, an arrival, or something dropping out of the sky. Each is moved instantly to the nearest free tile that lies outside the cleared circle but within three tiles beyond it, and anyone with nowhere to go stays put. Party members caught up in it have their queued movement cancelled, and everyone moved can be made to flinch.

optional.name: strings[0]
optional.description: Only move characters of this faction. Leave it out, or give an empty value, to move everyone in range.

optional.name: floats[0]
optional.description: How many tiles around the spot to clear. Defaults to 1.

optional.name: bools[0]
optional.description: Pass true to make each moved character play their flinching animation, as though they had been shoved. Defaults to false.

optional.name: tileCoords[0]
optional.description: The spot to clear around. If omitted it defaults to (-1,-1), just off the map's corner, where it will find nobody.

tasks.officialDescription: Puts all actors within fValue of XY to the nearest occupiable tile within fValue+3. If b1, animate pain. If sValue1 specified, move only actors of that faction.

tasks.name: relocateActors_point

uses.description: Gathers every character standing near a spot and puts them onto the map's arrival points, which is how a scene lines a crowd up in prearranged positions. Each is placed on one of the ten arrival points of a chosen set, in order, facing the way that point faces; if there are more characters than points the leftovers are left where they are. Party members caught up in it have their queued movement cancelled, and nothing happens if the map has no arrival points of that set.

optional.name: strings[0]
optional.description: Only gather characters of this faction. Leave it out, or give an empty value, to gather everyone in range.

optional.name: strings[1]
optional.description: Which set of arrival points to use, from 0 for the main set through to 4, written as text. Because a plain number written in a taskString would be taken as a number rather than a string, it has to be forced into a text slot, and text that does not read as a whole number stops the task with an error. Defaults to 0.

optional.name: floats[0]
optional.description: How many tiles around the spot to gather characters from. Defaults to 1.

optional.name: bools[0]
optional.description: Pass true to use only arrival points that nobody is standing on. Defaults to false.

optional.name: bools[1]
optional.description: Pass true to shuffle the arrival points first, so characters land in a random order rather than the authored one. Defaults to false.

optional.name: tileCoords[0]
optional.description: The spot to gather characters from. If omitted it defaults to (-1,-1), just off the map's corner, where it will find nobody.

tasks.officialDescription: Puts all actors within fValue of XY onto travel point set # sValue2. If sValue1 specified, move only actors of that faction. If b1, only use unoccupied tiles. If b2, randomize tiles.

tasks.name: placeActorFromBoardedShip

uses.description: Brings a crew member off the ship currently being boarded onto the boarded deck, placing them at one of the map's arrival points whether or not anything is already standing there. Every crew member of that kind is brought across, so a ship with three of them puts all three on the same spot. It requires a boarding to be under way with a target ship set, and fails outright if the text value is missing.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The kind of crew member to bring across. Every crew member of that kind aboard the boarded ship is placed.

optional.name: tileCoords[0]
optional.description: Which arrival point to place them on, given as the point number across and the set number down rather than as a real tile. If omitted it defaults to (-1,-1), which names no valid arrival point.

tasks.officialDescription: Places actors from currently boarded ship of actorType string0 at travelpoint specified by XY (point# X, set# Y)

tasks.name: setupLocationAsPlayerPort

uses.description: Turns the place the player is currently at into their home port in one stroke: it becomes a port serving basic food, gains a home marker on its sign, opens a shipwright selling cogs, caravels and pinnaces, starts hiring humans and scurio, and has its quests reset. Its shop is stocked with an endless supply of life shards, revive dust, splints and shovels, five experience gems and three random ability tablets, with ability crests held back until the port grows wealthy. Its own map symbol is cleared, and if the player belongs to a faction the port is locked to that faction so it can never change hands. It requires the player to be at a place, and fails outright otherwise.

tasks.officialDescription: Sets the current location as a player-owned port. This also adds ships, items, and spawnData to the location's lists.

tasks.name: addIconToCurrentLocation

uses.description: Adds an icon to a settlement's map marker, the little symbols showing at a glance what services the place offers. By default an icon the place already shows is not added a second time, though that can be overridden to stack duplicates. Nothing happens if the place is unknown.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The name of the icon image to add to the place's marker.

optional.name: strings[1]
optional.description: The ID of the place to change. Leave it out, or give an empty value, to use the place the player is currently at; a name that matches no place also falls back to the current one.

optional.name: bools[0]
optional.description: Pass true to add the icon even if the place already shows it, giving it twice over. Defaults to false.

tasks.officialDescription: Alias of addIconToLocationID. Use it instead (this is functionally identical, however).

tasks.name: setPartyActorAsVendor

uses.description: Takes a party member out of the party and stations them at one of the home port's arrival points as a shopkeeper, giving them a conversation of their own and reserving their name so nothing else claims it. If someone was already standing at that point doing the same job, they are relieved: their conversation is cleared, they rejoin the party and fleet, and they are moved aside to make room. Where the person being replaced was the port's quest giver, the newcomer takes that role over.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The conversation the stationed character should use, which is what makes them a shopkeeper of a particular sort. Someone already at the post using this same conversation is the one relieved.

required.name: floats[0]
required.description: Which party member to station, counting from 0 for whoever is leading. Nothing happens if the party has nobody in that place.

required.name: floats[1]
required.description: Which of the map's arrival points to station them at, counting from 0. This slot is beyond what a trigger effect can supply.

tasks.officialDescription: Must be used as a taskString. Removes the party actor in slot floats[0] and places them on travelPoint floats[1], then switches their dialogNodeID to strings[0].

tasks.name: readdVendorToParty

uses.description: Brings a stationed shopkeeper back into the party. The character standing at a chosen arrival point is checked, and if they are running the named conversation their post is cleared, they rejoin the party, the landing party and the fleet, and they are moved to the nearest tile they can reach beside the player. Nothing happens if nobody is at that point or they are doing a different job.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The conversation the stationed character must be running for them to be taken back; it identifies which post is being closed.

required.name: floats[0]
required.description: Which of the map's arrival points to look at, counting from 0.

tasks.officialDescription: Adds the actor on travelPoint 'fValue' to the player's party if their dialogNodeID equals 'sValue'.

tasks.name: askForNewPortName

uses.description: Returns control to ordinary overworld play and opens a prompt asking the player to type a name for the port. The prompt cannot be dismissed by the player and clears itself when the next turn begins; whatever they type is passed on to be applied as the port's new name.

tasks.officialDescription: Brings up a text entry box for the player to rename the current location.

tasks.name: setupCafeFoodDialogOptionsWealth100

uses.description: Rebuilds a dialog node into a menu of the dishes the player's own port could serve. The basic dish always appears first, followed by the speciality of every wealthy port in the world outside the player's own, each shown as its picture with a tooltip giving its name, price, description and effects. The dish currently being served is shown but leads nowhere, so it cannot be chosen again, and a "Nevermind" option closes the menu. The changes are written into the node itself, so it should be a scratch node kept for this purpose.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The ID of the dialog node to rebuild as the dish menu. Its existing options are cleared.

tasks.officialDescription: Sets up the dialogOptions for dialogNode 'sValue' used to set the current supply port's cafe food.

tasks.name: changeCafeFood

uses.description: Changes the dish a settlement's eating house serves. Naming a dish sets it directly; naming another place instead copies that place's dish over and its hiring lists with it, replacing whoever the settlement was recruiting. Nothing happens if the place being changed is unknown.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The ID of the dish to serve. If this happens to be the ID of a place on the world map, that place's dish and hiring lists are copied over instead.

optional.name: strings[1]
optional.description: The ID of the place to change. Leave it out, or give an empty value, to use the place the player is currently at; a name that matches no place also falls back to the current one.

tasks.officialDescription: Changes a location's cafeFood_itemTypeID to 'sValue'. If sValue is the ID of another location, it will use the cafeFood_itemTypeID of that location instead and also change the location's auto_spawnDataID to match it. 'sValue2' is the ID of the location to change. If ID is not set, uses current location instead.

tasks.name: giveMathXPToActorWithDialogNodeID

uses.description: Awards experience to every character in the map running a particular conversation, which is how stationed shopkeepers and companions are kept level with the player without being in the party. The amount comes from a formula, but is capped so it can never take them past the total experience the player has earned, and never goes below zero. No floating numbers are shown, party size does not reduce it, and tiredness does not block it.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The conversation identifying which characters to award. Everyone in the map running it is awarded.

required.name: strings[1]
required.description: A formula giving how much experience to award each of them. It is evaluated without any actor attached, so it can only use values that do not depend on a particular character.

tasks.officialDescription: Gives formula 'sValue2' amount of XP to every actor in the current zone with 'sValue' dialogNodeID. Won't exceed player's total XP.

tasks.name: convertPlayerPortsToFaction

uses.description: Hands every port the player has founded over to a faction, locking each one to it so ownership can never be contested again. It is how a player's holdings are folded into an empire at the end of a storyline.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The ID of the faction to hand the player's ports to.

tasks.officialDescription: Sets all ports with a 'sport' tag (usually player established) to be ever-loyal to faction ID 'sValue'.

tasks.name: addLocationUnlockable

uses.description: Adds something to the list of goods held back at the place the player is currently at, to appear on sale once a condition is met, then checks the condition straight away so anything already qualifying goes on sale at once and quietly. It requires the player to be at a place, and fails outright otherwise or if any of its values are missing.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The ID of the item to hold back. The ID of a kind of ship may be given instead, which will be offered by the shipwright when the condition is met.

required.name: strings[1]
required.description: The condition that must come out at 1 or more for the item to go on sale, evaluated against the player. Typically a check on the port's wealth.

required.name: floats[0]
required.description: How many go on sale when the condition is met. A value of -2 clears out any existing stock of that item first, replacing rather than adding to it.

tasks.officialDescription: Adds an unlockable to the current Location of ID sValue, quantity fValue, and fReq sValue2. Use addUnlockableItemToLocationID to add an unlockable to a specific location instead.

tasks.name: task

uses.description: Runs another task written out in full as a single value, with the same trigger area handed on to it. It exists so a task can be built up as text — by joining pieces together or pulling them out of a global variable — and then run. Because a comma-separated task cannot hold a comma inside one of its values, this is only useful from a trigger effect, where the value can carry the commas the nested task needs.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The whole task to run, written as one comma-separated value.

tasks.officialDescription: execute a task set as a comma-separated string in 'sValue'

tasks.name: task_gvar

uses.description: Runs a task that has been stored in a global variable, with the same trigger area handed on to it. It is how a mod remembers a piece of work to do later and then does it, letting one scene decide what a later one will run. Nothing happens if the variable is unset or holds 0.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The name of the global variable holding the task to run, written as one comma-separated value.

tasks.officialDescription: execute a comma-separated task as defined by global variable 'sValue'

tasks.name: dominateworld

uses.description: Makes every port in the world rich and, if the player belongs to a faction, hands them all to that faction and locks them there so ownership can never be contested again. It is a debugging shortcut for reaching an end state, and it cannot be undone.

tasks.officialDescription: Sets wealth to 100 for all overworld ports and converts them to the player's current faction.

tasks.name: gc

uses.description: Frees up memory: every map the game was keeping loaded in the background is discarded, and the memory cleanup is run twice over to catch anything that comes free on the first pass. The game may stutter briefly while this happens, and maps that were held ready will have to be loaded from disk again next time they are needed.

tasks.officialDescription: DO NOT USE. Forces program garbage collection.

tasks.name: clear

uses.description: Wipes away everything the developer tools have put on screen: the pictures pinned up over the world, the effects drawn ignoring darkness, and all the on-screen debug messages. It leaves the game itself untouched.

tasks.officialDescription: Clears all text from the console window.

tasks.name: debug_drawStrings

uses.description: Prints a message on screen as a debug message under a label of your choosing, staying up for about ten seconds. Printing again under the same label replaces the previous message rather than adding a second one. Nothing is printed if the label is empty or no message is supplied.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The label the message is filed under. Reusing a label replaces whatever was shown under it before. An empty label prints nothing.

required.name: strings[1]
required.description: The text to show.

tasks.officialDescription: Displays a debug message using 'sValue' as the type and 'sValue2' as the message.

tasks.name: loadItOnUpYo

uses.description: Moves the party to another map immediately, without going through the world map, placing them on a chosen tile facing a chosen direction. Everyone stops moving, drops out of any animation and becomes solid again as they arrive, and the overlaid layer is cleared away. The change can be faded or instant depending on the speed given.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The ID of the map to move to.

required.name: floats[0]
required.description: Which way the party should face on arrival, in degrees. Pass -1 to leave their facing alone.

required.name: floats[1]
required.description: How fast the screen fades across the change. A negative value keeps the overlaid layer loaded through the move. This slot is beyond what a trigger effect can supply.

optional.name: tileCoords[0]
optional.description: The tile on the new map to place the party on. If omitted it defaults to (-1,-1), which is off the map.

tasks.officialDescription: DO NOT USE. Moves the player to zone strings[0] at position tileCoords[0], facing floats[0] with floats[1] as the fadeSpeed.

tasks.name: maximizeWindowSet

uses.description: Maximises or unmaximises the game window. Calling it bare unmaximises, restoring the window to its previous size.

optional.name: bools[0]
optional.description: True to maximise the window, false to restore it. Defaults to false.

tasks.officialDescription: DO NOT USE. Maximizes the game window if bValue1 is true.

tasks.name: maximizeWindowIfTrue

uses.description: Maximises the game window and stops the main menu backdrop and the whole interface layer from being drawn, leaving a bare view. It only does anything when told true; told false, or told nothing, it does nothing at all. It is meant for setting up a clean full-window view before something is captured or displayed.

optional.name: bools[0]
optional.description: Pass true to maximise the window and hide the interface. Defaults to false, which does nothing.

tasks.officialDescription: DO NOT USE. Maximizes the game window if bValue1 is true.

tasks.name: changeScreenResolution2

uses.description: Reapplies the display settings the game currently wants: any pending window size change is dropped, full screen is switched on if it should be, and a window that is not full screen has its border restored. It is the second half of a resolution change, used to settle the window after the first half has been applied.

tasks.officialDescription: DO NOT USE.

tasks.name: uploadmod

uses.description: Publishes a mod folder to the game's online workshop as a brand new entry. The folder is checked first: it must exist, hold at least one file, and contain a 512 by 512 image named after the folder to serve as its thumbnail, and a message explains which of these is missing if the check fails. While the upload runs a progress message is shown and the player is prevented from acting. Leaving the folder name out prints an error and does nothing.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The name of the mod folder to upload, as it appears in the game's mod directory.

tasks.officialDescription: DO NOT USE. Uploads a new mod using the mod folder 'sValue'.

tasks.name: getmod

uses.description: Remembers a workshop entry's number so that a following upload edits that existing entry rather than creating a new one. A value that does not read as a whole number clears the remembered entry instead, and leaving it out prints an error and changes nothing.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The workshop entry's number, written as text. Because a plain number written in a taskString would be taken as a number rather than a string, it has to be forced into a text slot; anything that does not read as a whole number clears the remembered entry.

tasks.officialDescription: DO NOT USE. Sets mod ID 'sValue' as the mod currently being edited, for use with other mod tasks.

tasks.name: editmod

uses.description: Uploads a mod folder over an existing workshop entry, replacing both its contents and its thumbnail image; the entry updated is whichever one was last remembered. The folder is checked first: it must exist, hold at least one file, and contain a 512 by 512 image named after the folder, and a message explains which of these is missing if the check fails. While the upload runs a progress message is shown and the player is prevented from acting. Leaving the folder name out prints an error and does nothing.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The name of the mod folder to upload, as it appears in the game's mod directory. Its thumbnail image must be named after the folder.

tasks.officialDescription: DO NOT USE. Uploads mod changes for the mod currently being edited, using mod folder 'sValue'.

tasks.name: editmodtags

uses.description: Replaces the tags on the last workshop entry that was uploaded or looked up, without touching its files. Every value given becomes one tag, with leading spaces trimmed off each. A progress message is shown and the player is prevented from acting while it uploads, and on success a message offers to open the entry's page. Leaving out the values prints an error and does nothing.

required.name: strings[0+]
required.description: Any number of tags to set on the entry, one per text value; several may also be packed into one value separated by commas. Leading spaces are trimmed from each. These replace the entry's existing tags entirely.

tasks.officialDescription: DO NOT USE. Changes the tags for the mod currently being edited to each strings[] set.

tasks.name: loadModPageInBrowser

uses.description: Opens the workshop page of the last mod that was uploaded or looked up in the machine's web browser, leaving the game running behind it. It is the follow-up offered after a successful upload so the author can finish filling in the entry's description and visibility.

tasks.officialDescription: DO NOT USE. Opens the modding reference guide URL (located on Steam) in the player's default browser.

tasks.name: test

uses.description: A leftover developer scratch command with no meaningful effect on the game: it prints a short piece of test text on screen as a debug message and queues a do-nothing task a second later. There is no reason for a mod to use it.

tasks.officialDescription: DO NOT USE.

tasks.name: UIPartInputCommand

uses.description: Sends a command straight to the game's interface, as though a button had been pressed, complete with the name, number, text and second number a button would pass along. It reaches parts of the interface that have no task of their own, so it is the way a mod drives menus and windows directly. What the command does depends entirely on which one is named; an unrecognised name does nothing.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The interface command to send, spelled exactly as the game names it.

required.name: strings[1]
required.description: The name passed along with the command, which most commands use to say what they are acting on.

required.name: strings[2]
required.description: The text value passed along with the command.

required.name: floats[0]
required.description: The number passed along with the command, which many use as an index or an identifier.

required.name: floats[1]
required.description: A second number passed along with the command. This slot is beyond what a trigger effect can supply.

uses.description: Sends a command straight to the game's interface with no arguments, as though a button with nothing attached had been pressed. It reaches parts of the interface that have no task of their own. What the command does depends entirely on which one is named; an unrecognised name does nothing.

required.name: strings[0]
required.description: The interface command to send, spelled exactly as the game names it.

tasks.officialDescription: Calls handleUIPartInput_command(string0, string1, float0, string2, float1)

tasks.name: noSpeechFXLookOrAnim

uses.description: Does nothing when run. It is a reserved name that produces no observable effect in the game, and any values given to it are ignored. One of these names, noSpeechFXLookOrAnim, is nonetheless meaningful as a dialog node's marker rather than as a task: a node carrying it suppresses the speaker's talking sound, their turn towards the listener and their gesture on the opening line.

tasks.officialDescription: Must be used as a dialog specialEffect. The current dialogNode won't show its text reveal FX or play any set animations. The currentActorTalkingTo also won't look at the player.
